items.statement: Expect progressively stronger performance in coming period driven by tightening global supply, long-term gas arrangement, and stronger business mix
items.quote: So overall, with these levers coming into play, we are confident of progressively stronger performance in the coming period.

items.statement: FY27 capex of INR 800-1,000 crores including maintenance to complete Gopalpur and Dahej projects
items.quote: So there is almost INR 800 crores to INR1,000 crores capex spending, including maintenance.

items.statement: Chemical margins to improve from Equinor LNG contract benefit flowing through ammonia business
items.quote: However, the way we look in the business, each business has been seen separately based on IPP transfer pricing, not based on cost plus. So each business on its own will show the profitability and Equinor gas contract benefit will finally flow into our ammonia business, which is PCL.

items.statement: Ammonia business margins significantly better than before due to elevated ammonia prices and gas cost advantage
items.quote: But yes, our margin in ammonia business will be significantly better than what we used to discuss or what we used to talk about.

items.statement: TAN demand strengthening in Q4 due to mining targets, seasonal softness expected in Q2 but no long-term demand destruction
items.quote: This trend is likely to continue. Although we are getting into a soft season, as you know, we are getting into monsoon. So Q2 is cyclically and seasonally weaker in terms of demand, but we don't see any long-term demand destruction for any reason.

items.statement: Specialty and Croptek now 33% of Crop Nutrition revenue, up from 30% previous year
items.quote: Specialty and Croptek now contributes around 33% of segment revenue, up from 30% previous year, which is a very important structural level lever for improving margins over time.

items.statement: B2C segment in Mining Chemicals now 16% of revenue, up from 13% last year
items.quote: The B2C segment continued to scale well, now contributes around 16% of the revenue compared to 13% last year.

items.statement: Gopalpur TAN facility expected to reach 90-95% utilization by end of FY27 on TPD basis
items.quote: We expect by end of this year, we should be at least touching 90% to 95% utilization on a TPD basis.

items.statement: Ammonia supply for Gopalpur secured through own production, trading expertise, and continuous supplier contracts
items.quote: We have a contract in place or we know from where the source is in place. Since we have -- we are already in importing and selling ammonia for us, some more additional quantity need to buy and supply into that plant. So that's not a challenge for us.

items.statement: IPA prices elevated due to LPG shortage and RGP constraints, expected to remain high until situation normalizes
items.quote: So will the price will remain elevated for some time? Yes, price will remain elevated for some time before the situation becomes normal and then we'll have to see what will be the normal IPA prices once things go back.

items.statement: CCD of INR 800 crores issued in Q1 FY26: INR 500 crores third party, INR 300 crores promoter entity, conversion in ~30 months
items.quote: The CCD was issued last year in quarter 1 actually. And that CCD was issued as a mix of third party as well as a promoter entity participated in that. The split was INR 500 crores was issued and subscribed by third party and INR300 crores by promoter entity.

items.statement: First Equinor LNG cargo received in May 2025, multiple parcels lined up for the year, fully secured gas supply
items.quote: Another key milestone during the period has been commencement of supply under our long-term LNG contract with Equinor with the first shipment already received in May. This strengthens our ammonia value chain by improving supply security, cost visibility and integration advantage.

items.statement: Q4 ammonia plant shutdown had one-off impact of INR 70-75 crores, plant now performing well with capacity and efficiency improvements
items.quote: Also, while Q4 saw a long -ish planned shutdown for our ammonia plant to also bring in some efficiencies and capacity improvements, and that brought in an impact of around INR 70 crores in Q4.

items.statement: Chardham Chemicals acquisition for ~INR 120 crores for land, licenses, equipment, location, and speed to market; no revenue currently, revamp planned
items.quote: But what it is made up of is it's the value of the land. It is the value of the licenses. It is the value of some plants and equipment. It is the value of the location of the facility, which is the proximity to the market. And last but not the least, it's the get-to-market speed through this acquisition compared to if we were to put up a greenfield site.

items.statement: Expects INR850-900 crores inflow from Dubai project over next six months, entirely for deleveraging.
items.quote: And we expect that about INR850 crores to INR900 crores should flow into us over the next six months.

items.statement: After Dubai and associate inflows, external borrowings expected at INR700-800 crores by year-end.
items.quote: So we expect that our external borrowings will be in the range of around INR700 crores and INR800 crores which we are able to manage from our operations.

items.statement: Estimated profit from Dubai project post completion around INR600 crores; capital invested INR270-275 crores.
items.quote: So, since we are a 50% JV partner, our share of the profit, the estimated profit post completion should be around about INR600 odd crores.

items.statement: Real estate development management EBITDA margins typically 70-75%.
items.quote: Typically our -- being a service revenue, typically our EBITDA margins are in the range of about 70% to 75%.

items.statement: Hyderabad and Kolkata real estate projects to complete in about five years; Bangalore plotted development in 18 months.
items.quote: the Hyderabad, Kolkata ones will take about five years f or completion, and this revenue of the top line will be recognized over a period of 5 years, based on the sales velocity.

items.statement: No major ethanol expansion plans; capitalizing existing plant with syrup and B-heavy diversion.
items.quote: Right now, we are not having any major expansion plans. Since Zuari has already having a joint venture in Envien.

items.statement: Ethanol sector has ~100% overcapacity; OMC tenders not coming; expects improvement with higher blending.
items.quote: And we understand that now that capacity stands increased to about 2,000 crores liters. So it's almost like a 100% over capacity currently in ethanol.

items.statement: Sugar prices expected stable near-term; closing stocks ~5.6 million tons, about two months consumption.
items.quote: Sugar prices are expected to remain stable in the near-term as closing stocks are estimated at about 5.6 million ton, which was 5.3 million ton last year, which is equivalent to about two months of consumption.

items.statement: Stagnant ethanol prices pressure profitability; expects long-overdue revision in ethanol prices.
items.quote: While stagnant ethanol prices have continued to put some pressure on profitability, we remain quite optimistic as I said earlier about the sector outlook.

items.statement: Macroeconomic situation affecting capex plans in India and Middle East; increased input prices for sugar business.
items.quote: Looking ahead, I think the macroeconomic situation, of course, is a concern to all of us. It is affecting capex plans both in India and the Middle East.

items.statement: Goa land bank 260 acres, book value INR163 crores; no monetization factored in future plans.
items.quote: So currently Zuari Industries is holding around 260 acres of land parcel and the value in the books of account is around INR163 crores.

items.statement: Sugar division achieved highest ever capacity utilization of 101.7% and record crushing.
items.quote: The best part was that we achieved the highest ever capacity utilization of 101.7%.

items.statement: Ethanol distillery ran 316 days, highest ever, with production of 372 lakh liters.
items.quote: 316 days, which probably was the highest ever performance.

items.statement: Targets 20-25% top-line growth, revenue INR750-800 crores, and 20%+ EBITDA margins for FY27.
items.quote: We have set a growth target of 20% to 25% on top line over last year, which would result in a revenue of around INR750 crores to INR800 crores. We hope to continue EBITDA margins of 20% plus.

items.statement: Targets order intake of INR800-1,000 crores for FY27, with INR450-500 crores expected by Q2.
items.quote: And as I mentioned, we are targeting an order intake of around INR800 crores to INR1,000 crores in the current financial year.

items.statement: Capex of ~INR40 crores for FY27; Saravali and M.E. Energy Phase 2 expansions to complete by Q2.
items.quote: It remains the same what we've been guiding for in the last 2, 3 calls, which is around 40 crores odd.

items.statement: Aims to maintain EBITDA margins of 22-23%, including other income, with 20%+ as buffer.
items.quote: We have also mentioned we are looking at maintaining margins of 22%, 23% in all our commentary.

items.statement: Strong inquiry pipeline of INR4,000+ crores across sectors like fertilizer, nuclear, petrochemicals.
items.quote: We continue to have a strong inquiry pipeline of INR4,000 crores plus at a consol level across various sectors.

items.statement: Exports expected to contribute 30-40% of revenue in future.
items.quote: We believe exports will play a critical role going into the future. And we think 30% to 40% of our revenue can come from exports.

items.statement: No cost pass-through; mitigates risk by booking materials immediately upon order receipt.
items.quote: Our costs are not passed through, okay? We mitigate all the risk by placing orders on time.

items.statement: Monga Strayfield faced dispatch delays due to Middle East logistics, expected to normalize by H1 FY27.
items.quote: That impacted our revenue a bit in Q4 for the subsidiary, which hopefully will also get mitigated by second quarter of this year.

items.statement: No further dilution expected; all warrant conversions completed and funds being utilized for growth.
items.quote: All warrant conversions have happened. So there's no further dilution expected.

items.statement: Working capital days to reduce as large receivables, including INR50-60 crores from Moroccan order, are collected.
items.quote: The end of the year included some large orders like the Moroccan order, which nearly INR50 crores to INR60 crores is receivable in the next 2 to 3 months.

items.statement: Nuclear orders execution to take over a year; 2-3 projects in pipeline.
items.quote: I expect then that it would take another year plus for the complete execution.

items.statement: M.E. Energy expects more orders from ferrous alloy and steel sectors in first 8-9 months of FY27.
items.quote: For the early part of this financial year, maybe first 8, 9 months, we'll have more larger value orders from ferrous alloys industries or steel industry rather than cement industry

items.statement: Granules India order remains on hold with no change in status.
items.quote: It is still at the same level, status quo.

items.statement: Expects 16% EBITDA margin for entire business excluding Omeras within 2 years.
items.quote: Yes, that would be correct. That would be correct. Again, 16% EBITDA margins, I would expect from the entire business with the exception of Omeras because Omeras is right now in the turnaround mode.

items.statement: Consolidated revenue to exceed INR2,000 crores in 2 years including Omeras.
items.quote: I think if we do less than INR2,000 crores, we will be disappointed. I think -- but this would -- but I would only -- the only difference would be I would include Omeras in the INR2,000 crores number.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin expected 14-15% next year.
items.quote: Will be in the range of between 14% and 15% on a consol basis.

items.statement: Heat transfer business to grow 15-20% for next 2 years.
items.quote: So, I think we expect the heat transfer business overall to grow at a 15% to 20% range for the next couple of years.

items.statement: Consolidated order book at INR681.6 crores as of March 31, 2026.
items.quote: Our consolidated order book stood at approximately INR681.6 crores as of March 31, 2026, providing healthy visibility for FY27 and reinforcing confidence in our future growth trajectory.

items.statement: Omeras order book around INR78 crores, doubled from Dec 2025 to Mar 2026.
items.quote: Also, the current order book at Omeras is around INR78 crores, which provides an encouraging visibility for FY27 and creates a stable base for profitable plant operations in the coming months.

items.statement: Omeras expected to achieve double-digit margins next financial year.
items.quote: In terms of getting to double-digit margins, I would expect that to happen in the next financial year for Omeras on a stand-alone basis.

items.statement: Omeras EBITDA breakeven at annual revenue of INR200-225 crores.
items.quote: So, that's our rough breakeven calculation. Of course, it depends on margins and some dynamics of the business. But probably that's the kind of number that we are looking at, which effectively means that at roughly about INR200 crores, INR225 crores kind of an annual revenue, Omeras will be at EBITDA breakeven.

items.statement: Gas price increases largely passed on to customers.
items.quote: Yes. So, the gas prices have definitely increased. We, as with so many other things that have changed because of the recent conflict in Iran. Now so far, we have been able to pass on the price increases to a large extent, but so there has been the impact.

items.statement: Pharma API sector driving growth; specialty chemicals gradual recovery; agrochemicals subdued.
items.quote: So, most of the capex currently in India is happening in the pharma sector, API, I should say. There is also demand in the custom manufacturing sector. I think as I explained, the specialty and the agro are in some form not keeping up with the pace of the others.

items.statement: Thaletec products contributed ~20% of India glass lined products this year.
items.quote: And this year, Thaletec products have contributed close to about 20% of the overall Glass Lined India products.

items.statement: India capex for Omeras tanks to be commercially operational by end of FY27.
items.quote: Yes. We expect to be commercially operational by the end of this financial year. So, this will -- the capex in India will probably reflect in next year's financials from a revenue perspective.

items.statement: Geopolitical situation causing some companies to defer decisions, especially CDMO and agrochemical.
items.quote: I mean everything was going well until about February. What we are seeing is some companies are deferring some decisions because of the ongoing geopolitical situation. So, while the -- I mean pharma -- the pharmaceutical and the API sectors are not yet doing that, but especially the CDMO or the agrochemical companies,

items.statement: Board recommended dividend of 55% for FY26.
items.quote: Further, the Board has recommended a dividend of 55% for FY26, reflecting our confidence in the long-term fundamentals and cash flow generation capabilities of the business.

items.statement: Expects double-digit year-on-year revenue growth, though not as high as Q4's 35% jump.
items.quote: But yes, on year-on-year growth, we will have a double-digit growth as we have explained in our previous call as well.

items.statement: Expects 25-30% ADR growth from organic and refurbishment benefits.
items.quote: So, in combination of all three, as and when the new inventory comes in, I think we can expect anywhere between 25% to 30% growth in ADR.

items.statement: Plans to invest over INR 100 crores in phased renovations across properties.
items.quote: We outlined a plan to invest 100 plus crores to renovate and upgrade existing properties in three phases.

items.statement: Second phase of renovation at Marriott Hyderabad to complete in FY27; third phase in FY28.
items.quote: Building on this progress, the second phase of renovation at Marriott Hyderabad commenced in the first week of April and is expected to be completed during FY '27, while the third phase is targeted for completion during FY '28.

items.statement: Convention center renovation to finish by end of FY27, with investment recouped in 1.5 years.
items.quote: We look to finish this renovation by the end of this year. And we look to recoup the investment made into this in a period of one and a half year.

items.statement: Expects twofold increase in EBITDA from new convention center and Marriott renovation.
items.quote: We are going to see a substantial twofold increase in the EBITDAs because of this addition.

items.statement: F&B margin is 45-50%, with gross margin close to 85%.
items.quote: The margin in F&B is about 45% to 50%. And the gross margin is close to 85%.

items.statement: Expects demand to recover in next couple of months and ADR to return to earlier levels by year-end.
items.quote: But ideally, we'd like to believe that for the next couple of months, we will see some of the demand start coming back. And once the wedding season and a lot of other domestic corporate events start coming back towards the end of the year, I feel that the ADR will go back to the earlier numbers.

items.statement: No new supply expected in next couple of years, supporting ADR stability.
items.quote: And we don't foresee any new supply coming into the next couple of years as well. So, that way, we are not very concerned by what's happening.

items.statement: Room revenue contributes 55-60% and F&B 35-40% for Marriott and Courtyard; for executive apartments, rooms 64-65% and F&B 32-33%.
items.quote: What I can tell you is, in general, for our Marriott and Courtyard complex, our room revenue contribution is about 55% to 60%, whereas F&B contributes about 35% to 40%. Whilst in the executive apartments, room revenues contribution is about 64% to 65%, and F&B is about 32% to 33%.

items.statement: Sees no impact on ADRs from upcoming supply, as less than half of announced projects may open.
items.quote: So, we see that in no way affecting our ADRs, and our ADRs are still going to be strongly improving because the supply will be less. And second thing, in hotel projects, the planning and the execution and the capital allocation and the time management is very crucial, and the debt management. So, we see, even though a

items.statement: Comfortable with current debt levels and does not anticipate further increases in interest expense.
items.quote: We don't see any further increase. We have healthy cash revenues and healthy cash balances to fund our ongoing renovations.

items.statement: Expects to start paying dividends from next year after completing convention center renovation.
items.quote: So, mostly the board also discussed this issue several times, and we expect to give you a good outcome from next year.

items.statement: Targeting 10-15% sales growth for FY27 base business
items.quote: So we hope we can continue between 10% to 15% again this year. That's our target.

items.statement: Targeting around 12% EBITDA margin for base business in FY27
items.quote: Yes, Sagar, we are targeting something around that. We are targeting a good sales growth as well, but we have to see how the market reacts.

items.statement: Fill-finish facility capex estimated at INR50 crores including equipment and filing
items.quote: So the total capex we are estimating is around INR50 crores, which includes equipment and capability but one size. So and filing dossier, so all of that is included.

items.statement: FY26 revenue mix 30% regulated markets, 70% ROW
items.quote: For this year, whole year, 30% is regulated and 70% is ROW. That's what the end of year number, Loveleen.

items.statement: Exblifep commercial discussions active in US, Russia, Latin America, Southeast Asia with term-sheets and definitive agreements under discussion
items.quote: Currently, we are actively discussing opportunities in the United States, Russia, Latin America and Southeast Asia. In some of these markets term-sheets, all definitive agreements are under discussion.

items.statement: Expect at least 50% of Enmetazobactam out-licensing deals signed within six months
items.quote: I would love to do that. But if you have to assume something, I would say 50% will be signed in for sure.

items.statement: Enmetazobactam lifetime sales maintained at $1-2 billion, peak in year 4-5 post-launch
items.quote: We still maintain the lifetime sales would be between $1 billion to $2 billion overall during the life of the patent. And the peak should be reaching fourth or fifth year of the launch, not three years.

items.statement: 7ACA project on track for commissioning in Q1 CY2027
items.quote: We are still committed to the commissioning in the first quarter of calendar year 2027.

items.statement: Cefiderocol facility commissioning by end CY2026, product launch expected Q2-Q3 CY2027
items.quote: The Cefiderocol facility remains on track for commissioning by the end of this calendar year. Subject to regulatory approvals and registrations, we expect product launch during Q2 or Q3 of calendar year 2027.

items.statement: Merger with Dhanuka Labs expected to contribute 1-2% EBITDA margin expansion
items.quote: As these synergies begin getting realized over time, we internally estimate that the merger itself can potentially contribute nearly 1% to 2% EBITDA margin expansion.

items.statement: Base business growth driven by non-regulated markets, particularly Africa and South Asia
items.quote: We believe that the growth, as we have been maintaining, the growth is mainly coming from the non-regulated markets, as more and more population get access to the antibiotics. And the next growth is probably going to come from Africa and probably South of Asia.

items.statement: Pricing recovery uncertain due to war, supply chain costs, competitive intensity, geopolitics
items.quote: Going forward, we still need to monitor the impact of pricing due to the war, supply chain costs, global competitive intensity and geopolitical situations.

items.statement: Plan to launch 5-6 large sterile products covering ~2/3 of US Cephalosporin market ($1.2B opportunity) over next 5 years
items.quote: Over the next few years, Orchid plans to launch approximately five to six large sterile products catering to nearly two-thirds of the U.S. Cephalosporin market opportunity. This overall opportunity size is estimated at approximately $1.2 billion.

items.statement: Downstream capacity for 7ACA utilization to be added via reengineering existing plants, exact investment TBD
items.quote: At this point of time, we are trying to reengineer the existing plants only. We'll probably have the exact number, say, after a few months' time.

items.statement: Dhanuka Labs FY26 revenue INR450 crores (down ~10% YoY), EBITDA under audit
items.quote: Yes. The revenue numbers are INR450 crores, which was INR500 crores last year, so almost same 10% reduction. EBITDA numbers, I don't have at this point of time.

items.statement: Cyient Semiconductors signed a definitive agreement for INR 300 crore funding from EAAA Alternatives at INR 4,650 crore equity valuation.
items.quote: And today, I'm proud to announce that Cyient Semiconductors has signed a definitive agreement for its first external funding route, a total of INR300 crore s with equity valuation at INR4,650 crores from EAAA Alternatives who were formerly known as Edelweiss Alternatives

items.statement: Parent Cyient committed up to $100 million investment in Cyient Semiconductors, with ~$30 million already deployed.
items.quote: Cyient is also committed to our original investment thesis of up to $100 million based on capital needs and context of our group companies.

items.statement: Raised capital will be deployed into R&D, lab infrastructure, and working capital for growth roadmap execution.
items.quote: The capital that we are raising will directly go into R&D, lab infrastructure and working capital to execute on our growth road map.

items.statement: ASIC and ASSP pipeline includes approximately $100 million of qualified opportunities.
items.quote: And finally, commercially, our ASIC pipeline includes approximately $100 million of qualified opportunities, and we were selected as the L1 bidder on the SCL semiconductor modernization initiative.

items.statement: Selected as L1 bidder for SCL semiconductor modernization initiative, a flagship government program.
items.quote: And finally, commercially, our ASIC pipeline includes approximately $100 million of qualified opportunities, and we were selected as the L1 bidder on the SCL semiconductor modernization initiative, one of India's flagship semiconductor programs supported by the government of India.

items.statement: Power ASSP including Kinetic is 50-60% of business; ASSP share expected to increase over next 3-4 years as products commercialize.
items.quote: So today, Power ASSP s including Kinetic is roughly 50% to 60% of our business. The rest of the business is split between services and ASIC turnkey. As we progress and we develop our own products which we are working on, we do believe that ASSP revenue share will increase in the next 3-4 years

items.statement: ASSP gross margins typically 50-60%, higher than custom ASIC turnkey and services segments.
items.quote: From a gross margin standpoint, ASSP given it is product and IP driven will have the highest gross margin typically in the 50% to 60% range, depending on which customer segment you sell, followed by custom ASIC turnkey followed by services.

items.statement: Targeting breakeven late FY27 or early FY28, but may shift a quarter or two to pursue growth opportunities.
items.quote: For now, we are still looking at a breakeven late FY27, early FY28. But based on the investor conversations, we'll come back.

items.statement: Addressable market opportunity for power semiconductors approximately $8.5 billion with low- and high-voltage product strategies.
items.quote: With our acquisition and internal investment in low- and high-voltage product strategies, we're positioning Cyient semiconductors to participate in the addressable market opportunity of approximately $8.5 billion.

items.statement: Launched 7 new GaN products with Navitas targeting Indian market, primarily 650-volt GaN for chargers and industrial power supplies.
items.quote: In partnership with Navitas as well, we launched 7 new GaN products, specifically targeting the Indian market.

items.statement: Kinetic acquisition funded via ~$80 million foreign currency debt at Singapore entity; new fund raise adds INR 200 crore debt and INR 100 crore equity.
items.quote: We funded Kinetic through debt raised at Singapore entity because we got pretty good rates and we felt like that's a good use of our capital.

items.statement: Valuation at 6-7x revenue based on FY26/FY27; semiconductor peers trade at 5-15x revenue; M&A transactions at 10x+ revenue.
items.quote: This valuation roughly works out to be 6x revenue to 7x revenue, depending on which revenue we consider, FY26 or '27. The way to think about it is along these 3 lines: trading comparables with global semiconductor companies. Most semiconductor companies today are trading anywhere between 5x to 15x revenue depending on their profile.

items.statement: Data center power share growing from 2% in 2025 to 8% in 2030; power optimization critical for AI scale.
items.quote: The share of power for data centers is going up from 2% in 2025 to 8% in 2030.

items.statement: Actively developing 800-volt to 50-volt power architecture with GaN as component; participating in OCP for AI data center standards.
items.quote: We are working on the 800-volt to 50-volt power architecture, and GaN will be one of the components of that architecture.

items.statement: Filed 4 patents on high-voltage DC architecture and advanced delivery systems for AI data centers with hyperscalers.
items.quote: And during the year, we filed 4 patents focused on high-voltage DC architecture and advanced delivery systems for AI data centers along with NVIDIA, Google, Meta and other hyperscalers and infrastructure companies.

items.statement: Deliberately chose debt over equity to protect against dilution; not in a rush to raise more capital; will be selective on partners.
items.quote: We made a deliberate choice not to issue a large amount of equity at this stage to protect it against dilution and preserve the shareholder value we are working to create. Debt at this stage was simply the more flexible instrument.

items.statement: Reaffirm FY27 top line growth at 15% to 20% rate with potential for much stronger growth over coming years
items.quote: Further, we continue to see robust opportunities across all three product segments in the defines market and therefore reaffirm our FY27 top line growth at 15% to 20% rate, with a potential for much stronger growth over the coming years.

items.statement: Plan to book sales of INR1300 crores to INR1400 crores in FY27, around 15% to 20% growth compared to FY26
items.quote: Regarding execution front, we have planned to book sales of INR1300 crores to INR1400 crores, that is around 15% to 20% growth compared to FY26, covering 40% of R&D and 60% from the production area.

items.statement: Expect minimum 50% growth in both order booking and sales for ARC in FY27, with visibility of INR200 crores order book and expected to cross INR600 crores sales
items.quote: Going forward in FY27, we expect to outperform and we expect the minimum growth of 50% both in terms of order booking and as well as sales. As on date, we have visibility of INR200 crores order book in FY27 for ARC and also expected to cross INR600 crores sales.

items.statement: Standalone order book at INR2141 crores as on 31st March, with PNC of INR300 crores more orders expected in next couple of months
items.quote: In Q4 alone, we secured fresh orders worth of approximately INR530 crores, taking our total order book to a robust INR2141 crores as on 31st March, and concluded PNC of INR300 crores more orders which are expected to be received in next couple of months.

items.statement: Clear visibility of approximately INR1600 crores plus orders which can be booked in FY27, with 25% from R&D programs and balance from production orders
items.quote: Going forward, we have a clear visibility of approximately INR1600 crores plus orders which can be booked in the current year, that is FY27. Around 25% of this expected to come from R&D programs, while balance are basically driven by the production orders.

items.statement: Export margins improved with gross margin close to 40% on RF portion of SDRs co-developed with Rafael, higher than previous offset-based exports
items.quote: So, because of that, the value add is much higher than the regular exports that were recorded in the previous periods. Therefore, generally these carry good amount of value add. I would say the gross margin will be close to about 40% kind of thing in these exports.

items.statement: Management indicates current margins of 50%-55% are probably the top end and investors should factor in slightly lower numbers on margin front
items.quote: Okay, amid from a guidance perspective, I think we should very clearly state , this probably is the top end, you can actually you should factor in slightly lower numbers only on the margin front, so that there is no disappointment coming in at a later date.

items.statement: Annual capex of INR40-50 crores to continue, no additional capex beyond normal requirements for revenue tripling target
items.quote: Yes, in terms of the capex, as you know every year, we are augmenting the existing requirements by spending close to about INR40 crores, INR50 crores. So that will continue. Therefore, there won't be an additional capex beyond this what we are doing normally.

items.statement: Strong visibility in radar segment for airborne radar, fire control radar, surveillance and tracking radars, medium and long-range radars; EW segment growth from DRDO airborne platforms as DCPP; BEL programs like Nayan Shakti, Hima Shakti,
items.quote: Yes, the growth drivers, there are many programs are there, both, you know, especially in the radar segment, we have seen clear visibility in to grow in airborne radar, fire control radar and surveillance and tracking radars and medium-range and long-range radars.

items.statement: Transitioning from component manufacturer to IP-driven systems manufacturer and development-cum-production partner for strategic national programs; multiple Astra-owned IP branded products expected before Diwali
items.quote: We have in reality evolved from a component manufacturer to a deeply integrated, IP -driven systems manufacturer to now becoming a development-cum-production partner for strategic national programs.

items.statement: Su-30 upgrade program radar (Virupaksha) development completion expected in 2-3 months, qualification by FY28, production orders in 2-3 years; EW pod (Angad) development completion in 1 year, qualification thereafter
items.quote: For the radar, the AAAU which we have taken up development, that is on I think next two to three months we should be in a position to complete the development and hand over to DRDO. And in all probability, I think in maybe FY28, DRDO will be ready to qualify the overall radar.

items.statement: Aspire to nearly triple turnover over 4.5-5.5 years (up to FY30-FY31) based on 5-6 major programs including QRSAM, Uttam, Su-30 Virupaksha, Su-30 Angad, electronic mines, and JV business

items.statement: FY27 revenue growth at least 60%, similar to FY26.

items.statement: Revenue visibility of 9 months due to long-term infrastructure partnerships with banks and retailers
items.quote: Today for a bank and a retailer to replace or displace Pine Labs is a nine months effort. So honestly for us in our business to be able to see how the revenues are going to come through over the next nine months p eriod it is a very easy task there in front of

items.quote: Ramesh, answer around crypto is a very clear no. We have no interest in getting into crypto-related services. However, what is happening around stable coins is so exciting today when it comes to international markets.

items.statement: Company targeting above 20% EBITDA margin for FY27.

items.quote: Recently, we acquired an order from the Central Bank worth 88 crores. Now, Bank of Abyssinia is an Ethiopian bank; they're gonna… We'll get a technology revenue of 4 crore onl y from the Bank of Abyssinia
