items.statement: Redemption rates in India 7-10%; mature markets 45-50%; potential to increase redemption revenue 4x.
items.quote: in the Indian banking ecosystem, like, it's only about 7-10%, depending on which bank, which program, points are getting utilised. So the major issue is the loyalty discovery side of it.

items.statement: Reseller commissions 15-30% for international partnerships.
items.quote: Most of the time, when you work with the reseller, it's anything between 15% to 30% that goes to resellers.

items.statement: FY27 revenue expected north of INR 600-700 crore with full Netcom consolidation.
items.quote: So we should be heading close north of roughly around INR 600-700 CR from a top-line perspective.

items.statement: Margins to remain between 20-25%, with potential for larger increase as AI progresses.
items.quote: Our margins will remain between 20-25%.

items.statement: Expects to continue 24% YoY growth trajectory in coming years.
items.quote: No, we are anyway on a trajectory of 24% YoY growth. So, I think we should be able to continue that in the years to come.

items.statement: Invested around INR 100 crore in AI ecosystem, including ResolX.
items.quote: So, as yet, we are invested around INR 100 CR like that.

items.statement: Netcom acquisition funded with USD 23 million debt, USD 14.75 million disbursed; company otherwise debt-free.
items.value: USD 23 million debt, USD 14.75 million disbursed
items.quote: So, in this acquisition, we have exposure around 23 million debt. So currently, in the disbursement point of view, they have disbursed 14.75 million debt.

items.statement: ResolX has 10-12 active PoCs and 12-15 paid PoCs in pipeline.
items.quote: Today, ResolX is already live across seven engagements with 10 to 12 active proof of concepts across sectors, including banking, airlines, automobiles, and healthcare.

items.statement: Provides 20-40% TCO savings to clients, safeguarding own pricing.
items.quote: So, when we say that we will give you a TCO saving in a given range between 20-40%, it's a journey that we basically walk through with them to make it happen.

items.statement: 15% of customers have deployed AI solutions in one or more LOBs.
items.quote: So, about 15% of our customers have actively deployed our AI solutions in one or multiple levels of LOBs with them.

items.statement: AI industry adaptation across verticals will take 3-5 years, affecting margin expansion pace.
items.quote: But AI as an industry is still being a little more adaptive across multiple industries and verticals, and it will only progress over next 3-5 years.

items.statement: Plans 2-3 acquisitions over next few years, EPS accretive from day one.
items.quote: We have a strong inorganic pipeline in place and plan to make two to three acquisitions over the next few years.

items.statement: ResolX deployment takes 1.5-5 weeks, faster than competitors' 3-6 months.
items.quote: With us, we are able to deploy this in as low as about, one and a half to two weeks to a maximum of about four to five weeks.

items.statement: Passes 30-35% efficiencies to clients on day one of ResolX deployment.
items.quote: So today, wherever we've deployed, we've been able to pass on over 30-35% of efficiencies back to the client on day one of deployment.

items.statement: Capex guidance for FY27: INR1,500-1,700 crores total, with INR400 crores for Lead Acid and INR1,100-1,200 crores for New Energy
items.quote: In the coming year, we would be spending an amount in the range of INR1,500 crores to INR1,700 crores as capex, about INR400 crores or so in the Lead Acid Battery business and less -- rest of around INR1,100 crores to INR1,200 crores of capex in the New Energy business.

items.statement: FY26 capex was ~INR600 crores for Lead Acid (net ~INR500 crores after insurance claim) and the rest for New Energy projects including R&D lab and Customer Qualification Plant
items.quote: As far as capex is concerned, we have spent roughly about INR600 crores in our Lead Acid business, both between the Battery business as well as the Recycling business. And the rest of the money was spent on the new energy projects, including the research lab and then Customer Qualification Plant.

items.statement: Supplied >300 MWh telecom packs in Q4 FY26 and crossed cumulative 1 GWh stationary installations in FY26
items.quote: In the current quarter, we have almost supplied more than 300-megawatt hour of telecom packs to various telecom players. And in this current quarter, we have also infused about INR100 crores further into Amara Raja Advanced Cell Technologies, our new energy subsidiary.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 standalone EBITDA margin ~11%; Lead Acid operating margin 11.6% (ex-lithium trading) and 12.3% (with recycling adjustment); FY26 consolidated margin 10.8%, Lead Acid 12.2%
items.quote: As far as margins are concerned, the current quarter has seen the overall EBITDA margin standing at about 11% on stand-alone basis. But if I adjust for the trading revenue of lithium batteries, then the Lead Acid Battery business has generated an operating margin of 11.6%.

items.statement: Medium-term Lead Acid EBITDA margin target remains 13-14% even at INR2 lakh/ton lead price, driven by throughput gains and cost pass-through
items.quote: But as I mentioned in the earlier calls also that we would -- we are still hopeful to reach a 13% to 14% kind of an EBITDA margin even at a 2 lakh kind of a lead base predominantly on account of the initiatives that were alluded to earlier.

items.statement: Took 5-6% price increases in Domestic Automotive in Q4 FY26; may need another 2-3% in coming periods depending on rupee, freight, raw material costs and competitor moves
items.quote: To mitigate some of these raw material price increases, we have taken some price increases in Q4 at about 5% to 6% in the Domestic Automotive business in tranches. And now considering the way the rupee is depreciating and also the enhanced cost of freight and raw materials might force us to look at some more price increases in the coming periods.

items.statement: FY27 Lead Acid volume outlook: mid-to-high single-digit growth in replacement and industrial segments, with OEM growing faster; international markets to improve via localization strategies
items.quote: Along those lines, we'll continue to see that mid to high single-digit growth, which is one, of course, growing a bit better than the market, also further segmenting ourselves, for example, our renewed focus on home energy will sustain, and we're looking to, of course, develop new products and put them into market.

items.statement: New Energy mix shifting: long-term EV/ESS split moving from 80/20 toward ~2/3 EV and 1/3 ESS; ESS integration facility (5 GWh initial, 10 GWh ultimate) targeting production start by end of calendar year
items.quote: We're aiming to start production at the end of this calendar year with an initial capacity of 5 gigawatt hour in a facility with the ultimate capacity of 10 gigawatt hour.

items.statement: Customer Qualification Plant (CQP) in final commissioning; commercial cell samples to customers in next couple of months; Giga 1 (2 GWh NMC 2170) on track for June 2027 production start
items.quote: The Customer Qualification Plant, as Delli mentioned, is in the final phase of commissioning. We are running the final trials to stabilize all processes and optimistic that our ability to start delivering commercial samples is going to start to our customers in the next couple of months.

items.statement: Gotion LFP technology licensing stalled due to Chinese government restrictions on tech transfer; LFP cell production now self-driven, expected 2028 or later
items.quote: Since that time, I think all of you would have also been seeing in the news that sharing of technology, licensing technology is something that's been largely discouraged by the Chinese government. This is hitting all players and their technical tie-ups pretty equally.

items.statement: Cell manufacturing cost disadvantage vs China imports estimated at 15-20% initially; breakeven EBITDA margin 10-11% seen at 8-10 GWh scale with capex reduction and potential policy support
items.quote: I think it's like China plus 15% to 20% is the minimum that we can bridge immediately because we don't have local material and a couple of other things that is advantageous to China in terms of scale.

items.statement: Invested INR100 crores in AR Advanced Cell Technologies in Q4 FY26; cumulative investment ~INR1,500 crores
items.quote: And in this current quarter, we have also infused about INR100 crores further into Amara Raja Advanced Cell Technologies, our new energy subsidiary. With this, the overall investment into this subsidiary is about INR1,500 crores.

items.statement: BESS integration facility initial operating margins estimated at 6-7%, with upside as scale improves; will act as strategic lever for ESS cell manufacturing decisions
items.quote: The operating margins could be around, let's say, 6% to 7% to start with. But we feel as the opportunity progresses, while we are starting with the 5 gigawatt initial capacity, I'm sure it can be expanded further.

items.statement: Q4 FY26: 4-wheeler OEM volumes >30% growth, 2-wheeler OEM >30% growth, aftermarket 5-6% growth, tubular batteries >35% growth, industrial (ex-telecom) ~3-4% growth, telecom lead-acid declining but offset by lithium
items.quote: The 4-wheeler OEM volumes have seen a sustained growth over and above 30% during the current quarter. The aftermarket volumes also considering the larger base have grown about 5% to 6%, both in 4-wheeler as well as 2-wheeler.

items.statement: Total planned capex for Giga Corridor ~INR9,500 crores; capex per GWh reduced 20-25% from initial $55-60M estimate; target ROCE low double-digits at 8-10 GWh scale
items.quote: when we started the journey, we looked at somewhere around $55 million to $60 million per gigawatt hour of capex which today. I'm sure has come down almost by 20% to 25% already.

items.statement: Export volumes muted due to geopolitical issues (Middle East) and tariff barriers (North America); exports 11% of Q4 revenue, 12% of FY26 revenue; pursuing localization strategies to improve resilience
items.quote: During the current quarter, with the ongoing geopolitical issues, we have seen a muted growth in the export volumes of Automotive business. And we hope in the next coming quarters, the momentum will revive.

items.statement: Only capex this year is a new jaggery facility of about Rs 45 crore; no other capex plans
items.quote: The only CAPEX that we are doing this year is largely the new Jaggery facility. That is about a 45-odd crore CAPEX which we are doing. There are no other CAPEX plans.

items.statement: CPG business targets break-even within 6-8 quarters and aims to exit the decade with good single-digit EBITDA margin
items.quote: The intent is to break even within the next 6-8 quarters and exit this decade with a good single-digit percentage EBITDA on this business.

items.statement: Expect 10-15% increase in cane planting in Tamil Nadu for the upcoming season
items.quote: We have planted roughly about we are looking at about 10-15% increase in the planting.

items.statement: Ethanol production could rise to 17 crore litres from 16 crore litres if blending percentage increases
items.quote: We have, as Muthu pointed out earlier, produced about 16 crore liters. We would probably tend towards 17 crore liters if there is an improvement in ethanol blending percentage.

items.statement: Government unlikely to raise sugar MSP given inflationary pressures
items.quote: Not really. I think given the inflationary pressures it is unlikely.

items.statement: PSRIPL refinery closure on track; all loan obligations to be completed by 30 June 2026
items.quote: With the above, all the loans obligations of PSRIPL will get completed by 30th June 2026.

items.statement: CPG strategy shifts to higher-margin sweetener products (jaggery, brown sugar, premium whites) targeting 30%+ gross margins
items.quote: Lot of these value-added products move the business into the 30+% gross margin level. And this is really the intent in terms of how we want to move forward.

items.statement: Future CPG expansion focused on ethnic snacking and culinary convenience segments
items.quote: We are talking about ethnic snacking and culinary convenience. These are segments which we are looking at further.

items.statement: Nutra India stable; Valensa to drive top-line expansion and stronger bottom-line after restructuring and two new product launches
items.quote: I think what we will see in Valensa is an expansion of top line. As well as a stronger bottom-line performance.

items.statement: Cane cost rose to Rs 4,087/MT in Q4 FY26 from Rs 3,768/MT a year ago due to Rs 150/MT FRP increase
items.quote: So, cane cost for the current quarter is Rs. 4087 per metric ton (MT) as against the Rs. 3768 per MT of the corresponding quarter of the previous year.

items.statement: Ethanol pricing unlikely to see revision; government focus is on increasing blending percentages
items.quote: Our last read of the situation was that there may not be too much action on pricing but there will be an action on increase in blending percentages.

items.statement: Sugar sales volume in Q4 FY26 was 97,000 MT including 6,000 MT exports vs 73,000 MT a year ago
items.quote: As far as the sugar volumes are concerned, we sold about 97,000 MT, which includes about 6,000 MT of the exports, as against 73,000 MT of the corresponding quarter of the previous year.

items.statement: Tamil Nadu power tariff tribunal order not applicable; any benefit assessed as not substantial
items.quote: I don't think it's a substantial amount.

items.statement: FY27 overall revenue target ₹9,400-9,500 crores, 24-25% growth; Steel ₹7,200 crores, Lighting ₹2,200 crores.
items.quote: Overall, in Lighting and Steel, the revenue will be around ₹7,200 crores from the Steel Division and around ₹2,200 crores from the Lighting Division. So, the overall revenue will be ₹9,400 crores to ₹9,500 crores this year.

items.statement: FY27 combined EBITDA target ₹680-700 crores, 25-26% growth; Steel ₹470-480 crores, Lighting ₹200 crores.
items.quote: Similarly, in EBITDA, it will be around ₹480 crores in the Steel Division and around ₹200 crores in Lighting. So, this will be around ₹680 crores. In this also, there will be a growth of 25-26%.

items.statement: FY27 steel pipe volume target 11 lakh tons, 21-22% growth over FY26.
items.quote: Looking ahead to FY27, we are targeting overall volume of 11 lakh tons, representing growth of nearly 21% to 22% over FY26, supported by improving utilization levels, phased commissioning of new capacities and strong contribution from value-added products.

items.statement: FY27 exports target over 2.5 lakh tons, nearly double FY26's 1.36 lakh tons.
items.quote: Exports stood at 1.36 lakh tons for FY26, and we are targeting to cross 2.5 lakh tons in the coming year.

items.statement: FY27 Wire and Cable revenue target ₹260 crores, on track for 3-year ₹500-600 crores.
items.quote: Our FY27 revenue target for the Wire and Cable business is ₹260 crores, firmly on track with the three-year guidance of ₹500 crores to ₹600 crores business.

items.statement: Medium-term annual value growth target of 22-25% for Lighting and Consumer Durables segment.
items.quote: Overall, we are targeting value growth of 22% to 25% annually in Lighting and Consumer Durables segment overall -- over the medium term, supported by deeper distribution penetration, premiumization and continued investment in brand building.

items.statement: Steel Division order book over ₹1,000 crores, led by exports, spiral, and domestic API orders.
items.quote: The current order book of the Steel Division is about ₹1,000 crores plus, led by exports, spiral, and some domestic API orders, providing strong visibility for H1 FY27, which is expected to be the highest-ever half year for value-added product sales.

items.statement: Professional Lighting order book at ₹160 crores at end of Q4 FY26.
items.quote: The Professional Lighting business achieved double-digit revenue growth at ₹473 crores for the full year, being a 26% share in the total revenue of the Lighting segment and ended Q4 FY26 with an order book of ₹160 crores, providing healthy near-term execution visibility.

items.statement: FY27 steel EBITDA per ton expected around ₹4,700, with exports at ₹9,000-10,000 per ton.
items.quote: So, considering both things, we assume ₹4,700 per ton EBITDA for the whole year.

items.statement: Capacity to increase from 1.4 million tons to 1.6 million in FY27, then to 1.9 million by FY28-29.
items.quote: We have already reached 1.4 million. It was 1.2 something; now our capacity has already been enhanced to about 1.4and which will become around 1.6 million tons in the next one year, in FY27.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 expected highest-ever volume at 2.65 lakh tons, 27-28% growth.
items.quote: Our Q1 will have the highest-ever volume, around 2.65 lakh tons in Q1 itself and we will grow by about 27% to 28%.

items.statement: Imported raw material cost impact 30-35%, passed on with 1-2 month lag.
items.quote: The impact in our input raw material imported is around 30% to 35%. It's good that somehow it got passed on in the market, but it takes one or two months for it to be passed on, which reflects in the balance sheet.

items.statement: Value-added products contributed 43% of FY26 volume; exports to boost mix.
items.quote: And most importantly, the value-added products contributed 43% of overall volume during the year FY26.

items.statement: Expect high-single digit to low-double digit volume growth for combined business in FY27, followed by double-digit growth over next couple of years and double-digit volume CAGR over next 3 years
items.quote: For FY27, we expect to achieve a high-single digit to low-double digit volume growth for the combined business, which will be followed by a double-digit volume growth over the next couple of years. We expect a double digit volume CAGR over the next 3 years.

items.statement: Expect consolidated EBITDA margins to reach 16%-18% for combined business over next 24 to 36 months, including accounting change benefit
items.quote: In terms of margins, we expect the consolidated EBITDA margins to reach 16%-18% for the combined business over the next 24 to 36 months. The positive change in guidance also includes the change in the presentation and disclosure of selling expenses, which Mr. Dahanukar had spoken about earlier.

items.statement: Expect net debt-to-EBITDA ratio to go below 1.0x by FY29
items.quote: As guided in the past as well, we expect the net debt-to-EBITDA ratio to go below 1.0x by FY29.

items.statement: Capex will be maintenance capex of approximately INR 25 crore each in FY27 and FY28
items.quote: So capex, I think, will be maintenance capex for both the years. I do not think capex will be large. Approximately, we can take INR 25 crore in each of the years.

items.statement: Expect net debt of approximately INR 1,700 crore by end of March 2027 with upside bias
items.quote: By the end of March-27, you are looking at a net debt of approximately INR 1,700 crore or thereabouts. So you will see a reduction in the net debt with an upside bias to some extent.

items.statement: Expect some pressure on input costs and margins due to geopolitical scenario; working on cost optimizations to mitigate impact
items.quote: On the margin front, because of the current ongoing geopolitical scenario, we do expect some pressure on the input costs and margins. To combat this, we have identified and are working on several areas of cost optimizations, which will mitigate the impact of this increase in raw material prices.

items.statement: Potential price increase in Telangana expected to have reasonable impact on margins; timelines unknown
items.quote: Telangana is one of the potential states where we are expecting a price increase, but obviously, timelines are not known on that front. But given how large Telangana is for us as a state, it will have a reasonable impact on margins.

items.statement: UK FTA custom duty reduction benefit estimated at 60-100 bps on combined business margins, mainly for Imperial Blue
items.quote: Any reduction in custom duty, will reduce the scotch prices and consequently provide a positive impact on the gross margin levels. However, this will be majorly towards Imperial Blue business. It will not have any major impact on the Ex-IB portfolio of Tilaknagar. On the combined business basis, the margin benefit will be to the tune of 60-100 bps.

items.statement: 75% of Imperial Blue business exited TSMA by Q4 FY26; remaining 3 states to transition by March 2027
items.quote: In the Q3 earnings call, we had mentioned that TI will exit the TSMA for significant operations by the end of Q4 FY26, and we have delivered on that. 75% of the IB business has exited TSMA till Q4 FY26. For the states where we have exited TSMA in Q4 FY26, we have already started full-fledged operations at TI units. Now only 3 states remain under TSMA, and we expect to transition them over the cour

items.statement: TSMA fees expected to decrease quarter-on-quarter with full year impact of INR 55-60 crore
items.quote: Basically, you can consider TSMA fees to be decreasing quarter-on-quarter with a full year impact of, let us call it, anywhere between INR 55 crore to INR 60 crore.

items.statement: Karnataka policy change reduced MRP by INR 20 per nip for Imperial Blue and Mansion House; expect further volume uptake similar to previous price reduction that drove high-teens growth
items.quote: So as I had mentioned in my opening remarks, we expect an MRP reduction of approximately INR 20 on both the flagship brands, Imperial Blue and Mansion House, on the 180 ml pack size. So with the reduction in the MRP, we may expect a further uptake in the volumes going forward.

items.statement: Plan to launch brandy in northern markets in FY27 including mass, mid-prestige and luxury Monarch portfolio
items.quote: As it stands, we have not launched brandy in the northern markets. But having said so, we are in the process of doing that in FY27. This is true not only for the mass and the semi-prestige or mass and the mid-prestige portfolio, but even for our luxury portfolio in the form of Monarch.

items.statement: Working capital cycle expected in range of 53 to 55 days of gross revenue on ongoing basis
items.quote: Yes. So I think on an ongoing basis, Mehul, we can look at the working capital cycle in the range of 53 to 55 days of gross revenue. So that is the way I would look at it.

items.statement: Deferred consideration of EUR 28 million payable to Pernod Ricard after 4 years of acquisition; no other Imperial Blue related costs
items.quote: So Heer, there, as we mentioned in the earlier presentations as well, after 4 years of the acquisition, there will be a deferred consideration. There is a deferred consideration of EUR 28 million that we need to pay to Pernod Ricard. But apart from that, there are no other costs that are to be incurred.

items.statement: Shrirampur ENA distillery recommissioning under consideration; no timeline decided
items.quote: So it is under consideration. We will take a call at the appropriate time in terms of recommissioning of the distillery.

items.statement: Infrastructure can deliver INR4,000 crore revenue and INR700-800 crore EBITDA at optimal utilization, expected in 18-24 months.
items.value: INR4,000-odd crores top line and approximately INR700 crores to INR800 crores in bottom line in EBITDA
items.quote: But our infrastructure should be able to deliver around INR4,000-odd crores in top line and approximately INR700 crores to INR800 crores in bottom line in EBITDA, and which I have shared with stakeholders earlier, if we were to run at optimal capacity utilization levels.

items.statement: Medium-term EBITDA margin guidance remains 18-22%.
items.quote: medium-term view on margin profile remains between 18% and 22%.

items.statement: Home textiles will become approximately half of portfolio; new verticals to contribute the rest.
items.quote: Ultimately home textiles will become approximately half our portfolio.

items.statement: Board approved raising up to INR850 crore via NCDs, net debt neutral.
items.quote: the Board has also, at its meeting held on the 27th of May, approved raising of up to INR850 crores through issuance of senior secured redeemable nonconvertible debentures on a private placement basis.

items.statement: No additional capex for new verticals; will stay within maintenance capex budget.
items.quote: I've said that for the most part, we will be within our maintenance capex budget. I wouldn't want to take on more capex at this point until I'm delivering reasonably well on the operating performance for our investors.

items.statement: Middle East overhang to impact shipments to certain jurisdictions in Q1 FY27.
items.quote: We expect the Middle East overhang to continue to impact shipments to certain jurisdictions even during Q1 FY27 as we see at this point.

items.statement: New verticals revenue to start materializing from H2 FY27.
items.quote: it should start panning out in a more material format, say, starting H2 FY27 is what we estimate.

items.statement: Net debt target approximately INR2,000 crore within next 12 months.
items.quote: I think directionally, our next bus stop is we would like to bring our net debt down to approximately levels of INR2,000 crores.

items.statement: Current net debt approximately INR2,550 crore.
items.quote: The net debt is approximately 2,550.

items.statement: Near-term margin pressure from war and inflation, but medium-term outlook unchanged.
items.quote: But I think that in the near-term, there could be some pressure arising out of this war and it's the inflationary impacts that it had.

items.statement: India revenue was just over INR100 crore in FY26, expected to improve.
items.quote: Yes. It was just over INR100 crores actually. We expect that to improve further this year.

items.statement: Dividend for FY26 at INR0.25 per equity share.
items.quote: And our dividend for the year remains range bound at INR0.25 per equity share with trade-off value of INR5 per equity share for FY26.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 other income INR100 crore driven by forex gain of INR95 crore.
items.quote: The Q4 other income amounting to just INR100 crores was primarily driven by foreign exchange movements of approximately INR95 crores.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 capacity utilization: spinning 99%, sheeting 56%, terry towel 63%.
items.quote: And the utilization levels during the quarter stood at 99%, 56% and 63%, respectively, for spinning, sheeting and Terry Towel division.

items.statement: Expects INR300 crores revenue from new 150 KLPD unit at 100% utilization.
items.quote: So from that, if we run that at 100% utilization, we are expecting somewhere around INR300 crores from that 150 KLPD unit.

items.statement: Aims to maintain or improve EBITDA margins with new capacity and stable overheads.
items.quote: So yes, we are seeing the similar EBITDA margins going forward. Rather, there would be improvement in the EBITDA margin.

items.statement: Plans to utilize at least 75% of new 150 KLPD capacity from Q2 FY27.
items.quote: So, our expectation is that we'll be able to atleast utilize the 75% of the capacity starting from the second quarter.

items.statement: Proposed additional 250 KLPD distillery expansion at Fatehabad, to commission in about 2 years.
items.quote: We remain on track for proposed additional 250 KLPD distillery expansion at our Fatehabad plant in Haryana, which would be undertaken in line with the evolving industry landscape and policy implementation.

items.statement: Distillery EBITDA margin expected to be maintained or improved from 11.8%.
items.quote: I think we will be able to maintain or rather improve the EBITDA margin of 11.8%.

items.statement: Aims to be debt-free within 5 years, reducing finance costs.
items.quote: And we ha ve positioned ourselves, within 5 years, we should be a total debt -free company, which we are focusing on, you must have noticed from our financial results, the financial cost is coming down year-to-year.

items.statement: Plans to launch IMFL brands in North India then Pan-India, requiring about INR100 crores.
items.quote: So we do have that in the plan. First, we wanted to consolidate our portion, have a good amount of cash with the company because this IMFL business, first will take away about INR100 crores in the pocket for the launching of this IMFL brand on a Pan-India basis.

items.statement: Expects to realize about INR30 crores from sale of 18-acre land parcel.
items.quote: Value as of now, very difficult to say, but we should be able to realize close to about INR30 crores of fees from that parcel.

items.statement: Plans 20-ton CBG plant at Fatehabad after ethanol plant commissioning, within 2-3 years.
items.quote: And after the commissioning of that plant, another 1 year, we'll be taking for putting up a 20-ton CBG.

items.statement: Acquisition of remaining 25% stake in Svaksha Distillery to complete by end of June 2026.
items.quote: Further, the acquisition of the remaining 25% stake in Svaksha Distillery is getting executed as per the planned time line and is expected to be completed by the end of June 2026, following which Svaksha Distillery will become a wholly owned subsidiary of BCL Industries Limited.

items.statement: Biodiesel plant not operating due to lack of mandate; used as vegetable oil refinery.
items.quote: So, at present, we are operating that plant on a vegetable oil refinery. So, whenever there is, you can say, the policy revision of the biodiesel rates, we'll be able to participate and we are already enrolled as a biodiesel supplier with all the OMC.

items.statement: Edible oil business to continue bulk sales, revenue INR700-800 crores per annum.
items.quote: So that revenue will always be there about INR700 crores to INR800 crores per annum only will be.

items.statement: PML market growing at 18-20%, IMFL market at 12%.
items.quote: The IMFL market is growing at 12%. And this PML market, we are also growing at about 18% to 20%.

items.statement: Net debt about INR300-335 crores, including fund-based and non-fund based.
items.quote: It's about INR300 crores, INR335 crores, including fund-based and non-fund based.

items.statement: FY27 revenue target INR600-700 crores, with exports around INR200 crores.
items.quote: Yes, it is -- we are to be -- yes, targeting INR600 crores to INR700 crores.

items.statement: FY27 EBIT margin target 15-20%.
items.quote: Margins, it will be similar between 15% to 20%.

items.statement: Current order book INR1,569 crores, 4.04x FY26 revenue, to execute over 2-3 years.
items.quote: Highest ever order book stands at INR1,569 crores, representing 4.04x of FY26 revenue and providing strong medium-term visibility.

items.statement: Export order book 54%, domestic 46%.
items.quote: Exports is about 54% and domestic is about 46%.

items.statement: INR430 crores order: two-thirds to be executed in FY27, one-third in FY28.
items.quote: It will be -- I think two third will be done before the end of financial year '27, one third may still flow to next year.

items.statement: Export license for INR350 crores order expected in about 3 months.
items.quote: It's a running process always, this following up with the export license. Maybe I think in 3 months' time, we should be able to get this.

items.statement: Export license rejection risk exists due to government policy.
items.quote: Yes. This is -- see, under ARMS ACT and all this, this is -- export license is very important. And in this business, yes, there is a possibility of export license getting rejected also based on -- because this depends on the government policy.

items.statement: ISRO contract: INR18 crores per annum, constant, with 2.5 years remaining.
items.quote: That is around INR18 crores per annum. The contract life is about another 2.5 years.

items.statement: Katepally expansion to be commissioned by September, production from November.
items.quote: And the time frame what we are looking at is by September month, this will come into commissioning stage. And after commissioning, we may be -- in November month onwards, we are expecting that we can start producing for this facility.

items.statement: Andhra Pradesh 400-acre land acquisition in progress; commissioning expected in 1-1.5 years.
items.quote: We are currently in discussions with Andhra Pradesh government for acquisition of a 400 -acre land parcel to establish a dedicated defense manufacturing facility.

items.statement: Odisha capex plan delayed; phases 2 and 3 may take 4-5 years.
items.quote: So after that, the second and third phases, then we are thinking of Orissa and then which may take around 4 to 5 years.

items.statement: LD reversal claim of around INR30 crores pending with government.
items.quote: We are trying with the government. We have to see, it is around INR30 crores kind of thing.

items.statement: Jagdalpur O&M contract lost due to higher costs; no longer servicing.
items.quote: We have not got the last -- current running order. We lost that in our bidding. So Jagdalpur is no more being serviced by us.

items.statement: Raw material prices expected to increase 18-20% in Q1FY27 from Q4 levels
items.quote: Keeping in view the ongoing situation, raw material prices are expected to go up by 18 -20% in Q1FY27 from Q4.

items.statement: Price hikes of 4-5% in replacement market and 5-7% in export markets already taken; further 5-6% hike underway
items.quote: We have already taken a hike of 4-5% across products in replacement market and 5 -7% in export markets. The situa tion is being actively monitored for JK Tyre & necessary further price hikes to offset the increase in raw material prices (further hike of 5 -6% is underway).

items.statement: Board approved additional brownfield expansions for PCR and TBR at Rs.4,980 crore in phases until 2029, increasing capacities by 24%
items.quote: the Board, in addition to the expansion projects of Rs.1,130 crore under implementation, has approved to undertake further brownfield expansions for PCR and TBR segments at an aggregate cost of Rs.4,980 Cr in phases until 2029. This will increase TBR & PCR capacities by 24%

items.statement: Total expansion outlay of Rs.6,110 crore (including Rs.1,130 crore announced earlier) to be completed by FY29 with yearly cash outlay of ~Rs.1,200 crore
items.quote: these total expansions of Rs.6,110 crores will be completed by FY29. Total cash outlay on yearly basis would be roughly around Rs.1,200 crores

items.statement: Q4FY26 EBITDA margin expanded 270 bps to 12.9% driven by higher volumes, improved product mix and cost optimization
items.quote: Consolidated EBITDA for Q4 stood at Rs.546 crore, registering a 42% growth. EBITDA margin was recorded at 12.9%, an expansion of 270 basis points. This growth was driven by higher volumes, an improved product mix and sustained cost optimization initiatives.

items.statement: Demand expected to remain buoyant in FY27 with healthy growth in replacement and OE markets; no OEM order book cuts seen
items.quote: the demand in the tyre industry is expected to remain buoyant for FY27 on the back of healthy growth in both the replacement and OE markets. We have not seen any order books getting cut from any of the OEM

items.statement: Premiumization strategy driving growth; premium passenger tyres (16" and above) grew 13% in domestic markets in FY26
items.quote: This growth has been contributed by JK Tyre & increased sale of premium tyres (16' & above) which have grown by 13% in domestic markets (FY26 v/s FY25)

items.statement: West Asia crisis causing supply chain disruptions and surge in crude oil, petrochemical and commodity prices creating inflationary environment
items.quote: West Asia crisis, which has led to disruptions in supplies of crude oil, petro chemicals and other critical commodities, leading to an unusual surge in prices, thereby creating a highly inflationary environment.

items.statement: No order book cuts from any OEM across CV, passenger or other lines despite geopolitical uncertainties
items.quote: We have not seen any order books getting cut from any of the OEM, be CV s, passenger or any other line.

items.statement: Capex to be funded through debt-equity ratio of 2:1 using bank loans and internal accruals; leverage ratios expected to remain comfortable
items.quote: the total amount of Rs.6,110 crores of projects will have the debt-to-equity which we have announced of about 2:1. So, we have to take the funds from the bank plus our internal accruals

items.statement: Raw material cost increase of 18-19% expected in Q1FY27; some softening seen in crude oil prices may bring down RM prices beyond Q2
items.quote: On the raw material prices, we are seeing an increase of nearly 18% to 19% in Q1FY27, and going forward, actually, it will be depending on the war, but we are seeing some softening to an extent in the crude oil prices. This may have a positive impact on bringing down the overall raw material prices as we go forward beyond Q2 onwards.

items.statement: AUM growth guidance for next year in line with historical 15%-25% range.
items.quote: The next year guidance will be in line with anything between 15%-25% that we have been doing it for last 3-4 years.

items.statement: Wholesale segment expected to remain strong and key growth driver in FY27.
items.quote: The wholesale segment is expected to remain strong and will remain a key growth driver.

items.statement: SME retail expected to return to normalcy in FY27 as operating environment improves.
items.quote: We expect SME retail, which fell short of our growth ambitions in FY26, to return to normalcy in the coming year as the operating environment gradually improves.

items.statement: SME retail book expected to grow in FY27.
items.quote: Growth is expected in the SME retail book in FY27 as well and we expect to do better as the operating environment becomes more conducive.

items.statement: Absolute gross and net NPA not expected to increase next financial year.
items.quote: going forward we don't expect that the absolute gross and net NPA should increase in the next financial year

items.statement: Credit cost around 0.5% expected to stabilize; recoveries to cover fresh NPAs.
items.quote: the credit cost which has been around 0.5%, I think we should be stabilizing between that credit cost only and the recovery should take care of whatever fresh NPAs that we may see.

items.statement: Weighted average tax rate expected around 27% due to IndAS fee amortization.
items.quote: So, our tax percentage is always higher than the normal tax which is 25.17% I think weighted average will be around 27%.

items.statement: Concluded term sheet for Rs. 30 crore NCD issue to diversify funding.
items.quote: A notable milestone was also achieved this quarter was the conclusion of the term sheet of our Rs. 30 crore NCD issue which further diversifies our funding pool and increases access to debt capital markets.

items.statement: Leverage at 1.39x leaves headroom to increase leverage for FY27 growth.
items.quote: our leverage ratio stands at a comfortable 1.39x as of March 31, 2026, well within our conservative thresholds and leaving meaningful headroom to increase leverage for growth in FY27.

items.statement: AUM mix now 69% wholesale and 31% SME retail.
items.quote: our AUM mix has tilted further towards wholesale now at 69% of wholesale and 31% of SME retail.

items.statement: Off-book co-lending in wholesale to strengthen fee-based income in FY27 and beyond.
items.quote: We closed a few deals during Q4 and anticipate more activity in the coming quarters which should strengthen our fee-based income in FY27 and beyond.

items.statement: SME retail faces over-leveraged borrowers, stagnant income, and rising competition.
items.quote: Concerns such as over leveraged borrow profile, stagnant income growth across the MSME ecosystem and an increase in competitive intensity continue to affect the growth in SME retail verticals.

items.statement: Next 3 months focus on consolidating branches and improving productivity; new branches from Q3.
items.quote: So, the next 3 months will be to improve our productivity on the existing branches and rather than opening new branches that will start in the 3rd Quarter

items.statement: New ECL policy approved; provisioning to be more objective from coming year.
items.quote: The Board has also approved a new ECL policy this quarter aligned with our current business composition which will provide a more appropriate provisioning framework going forward.

items.statement: Targets 20% volume growth and 20% CAGR in revenue and profitability by 2030.
items.quote: We continue to expand our lead and copper capacities while strengthening our presence across adjacent nonferrous recycling segments to deliver 20% volume growth and 20% CAGR in revenue and profitability.

items.statement: Aims to maintain EBITDA margins above 8% and ROCE above 20%.
items.quote: Our growth is complemented by a strong focus on margin expansion with targets maintaining EBITDA margins above 8% and return on capital employed above 20%.

items.statement: Plans INR 180-200 crores capex in FY27 for capacity augmentation.
items.quote: For the current year, our capex will be well within number -- approximately around INR 180 crores will be the capex – INR 180 crores to INR 200 crores for this financial year.

items.statement: Plans INR 50-60 crores capex in FY28 for Phase II copper expansion.
items.quote: And the following financial year will be probably in the range of INR 50 crores to INR 60 crores, unless additional anything else is specifically added, which we'll keep you updated.

items.statement: Targets over 60% of revenue from value-added products long-term.
items.quote: At the same time, we remain committed to enhancing operational efficiency through innovation, modernization and increased value addition with the goal of deriving over 60% of re venue from value -added products.

items.statement: Expects lead volume of 125,000-130,000 tons in FY27.
items.quote: In terms of volume, like I just spoke to, we're looking at somewhere around 125,000 - 130,000 tons of volume for this year.

items.statement: Targets copper volume of 12,000 tons in FY27 including cathode.
items.quote: Yes. So including the copper cathode the volumes on copper will be approximately 12,000 tons.

items.statement: Expects copper volume of 24,000-28,000 tons in FY28.
items.quote: Yes. Towards the end of FY '28, we should be able to do a volume of 36,000 tons, close to -- so in FY '28, we can look at anywhere between 28,000 -- 24,000 to 28,000, 29,000 tons of copper.

items.statement: Guides lead EBITDA per ton of INR 17,000-19,000.
items.quote: In lead, we'll give you a margin guidance of 17,000 to 19,000 as we've been doing.

items.statement: Guides copper recycling EBITDA per ton of INR 35,000-40,000.
items.quote: And on a conservative basis, for copper on the recycling part, anywhere between 35,000 to 40,000 trying to maintain on the upper band.

items.statement: Expects copper cathode EBITDA per ton of INR 60,000-70,000.
items.quote: And once the cathode part comes in, right now with our numbers, we are looking at a margin of 60,000 to 70,000 again being on the upper band on a conservative level.

items.statement: Targets 15% year-on-year lead volume growth in FY28.
items.quote: Year-on-year on the lead volumes, we are looking at about 15% in growth volumes.

items.statement: Copper cathode plant Phase 1 commissioning targeted by December 2026.
items.quote: The project will be implemented in 2 phases of 18,000 metric tons per annum each and Phase 1 is targeted for commissioning by December 2026, which marks a significant step in expanding our nonferrous recycling portfolio and enhancing value-added capabiliti es.

items.statement: Notes 10-20 day delays in raw material receipt due to Middle East conflict.
items.quote: There has been a little delay in overall receiving of the material, like I said earlier as well, when I was speaking with Shweta that I mean this is -- I mean, most -- there has been 10, 15 days, 20 days delay in receiving of the raw material, and that is actually the major impact.

items.statement: Company expects to continue growth trajectory in FY27 with strong performance across businesses.
items.quote: The company is expected to continue its grow th trajectory in FY '27, delivering strong performance across its business.

items.statement: Revenue growth in FY27 expected to be much more than 10-12%.
items.quote: I would probably reckon it will be much more than that.

items.statement: Africa business expected to reach 8-10% EBITDA margin in H2 FY27.
items.quote: I anticipate that in the second half of FY '27, Africa business would have an EBITDA margin of somewhere between 8% and 10%, and we are working towards that.

items.statement: Africa revenue targeted at $115-120 million in FY27 vs ~$80 million in FY26.
items.quote: we should at least target approximately $115 million, $120 million in revenue regardless of what the AGOA status is.

items.statement: Two new planned factories to cost INR80-100 crores, spread over 2 years.
items.quote: The capex should be for both of them put together should be of the order of INR80 crores to INR100 crores. Probably it will get spread over 2 years.

items.statement: BTPL mill capacity can be raised to 100 lakh meters/month with INR50-60 crores additional capex.
items.quote: the mill has currently a capacity of 70 lakh meters a month and can be raised to 100 lakh meters per month with an additional capital expenditure of about INR50 crores to INR60 crores.

items.statement: BTPL expected to turn operating profitable in H2 FY27; merger to conclude Q3 FY27.
items.quote: It is expected to turn in operating profits in the second half of the financial year.

items.statement: BTPL FY27 revenue expected to exceed INR1,000 crores.
items.quote: The revenue for FY27 for that company should be in excess of INR1,000 crores based on the momentum that it is going.

items.statement: Company gave 15% tariff rebate and 3% sharper pricing; rebate gone from mid-Feb, sharper pricing continues in H1.
items.quote: Rebates were to the order of up to 15%, part of it which we clawed back by asking rebates from our supply chain. The sharper pricing was to the extent of 3%, which continues in H1.

items.statement: Endeavor to pass back input cost increases to customers in H2, may only partially succeed.
items.quote: in the second half, our endeavor is to try to push back as much of these price increases back to the customer.

items.statement: Order book described as robust and strong; booking spring '27 orders.
items.quote: we seem to find that our order book is relatively very robust and strong.

items.statement: Two new premium customers added in FY26 will contribute ~5% of revenue in first year.
items.quote: the contribution from these new customers in the first year will be of the order of single-digit percentage of total revenue, maybe more like 5%.

items.statement: Section 301 tariff from July could raise tariffs to ~20% for rest of world; Kenya stays at 10%.
items.quote: Section 301 tariffs from July where tariffs may go up to 20%-odd for rest of the world.

items.statement: Net debt increased INR395 crores due to capex, BTPL investment, and working capital.
items.quote: Net debt has increased by INR395 crores, primarily driven by capex investments for incremental capacity expansion, additional investment s in BTPL and increased working capital on account of volume increase.

items.statement: Acquired entities expected to perform as per plan in FY27.
items.quote: So now going forward in the year FY27, the expectation is that all these acquired entities will perform as per plan in that year.

items.statement: FY27 margin expected to improve by a couple of percentage points Y-o-Y.
items.quote: But otherwise, I feel that there will be a couple of percentage point improvement in margins Y-o-Y on account of the disruptions being behind us.

items.statement: BTPL targeting EBITDA breakeven in H1 FY27 and 6-7% EBITDA in H2 FY27.
items.quote: In FY27, the company is aiming at, at least EBITDA breakeven in H1, and they intend to achieve EBITDA positive in H2. We can expect EBITDA around 6% to 7% in H2.

items.statement: FY28 steady-state India EBITDA margin guided at 13-13.5%.
items.quote: then I think the India EBITDA margin should be of the order of 13%to 13.5%

items.statement: FY28 steady-state Africa EBITDA margin guided at 10-10.5%.
items.quote: whereas the Africa EBITDA margin should be about 10% to 10.5% for that year.

items.statement: Bombay Rayon FY28 EBITDA margin expected near 12%, FY29 near 14%.
items.quote: Bombay Rayon in FY '28 also should be contributing an EBITDA margin of anywhere,I would say in FY '28, perhaps more closer to 12%. But if I, let's say, take an FY '29 view, it should also be of the order of 14%.

items.statement: FY28 revenue mix India:Africa expected 75:25 to 80:20.
items.quote: And the ratio between India and Africa from a revenue standpoint should be about 75%to 25% or anywhere between 80% to 20%.

items.statement: Africa revenue run rate 24-25M in H1, ramping to 32-33M in H2, full year 115-120M.
items.quote: So, I think from a Q1, Q2 standpoint, we should be at a revenue run rate of about 24 million, 25 million. And second part of the year, it will catch up to go to that 115 million to 120 million revenue.

items.statement: Added 12M pieces capacity (7.5M India, 4.5M Africa); total capacity to reach 104M pieces.
items.quote: So, in total, with the new capacities coming on board, our capacity in terms of pieces will reach 104 million, but it comes with a caveat for India you should consider the average realization at the rate of INR500 and in case of Africa, you please take $2.5 average realization per piece.

items.statement: Sharper pricing given for H1 FY27 due to high tariffs; effect to reverse in Q3/Q4.
items.quote: we booked our business at a little sharper pricing because we were booking H1 business when the tariff was insanely high on India, and we wanted to keep the revenue rather than let it go out because at some point when the tariff reverses, we didn't want to see business vaporize from the region.

items.statement: Management sees demand not a challenge except occasional geopolitical blips.
items.quote: I see demand not to be a challenge, except for occasional blips here and there based on geopolitics.

items.statement: Potential Section 301 tariff from July could disrupt business.
items.quote: So come July, there could be a Section 301 tariff, which may get imposed.

items.statement: BTPL depreciation INR50-54 crores and interest INR25 crores.
items.quote: Depreciation is around INR50 crores to INR54 crores and interest on the debt component is around INR25 crores.

items.statement: Industry installations expected at 8 GW in FY27 and 10 GW in FY28, reaching 15 GW by FY30/31
items.quote: Our numbers would be more or less plus/minus you can give some leeway, 8 gigawatt in '27 and maybe 10 gigawatt in '28. I also mentioned that FY '30 or '31, we should be looking at around 15 gigawatts.

items.statement: Run-rate capex of about INR 600 crore per year, plus or minus INR 50 crore
items.quote: We would have a run rate of about INR600-odd plus minus 50 going forward.

items.statement: Order book at 5.9 GW, up from 5 GW opening; EPC share grew from 20% to 28% in H2 FY26, targeting 50% by FY28
items.quote: Order book of 5.9 gigawatt consists of 66% of C&I and PSU segment, which is fast growing. The focus now is on expanding our EPC offering, which has grown from 20% to 28% in H2, which enhances our competitive edge and further help to accelerate order book growth.

items.statement: WTG contribution margin at 24.5%; consolidated EBITDA margin expanded to 18.1%, up 100 bps YoY; management expects WTG margins to not materially go down in FY27
items.quote: WTG margins, I don't think materially can go down.

items.statement: Steel largely pass-through; cost management, supply diversification, Make in India, and volume leverage to mitigate inflation; some contracts have forex pass-through
items.quote: Steel is largely a pass-through other than maybe some PSU contracts. So I'm not really very worried about steel. I mean, like I said, we should have a fair capability of maintaining margins where we were exiting.

items.statement: Power demand growing 5-6% since April; peak demand touched 270+ GW; wind installations crossed 6 GW in FY26, highest since 2017; strong pipeline of STU, PSU, C&I bids
items.quote: For FY '26, has been a defining year for the wind sector with installations crossing 6 gigawatt, its highest since 2017, surpassing the previous peak and clearly underscoring the strong demand revival.

items.statement: S144 order intake near 9 GW; Blue Sky platform (S175, S163) launched for Europe; 4.5 GW manufacturing capacity fully operational; 3 AI-enabled smart blade factories
items.quote: Our S144 order intake has reached close to 9 gigawatts, a strong endorsement o f its advanced technology and customer trust. The Blue Sky platform launched in Spain marks o ur reentry into European and other export markets with S175 and S163 turbines

items.statement: CERC tightening DSM for wind from +/-15% to +/-10%; new projects to bid at fossil fuel levels from April 2026; Suzlon developed scheduling/forecasting model to mitigate
items.quote: the CERC has come now for wind changing it from plus minus 15 to plus minus 10. And for the existing projects as well as the y said that the path is set by 2031, we will reach the fossil fuel level. And in fact, new projects are going to bid it out from 1st of April 2026

items.statement: Net cash balance INR 2,384 crore; net worth INR 9,464 crore; adequate working capital limits tied up; DevCo capital deployed INR 300-350 crore against INR 300 crore threshold
items.value: INR 2,384 crore net cash, INR 9,464 crore net worth
items.quote: We are pleased to report that our balance sheet as of M arch '26, reflects the position of exceptional strength with consolidated net worth of INR9,464 cr ores. Our net cash balance at INR2,384 crores further enhances our financial flexibility and resilience

items.statement: Deferred tax asset recognition of INR 742 crore in FY26; unrecognized deferred tax assets estimated at INR 3,000-3,500 crore; only deferred tax charge (non-cash) for next two years
items.quote: Rough estimates on this are in the ra nge of about INR3,000 crores to INR3,500 crores in terms of unrecognized deferred tax assets

items.statement: Commissioning momentum: 830 MW in Q4, 2,456 MW in FY26; 971 MW erected not commissioned (350 MW ready); 332 MW commissioned in Q4; trend expected to continue in FY27
items.quote: We have achieved ramped up commissioning momentum with 332 megawatts in quarter 4, and this trend is expected to continue in FY '27 pursuant to operational excellence we have done in the last few quarters.

items.statement: Guiding for at least 50% revenue growth over the next 2 years
items.quote: No, we are guiding for at least 50% revenue growth over the next 2 years.

items.statement: Targeting 170-200 new store openings in FY27
items.quote: I think for this year, the target would be anywhere between 170 -200 stores, completely dependent on how we are performing and how the momentum continues.

items.statement: Guiding for 8%-10% same-store sales growth going forward
items.quote: So, we are just doubling down on all the strategies that have previously worked on us and now investing more in technology that can future support this better.

items.statement: Per store capex and inventory cost rising to Rs 2.7-2.8 crores, with capex portion at Rs 1.2-1.3 crores
items.quote: It's about Rs. 2.6 crores and it will increase because of the price increas e. So, it will become around Rs. 2.7 crores-Rs. 2.8 crores now. That includes CAPEX and inventory. So, the CAPEX would be about Rs. 1.2 crores-Rs. 1.3 crores and the rest would be paid inventory

items.statement: Expect to maintain pre-IndAS gross margin at 28%-30% by passing on raw material cost increases
items.quote: So, going forward you can look for us to maintain this gross margin anywhere between 28 %-30%. And like I mentioned earlier all the price increases in raw materials will be passed on to the customer.

items.statement: Plan to pass on 3%-4% yarn price increases to customers via higher MRPs while protecting gross margins
items.quote: Yes, so we have seen some movement in yarn prices and that would have to be transferred to the customer. So, we will maintain our gross margins and prices might go up in the future by 3%-4%.

items.statement: Saw some sales impact in May due to geopolitical tensions but April was strong and June is a key month; overall momentum positive in Tier-2/3 towns
items.quote: So, we have seen a little bit of sale impact in May because of the war but I think overall what we have seen in March , April, I think we can continue the positive momentum, and it will not have a huge impact, especially in Tier-2-3 towns.

items.statement: Product mix shift toward higher-ASP categories (kurtis, men's woven pajamas, casual shirts) drove ASP up ~4%-5%
items.quote: So, that's not a right insight. So, it's all because of product mix. So, what we have seen is products like kurtis, product like men's woven pajamas, product like men's casual shirts, these were the highest growing categories for us.

items.statement: Increased safety stock by Rs 100-150 crores in March due to geopolitical supply chain disruptions; targeting 90-100 days inventory and 45 days creditors
items.quote: And about 100 to 150 is the pre GRC that we did, because we saw a lot of supply chain disruptions. And because we were opening so many newer stores, and we had a good festival coming up in April and wedding season, w e did early GRC and we wanted to have extra safety stock rather than empty shells at our store

items.statement: FY27 expansion funded by internal accruals and cash; debt preferred over equity if additional capital needed
items.quote: Yes. For at least this financial year, we are covered with internal accruals and the cash on the balance sheet.

items.statement: New stores EBITDA positive from month one (breakeven ~Rs 500/sq ft, start at Rs 700-750/sq ft); mature in 3-4 years
items.quote: So, it is EBITDA positive from the first month itself, because the breakeven point is around Rs. 500 per square feet of sale. And they start at about 700 to 750. But to mature and reach old stores level, it takes about three to four years.

items.statement: Old stores FY26 sales per sq ft Rs 1,124; new stores Rs 750; new stores defined as opened after FY24
items.quote: So, our old stores were at Rs. 1,124 per square feet for the whole year. And new stores were at Rs. 750 per square feet. And new stores is any stores that opened after FY '24?

items.statement: Inventory >1 year old <5%; >6 months old <24%; ~76% <6 months old and ~50% <3 months old
items.quote: So, more than 1-year-old inventory is less than 5% and more than 6 months old inventory is less than 24%. So, about 76% of our inventory is less than 6 months old and out of that also about 50% of the inventory is less than 3 months old.

items.statement: No plans for new formats or international expansion until reaching 2,500 V2 stores in India
items.quote: I think we don't want to dilute our focus till we have at least 2 ,500 V2 stores. I think we have built a very strong model. And we want to get to every part of the country because still good fashion and affordable price is not available to most middle class consumers in India.

items.statement: Ash & Coal Handling to continue same growth as last year; order book INR1,500 crores.
items.quote: We'll be continuing the same growth like last financial year in the current year for the Coal & Ash Handling business.

items.statement: Wind business to execute pending order of INR1,500 crores in current financial year.
items.quote: we are confident to execute the balance, whatever the pending order of INR1,500 crores in the current financial year.

items.statement: Ash & Coal Handling order pipeline at INR1,500 crores.
items.quote: With these additions, the ash and coal business now has an order pipeline of nearly INR1,500 crores, providing strong medium-term revenue visibility.

items.statement: Wind order book INR1,860 crores; INR238 crores executed last year.
items.quote: Venwind Refex Power Limited, already having an order of INR1,860 crores, we have executed INR238 crores during the last financial year

items.statement: EBITDA margin to be between 15% to 18% always.
items.quote: And the EBITDA margin anywhere, it will be between the 15% to 18% always.

items.statement: Wind business current EBITDA margin around 8%, expected to maintain.
items.quote: This current EBITDA margin is around 8%. And we'll be having a better margin, I mean, always in this wind business compared to the, our competitor.

items.statement: Diesel cost escalation recoverable 40-60% from customers.
items.quote: All our contract has the escalation clause, but not completely, it will be recoverable. There will be 40% to 60%, depending on the contract to contract, it is recoverable. It is a pass-through.

items.statement: Ash handling business to grow with thermal power capacity additions.
items.quote: Thermal power plant, as per the Government of India, there is new 50 gigawatt of the project is getting added in next 4 to 5 years' time. So thermal power requirement is going up.

items.statement: Focus on service business over trading; quality of profit prioritized.
items.quote: Our concentration is fully on the quality of profit and the quality of margin, then the revenue.

items.statement: Diesel price increase to have partial cost impact despite pass-through.
items.quote: there is certainly, there is an impact of the, will be there in the diesel cost increase because 40% to 60% will be a pass on, and there will be, the rest will be a cost impact.

items.statement: No immediate fundraise planned; sufficient cash and bank limits.
items.quote: Not immediately. Not immediately for the Refex Industries.

items.statement: Wind capacity to reach 2 GW by next year-end.
items.quote: we will reach about 2 gigawatts by next year-end by capacity-wise. Currently, we are just still building the capacity.

items.statement: Demerger expected to complete in 60-75 days.
items.quote: if we put a time line, another 60 to 75 days, this should get completed.

items.statement: Promoter pledge to be largely removed over next 6 months.
items.quote: We expect on various stages over a period of next 6 months, pledge removal will happen.

items.statement: Management projects 43-44% AUM growth for FY27, as communicated to lenders.
items.quote: So basically, for all the lenders, we have projected about 43% to 44% AUM jump for this year.

items.statement: Credit cost expected to fall below 2% this year after high levels in prior two years.
items.quote: I think, last 2 years have been on a high credit cost side. This year, we seriously expect that this number should go down below 2%.

items.statement: Targeting ~80% secured AUM by March 2027, including guarantee-backed loans.
items.quote: We remain firmly on track towards our medium-term objective of becoming a predominantly secured MSME lender, targeting nearly 80% secured AUM by March 2027, including loans backed by guarantee program.

items.statement: Renewable energy loans expected to be ~10% of AUM by March 2027.
items.quote: During the year, we also launched renewable energy loans, which would be a very significant part, I mean, maybe around 10% of the AUM by March '27, enabling MSME solarization and supporting sustainable financing opportunity.

items.statement: Solar loan yield around 22.5%, ~24% including fees; ATS ~4 lakh, 4-year tenure.
items.quote: Yield is around 22.5%. It will be around 24-ish if you include all fees and everything, yes.

items.statement: Disbursements to improve month-on-month; Q2 FY27 should be far better than last year.

items.statement: Inox Green FY27 EBITDA guidance upwards of INR600 crores.
items.quote: With all our investments formally folding into Inox Green's ba lance sheet, along with organic growth, we maintain our FY27 EBITDA guidance to be upwards of INR600 crores.

items.statement: Order book of 3.1 GW, added ~600 MW in FY26, execution visibility over 24 months.
items.quote: Coming to the order book, we continue to have a large and very well -diversified order book of 3.1 GW, I repeat again, 3.1 GW, having added almost 600 MW in this financial year, including orders from customers like Aditya Birla, Gentari / Amplus, Jakson Green, First Energy and Leap Green.

items.statement: Order book mix shifted to 50:50 turnkey/equipment supply, targeting 75% equipment supply.
items.quote: Our order book has changed substantially over the past few years from being largely turnkey to now 50:50 turnkey and equipment supply currently, which we plan to further increase to 75% going forward.

items.statement: Expect annual wind capacity addition of 8-10 GW over next few years.
items.quote: Going forward, we expect to see strong annual wind capacity addition of 8 to 10 GW over the next few years driven by RTC, FDRE and hybrid capacity additions, as we see renewable power generation move structurally from being a source of infirm power to firm power.

items.statement: Group company Inox Clean to add 3+ GW annually; 20-30% wind, providing recurring orders.
items.quote: Our Group Company, Inox Clean Energy plans to add 3 GW plus capacity annually over the next few years. Out of this, about 20% to 30% is expected to be wind.

items.statement: New 4.4-MW turbine on track; approvals and commercial launch within this calendar year.
items.quote: The launch of our new 4.4 -MW turbine is on-track, and we expect to receive all approvals and subsequently commercial launch -- launching the product within this calendar year.

items.statement: EBITDA margin to remain north of 20%, not below; O&M 50% margin business adds bias.
items.quote: So we have said that we have already given the guidance in presentation also that we are looking to go only North of around 20% or higher, not below that.

items.statement: PSU contract payment delays impacted receivables; expect improvement going forward.
items.quote: On the receivable front, there has been some challenges, especially in our PSU contracts, where we have seen payment delays. However, we expect the receivables cycle to see significant improvement going forward, given our s trategic pivot towards equipment supply orders going forward, as well as from an increase in the

items.statement: Demerger of Inox Green evacuation infra approved by NCLT; completion in 1-2 months.
items.quote: So, demerger has already been approved by the NCLT. Now you know the kind of administrative process is going forward. So, demerger has been approved. Now the NCLT has an administrative process that is going on. So broadly in the next 1 -2 months, it will get completed.

items.statement: Inox Green FY27 EBITDA to fully convert to operating cash flow; tax shield up to INR700 crore losses.
items.quote: Out of INR600 crore fees, broadly everything will be converted into the operating cash flow. As such, there will be no depreciation, no finance cost, and we have a tax shield up to INR700 crore of losses.

items.statement: Inox Clean targeting 10 GW IPP, 10 GW solar cell, 10 GW module over next 15 months.
items.quote: The group's strategic foray into renewable IPP power generation and solar cell and module manufacturing under Inox Clean with a three-continent play is a big game changer and expected to create huge value across the group with our 10^3 GW portfolio: basically 10 GW of IPP, 10 GW of solar cell and 10 GW of solar module

items.statement: Inox Green to become largest O&M company in India this year, among largest globally by 2030.
items.quote: Further, Inox Green will be the largest O&M company in India over the course of this year and is well placed to become one of the largest globally by 2030.

items.statement: Inox Green portfolio at 13+ GWp; acquisitions of 6.5 GW operational wind O&M assets to complete soon.
items.quote: Inox Green portfolio stands at 13 + GWp comprising of approximately 10.5 GW of wind assets and the balance being solar assets.

items.statement: Medium-term export contribution target of 20-25% of overall revenues.
items.quote: Export contribution increased significantly, crossing 20% in Q2 FY '26, while the company continues to maintain a medium-term target of 20% to 25% export contribution to overall revenues.

items.statement: Indonesia transfer case orders for Mahindra Scorpio pickup and Tata Yodha on track for FY27 completion.
items.quote: No, it is on track for FY '27.

items.statement: New component programs to add annual revenues near INR100 crores with over 1 million parts annually.
items.quote: In addition, the newly secured component programs are expected to contribute annual revenues nearing INR100 crores with volumes exceeding 1 million parts annually.

items.statement: Expects EV volumes to double by July with new model production start.
items.quote: So next month or definitely by July, this new model will be going into production, and we are expecting almost a doubling of the EV volumes.

items.statement: Expects components segment momentum to sustain in coming quarters.
items.quote: We expect this momentum to sustain in coming quarters as well.

items.statement: Board approved US subsidiary with initial investment of INR3 crores for offices and warehouse.
items.quote: This INR3 crores is just an initial setting up of offices, infrastructure, maybe a small warehouse to keep exhibits and things.

items.statement: Automatic transmission opportunity seen at 80,000-100,000 units per year, with potential upside.
items.quote: The automatic transmission number is extremely conservative. That is about -- the number we put up there is for about 80,000 to 100,000 per year.

items.statement: Potential INR300 crores revenue from 4-wheel drive business, with upside if breakthrough.
items.quote: I think we have called out a potential of around INR300 crores on the 4-wheel drive.

items.statement: EV market extremely competitive with Mahindra and MG Motors as competitors.
items.quote: But I must say that the EV market is extremely competitive. We have to remember that there is Mahindra also in this.

items.statement: Maintains debt-free balance sheet and expects healthy net cash position despite expansion.
items.quote: And even after factoring in future expansion plans and increased working capital requirements associated with growth, the company expects to maintain a healthy net cash position.

items.statement: Board recommended final dividend of INR3.27 per equity share for FY26.
items.quote: The Board of Directors has recommended a final dividend of INR3.27 per equity share of INR5 each for FY '26, subject to shareholders' approval.

items.statement: Transfer Case volumes reached 52,000 units in FY26, up from low 30s in FY25.
items.quote: This year we have accomplished about 50,000, 52,000?

items.statement: Team working to achieve INR 1 billion revenue target as soon as possible, before deadline.
items.quote: We are working very hard to achieve this target as soon as possible before the target deadline, what we have said.

items.statement: Planning to add French fries and chicken to product portfolio; very initial stage, no volumes committed.
items.quote: We are working on learning product, and we are also thinking to add French fries to our market. But it is very initial stage, very initial.

items.statement: Continued strong demand across major business verticals from existing and new international buyers.
items.quote: We continue to witness heavier demand across our major business vertical during the year.

items.statement: Freight and logistics costs rising multi-fold due to Middle East geopolitics; could pressure product pricing if not normalized.
items.quote: If this geopolitical situation does not normalized, sooner it will really give us very bad rate on our product pricing.

items.statement: Input cost inflation driven by weather, livestock transport costs, and farmer pricing power.
items.quote: So climate is there, and the cost of transportation is there. These are the factors which impact directly.

items.statement: Expects room to raise prices when New Zealand and Australia costs rise; higher volumes improve operating cost.
items.quote: So we will be having a room to increase our prices, and also when we have a good pricing in India, so we are able to produce more quantity

items.statement: FY26 standalone EBITDA margin improved to 3.12% from about 2.4% in FY25.
items.quote: The EBITDA margin improved to 3.12% during the FY2526, as compared to approximately 2.4% in FY2425.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin improved to about 4.11% in FY26 from about 3.57% last year.
items.quote: The EBITDA margin improved to approximately 4.11% during the current year as compared to approximately 3.57% of last year.

items.statement: Philippines 25% sales target not achieved; working to expand product varieties and educate market.
items.quote: In the last year, the target we said for the Philippines was not achieved, but we are working very closely with our client base

items.statement: Rice business growing steadily with repeat orders; contribution small but expected to become significant.
items.quote: But we work very closely with all our clients, and we are retaining the clients and, slowly, slowly, but steadily we have a growth of rice exports also.

items.statement: Malaysian authority approval for one subsidiary enabled better capacity utilization at that plant.
items.quote: In this year we have achieved the Malaysian authority’s approval for one of our subsidies.

items.statement: OFS at INR 18 per share done to achieve minimum public shareholding; floor price decided by board per SEBI circular.
items.quote: Basically, it was decided on the basis of current market value price. Floor price, the board decided.

items.statement: FY27 revenue growth guidance of 18-20%, with internal target higher.
items.quote: But our focus of 18% to 20% growth for the whole year , and working on an EBITDA of about 7.5% on average and a PAT between 4% to 4.5%, that will be the kind of guidance with which we will continue to look at the future.

items.statement: FY27 EBITDA margin guidance of 7.5-7.8%.
items.quote: While we have reported EBITDA at 13.7% for the quarter and 11.5% for the whole year, we are still giving the guidance of 7.5% to 7.8% for the future.

items.statement: FY27 PAT margin guidance of 4.0-4.5%.
items.quote: And we remain very optimistic and confident about our target of a minimum 20% growth, 7.5% EBITDA and 4.5% PAT.

items.statement: Plan to open 18-20 stores in FY27, focused on franchisees.
items.quote: 18 to 20 stores is what we would like to open.

items.statement: Customs duty hike gain expected at 6-7% of inventory value, realized in Q1-Q2 FY27.
items.quote: So, this inventory will get sold in quarter 1 and quarter 2, but effectively it should be in the range of at least 6% to 7% , but we don't know what is going to happen in future.

items.statement: Sustainable ROE/ROCE target north of 16-17% excluding inventory gains.
items.quote: So, north of 16%, 17% is a good target.

items.statement: April 2026 sales grew 40-50% YoY, but May saw slowdown due to PM appeal and Adhik Maas.
items.quote: I must tell all of you that in the month of April, we saw very strong and rob ust growth compared to last year’s April, of close to 40% to 50%.

items.statement: Old gold exchange expected to remain 50-55% of business, with minimal margin impact.
items.quote: I think that old gold exchange is a minimum 50% of the overall business to move ahead from that , what we are seeing should be something that should be a benchmark , and we should work towards getting it.

items.statement: Risk of customs duty reduction in future could reverse gains; hedging via MCX challenging due to high margins.
items.quote: So, thank you for raising this question. You can ask me one -to-one. We are cognizant of that. But I don't think that it will be possible to cover the entire hedging position through MCX because now the MCX margin has increased to almost 25% - 26%, which is becoming a challenge.

items.statement: Inventory days target of 160-180 days, down from current 188 days.
items.quote: But yes, we will explore all possible options to ensure that inventory days are in the range of 165 days to 180 days.

items.statement: Marketing expenses to be maintained at 1.8-2.2% of revenue.
items.quote: No, I think that the marketing expense is 1.8% to 2.2%, we will continue at that kind of thing that we will invest for the future.

items.statement: GML declined due to cash flow mismatch; intent to increase to 50%+ as borrowing cost is 3-3.5%.
items.quote: But obviously, we intend to increase the GML portion to 50% plus.

items.statement: Free cash flow guidance not provided; remains negative due to inventory and gold price rise.
items.quote: No, I'm not able to give a comment on this. So, we have debated a lot on this, and the numbers are there. So, to me, it does not seem to be easy.

items.statement: EBITDA margin guidance range of 16% to 19% for FY27
items.quote: EBITDA margins always hovers around 16% to 18%, 19%.

items.statement: Inventory days target of 120 to 150 days
items.quote: Anywhere between 120 days to 150 days.

items.statement: Plan to add 200 to 250 stores in FY27 with 500-1,500 sq ft each
items.quote: We are planning to add almost 200 to 250 stores. Having said that, the square feet of the store would be around 500 to 1,500 square feet.

items.statement: FY26 EBITDA margin expanded to 19% from 17.5% in FY25
items.quote: Our EBITDA margins expanded from 17.5% in FY25 to 19% in FY26, and this was on the back of operating leverage and cost efficiency measures.

items.statement: No price increases planned for next 3-6 months; covered on cost side until post-September
items.quote: In the near future of three to six months, we don't see any price increase. With respect to price increase, I mean the price to the consumer. We would not like to change that.

items.statement: Underlying demand for branded footwear and apparel intact; Tier 2/3 shift to organized retail continues
items.quote: The structural shift from unorganized to organized retail in both footwear and apparel continues to work in our favour. Consumer sentiment in our core segments, particularly casual, athleisure and activewear, has remained resilient.

items.statement: Online repeat customer rate 54% to 58% across marketplaces
items.quote: The data we get from the Myntra's and Flipkart's of the world, it is anywhere between 54% to 58% repeat customers in our brand.

items.statement: Gross margin compression due to e-commerce rebate accounting change; no impact on PBT
items.quote: The gross margin, you can see the shrinkage came because of the top-line, and not basically because anything we had done differently this year. Hence, our net result, if you see our PBT and everything, there's no impact on that.
