items.statement: Board recommended final dividend of INR2 per equity share (face value INR2)
items.quote: We are pleased to announce that the Board has recommended a final INR2 per equity share on the face value of INR2.

items.statement: Channel mix: 70% offline retail, 30% online (marketplace model via Flipkart, Myntra)
items.quote: Our retail stores, which we term as the offline business, it contributes almost 70%, close to 70%, and 30% of the turnover comes from our online business, which is e-commerce and quick commerce put together.

items.statement: Other income INR133 crores in FY26, primarily e-commerce rebates and discounts (INR88 crores)
items.quote: Basically, the other income, if you can see, the basic component of that is the discount, rebate and discount, which you get from the e-commerce platforms. So, that's just basically the INR88 crores around is that.

items.statement: Anticipates margins to remain healthy in coming quarters.
items.quote: So we have been working hard to increase the profitability year-on-year, and we anticipate margins to remain healthy in the quarters to come.

items.statement: Working on detailed capacity expansion plan for Taloja; capex budget clarity in subsequent quarters.
items.quote: Having said that, we are working on a detailed plan in terms of what is the capacity expansion plan for the next 2 years. Maybe in the subsequent quarters, there will be more clarity that will be emerged in terms of the capex budget plan in the Taloja facility.

items.statement: Capex plans for India to be drawn up in next 2-3 quarters; Sharjah has spare capacity.
items.quote: And like Aslesh bhai explained to some of the gentlemen earlier, we will shortly be drawing up our capex plans in the next 2 to 3 quarters, and we shall let you all know about that.

items.statement: Board approved broad investment for South Africa; no investment planned yet, details to follow.
items.quote: We have just taken a broad approval from the Board for investment of the amount that we discussed. And we will soon get back to you with the detailed action plan in terms of our South Africa business.

items.statement: Passed on price rises to customers; pass-through contracts for 35-40% of customers, rest spot pricing.
items.quote: And we have passed through contracts with about 35%, 40% of our customers. And for the rest also, we have been revising our prices to to pass on all these price rises.

items.statement: Base oil prices rose 20-25% vs crude 10%; index-linked buying and sales provide pass-through.
items.quote: I mean, although the crude oil prices must have increased, say, by, say, 10%, but the base oil prices have increased by, say, 20%, 25%.

items.statement: Expects historical double-digit volume growth to continue.
items.quote: Volume-wise also, we have historically had volume growth in the range of 10% also every year. So we expect the volume growth also to be there.

items.statement: PHPO segment expected to grow at around 4% CAGR over next 4-5 years; remains company forte.
items.quote: We concentrate on the PHPO part of our business, where the growth is around 4% CAGR for the next 4, 5 years, and that remains our forte, and we expect to stay in that.

items.statement: Segmental mix: PHPO ~50%, lubricants 27%, PIO 10.19%.
items.quote: Our segmental mix remains well diversified with PHPO contributing approximately 50%, lubricants 27% and PIO 10.19%.

items.statement: Strait of Hormuz disruption impacted Texol plant; situation normalizing in last 15 days.
items.quote: But having said that, since last 15 days, the situation has normalized a little bit.

items.statement: Around 20-22% of raw material from Middle East; diversifying to Korean and domestic suppliers.
items.quote: So currently, around 20%, 22% of the total raw material is primarily coming from the Middle East suppliers. And obviously, we have tweaked our strategy. We've been focusing on buying more raw material from our Korean suppliers.

items.statement: Open to inorganic growth opportunities if something works out.
items.quote: Yes, we're open to inorganic growth opportunities. If something works out, we are open to it.

items.statement: FY27 consolidated revenue growth target of 23% YoY excluding new acquisitions with 5% EBITDA margin
items.quote: We aim for consolidated revenue growth of 23% year-on-year, excluding any new acquisitions with 5% EBITDA margins.

items.statement: EBITDA to operating cash flow conversion ratio target of at least 50% for FY27
items.quote: We aim to deliver EBITDA to operating cash flow conversion ratio to be at least 50% to ensure sustainable growth path for future.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 EBITDA margin at 4.5%, up 85 bps YoY; FY27 guidance at 5% EBITDA margin
items.quote: Our EBITDA margin was at 4.5%, that is 85 basis points plus year-on-year with EBITDA at INR86 crores, growing by 76%.

items.statement: Gross margin expanded 110 bps to 10.9% in Q4 FY26 driven by scale and commercial role
items.quote: Gross margin expanded by 110 basis points to 10.9% during the quarter, with gross profit growing by 59% year-on-year to INR207 crores.

items.statement: GLP-1 sales at INR10-12 crores per month (~5% of industry value) with disproportionate share due to cold chain
items.quote: So GLP-1, as we said, at the end of the day, see, we are doing approximately INR10 crores to INR12 crores of GLP sales per month, okay, which is approximately, I would say, let's say, 5% of all GLP value -- GLP overall industry value.

items.statement: MedTech segment contributes >15% of revenue, targeting 20% in 2-3 years with higher margins due to commercial role
items.quote: So on revenue side, the MedTech contribution now given all the acquisition that we have done and now everything we have consolidated in our revenues, it will be more than 15%.

items.statement: Depreciation increased due to IVD segment reagent rental model placing machines at customer sites
items.quote: Specifically, I would say, in the IVD segment of MedTech, where we are providing machines on reagent rental model, where we are putting our machines in the lab against a 5-year revenue contract with them, that -- those machines we are depreciating, right.

items.statement: Minority interest abnormally high at 38% of PAT in Q4 due to preponed sales in one subsidiary; expected to normalize to 25-27% in FY27
items.quote: So what we can say for next year, you can take around 25% to 27% of PAT before minority interest to be contribution from minority interest. This quarter, the minority interest was almost 38% of our PAT. That will be reduced by 10% to 12% in the next year.

items.statement: Finance cost expected to remain stable near-term then decline as IPO funds deployed and acquisition debt repaid
items.quote: So we expect finance cost to remain relatively stable and then come down in future. So because in the earlier years, we had the IPO funds, which were also parked pending investment into acquisitions, which has happened in the last year.

items.statement: Tax rate expected at 22-23% for FY27
items.quote: So we expect it to be in the range of about 22% - 23% for FY '27.

items.statement: Calendarization of FY26 acquisitions contributes ~11% to FY27 23% growth guidance; organic growth ~12%
items.quote: Calendarization impact is around 11%, and the rest is organic in our 22% guidance.

items.statement: Organic like-for-like growth ~15% but revenue recognition lower due to net margin accounting and exiting low-ROIC businesses
items.quote: Like-to-like growth is actually around 15%, which is again coming back to 1.5x of industry growth rate, but revenue recognized is lower in our financials, because of the accounting treatment.

items.statement: Acquisition valuations at 5-7x EV/EBITDA; promoters retained with skin in the game via partial stake
items.quote: The same that we have always said before, which is 5 to 7x of enterprise value to EBITDA.

items.statement: Largely insulated from Middle East crisis as minimal direct imports; work with local subsidiaries of global partners
items.quote: Largely, we are insulated. To be honest, like if you look at the last quarter, the conflict started in end of February, our numbers for the quarter was good. Next year also, we are forecasting good numbers.

items.statement: Working capital days improved to 59 in Q4 from 64 in Q3; incremental working capital needs minimal as Q4 balance sheet reflects annualized revenue base
items.quote: My quarter 4 already has a working capital investment of almost what, if you annualize INR1,900 crores of revenue -- 7,600 crores revenue worth of working capital is already there in the balance sheet, right?

items.statement: ROCE improved to 18.4% in Q4; targeting >20% in FY27 with further upside from 2-way moat of fragmented supplier and customer base
items.quote: ROCE for this quarter was 1.4%, right? And with the margin expansion to next year by another 0.5% from the current quarter, definitely the ROCE for next year will exceed 20%...

items.statement: FY27 revenue growth guidance of 45-55% with EBITDA margin 16-18% and PAT margin ~11%.
items.quote: We expect revenue growth of approximately 45% to 55% with EBITDA margin expected to remain in the range of 16% to 18% and PAT margins at around 11% to 11%.

items.statement: FY27 consolidated turnover expected between INR1,500-1,750 crore; PAT margin 8.75-10.25%.
items.quote: Yes, this year our consolidated turnover should be between INR1,500 crores to INR1,750 crore. And this PAT will be, yes, yes, PAT will be around same, 8.75% to 10.25%.

items.statement: FY27 targeted order inflow of approximately INR2,000 crore.
items.quote: Our targeted order inflow of financial ‘27 stands of approximately INR2,000 crore, while the current bid pipeline remains robust at INR6,000 crores, providing strong visibility for future growth.

items.statement: Three-year target: top line around INR3,000 crore.
items.quote: Three years down the line, we should be around INR3,000 crores top line.

items.statement: FY27 order book expected to be around INR4,000 crore by year-end.
items.quote: FY ‘27, it should be around INR4,000 crore.

items.statement: FY27 estimated capex of INR250 crore for equipment.
items.quote: Aashni, for this I told you that this year we are expecting – we are estimating a capex of INR250 crores.

items.statement: Current order book in hand is INR3,000 crore, split SRM INR2,112 crore and MIPL INR850+ crore.
items.quote: As of date, we have a INR3,000 crores order book in hand which needs to be executed in coming two years.

items.statement: FY27 bid pipeline of INR6,000 crore; conversion expected 60-70%.
items.quote: It will be more than 60% to 70% from this order book.

items.statement: Slope stabilization projects have better margins than road projects.
items.quote: They are much better than road.

items.statement: MoRTH circulars for bitumen and diesel insulate 80-85% of price escalation.
items.quote: In a kind of, MoRTH has issued circulars for bitumen and diesel, so which is insulating us to not 100%, but to something like 80% to 85%.

items.statement: No slowdown seen in projects; government infrastructure commitment unwavering.
items.quote: We don't have seen any - I have heard about slowdown, but I have not seen any slowdown in our projects so far which we are bidding.

items.statement: Order book mix: 51% slope stabilization, ~40% roads, 2% tunnels.
items.quote: If we see the order mix also, so 51% is the total order book consolidated which is from slope stabilization.

items.statement: No HAM projects won to date; bidding but unsuccessful.
items.quote: Unfortunately, we are not able to get any HAM project till date. Of course, we are bidding for those, but till date we are not able to get it.

items.statement: No QIP or equity fundraise planned for next three months.
items.quote: As of for next quarter -- next three months is no plan.

items.statement: FY27 India multi-channel growth will be much superior to FY26 due to RocketBees, Qwik, and offline initiatives
items.quote: So, FY27, we continue to believe that because of our initiatives that we will have a better growth overall for FY27 than compared to the entire FY26.

items.statement: India multi-channel EBITDA expected to grow double-digit in FY27 as manufacturing margin loss recovers by Q2 and operating leverage kicks in
items.quote: Yes, you will have it, Percy, it should. Effectively, we are saying the EBITDA, I would say the drop that we have seen because of manufacturing should be recovered fully by Q2.

items.statement: Plan to open roughly 100 company-owned and franchise stores in FY27 after pausing in FY26 for capital efficiency
items.quote: So, we will double down on our approach to open company-owned stores in FY27 and hopefully with a mix of COCO as well as FOFO stores, we should be opening roughly 100 stores in this year.

items.statement: India multi-channel GMV crossed $1 billion for the first time in FY26, growing 11% year-on-year
items.quote: for the first time, we crossed $1 billion in GMV for the India multi-channel

items.statement: India multi-channel gross margin pressure of 140 bps from diapering competition continued in Q4; manufacturing margin loss from rupee depreciation and crude-linked raw materials is transitory and will recover by Q2 FY27
items.quote: The good news would be that these are very transitional in nature. These will be passed on to the customers and the impact of the incremental gross margin loss apart from the Q3 will be regained back in quarter two as they are being passed to the customer in a regular BAU.

items.statement: Home brand mix and fashion share increasing to drive gross margin expansion in India multi-channel and international
items.quote: The levers, some of the levers, not all, but some of the levers that I want to highlight here for gross margin expansion are increase in the home brand share of top line and within home brands, also the fashion business share, 9 fashion share to the business

items.statement: International business faces moderation in consumer sentiment and import complexities due to Middle East situation, but focus remains on sustainable growth and loss reduction
items.quote: However, it has been a little bit of a moderation in consumer sentiment. I'm not going to say anything else about that, but, yes, there has been and there is some import complexities also is happening as we speak.

items.statement: 6-12 years age segment remains fastest growing part of India multi-channel business with strong long-term cohort retention
items.quote: So, we are seeing a positive traction and we continue to see a positive traction in 6 to 12 that remains the fastest growing part of our business when it comes to age group of children.

items.statement: Diapering category (15% of business) facing irrational competitive intensity from quick commerce and horizontal players for 4-6 quarters, pressuring gross margins by 140 bps
items.quote: We believe that its probably a 4-6 quarters sort of a phenomena. It'll go away. So, that's on the 140 bps that we are talking about, that we spoke in Q3, that has continued for this quarter.

items.statement: RocketBees expanded to 62 cities covering 40%+ of online delivery volumes by end Q4 FY26, ahead of 45-50% mid-year target
items.quote: Now by end of Q4, we have moved up to 62 cities and overall percentage of our online delivery volumes, we're able to deliver 40% plus by end of Q4 through our RocketBees initiative.

items.statement: Qwik quick commerce expanded to 5 cities, delivering 20%+ of online orders in covered catchments; target 10% of total B2C shipments by end FY27
items.quote: We expect over the full year of FY27, our Qwik deliveries over entire B2C shipments should cross roughly around 10% of our overall online business.

items.statement: GlobalBees core categories grew 28% YoY in FY26 with Rs 91.9 crore adjusted EBITDA (4.9% margin); brand rationalization to complete by Q1 FY27
items.quote: We did a revenue of 1876.8 Crores, which was a 28% year-on-year growth and a 91.9 Crore adjusted EBITDA post-corporate expenses, which translates to a 4.9% of revenue.

items.statement: Preschool business revenue grew 11% in FY26 with EBITDA margin improving 220 bps to 27%; store count more than doubled to 208+ in 2 years
items.quote: A healthy growth in revenue, 11% growth in revenue in FY26 over FY25 and around 220 bps improvement in the EBITDA from 24% in FY25 to 27% in FY26.

items.statement: Consolidated free cash flow positive for full year FY26; cash profit up 49% to Rs 312 crore
items.quote: Cash Profit for the entire year on a consol basis has roughly reached around 312 Crores, which is a 49% increase over the last fiscal year. Obviously, happy to report that we continue to PAT and cash flow positive in India multi-channel business and also on a free cash flow positive on a consol basis.

items.statement: RocketBees and Qwik logistics cost front-loading of 40-60 bps for few quarters until network matures, then costs normalize
items.quote: So, till then, you have to front-load, so, we will have some impact of 40 to 60 bps from few quarters, but in a medium term as the network matures, our cost will normalize to a regular sort of a cost structure that we had.

items.statement: Targeting 20-25% revenue growth for FY27, with exponential growth in FY28-FY29 once Filmistan and Thane contribute fully.
items.quote: So, cumulatively, if you see FY27, we may do 20%-25%. But once this Filmistan and Thane contribute for full year, then will have exponential growth in FY28, FY29.

items.statement: EBITDA margin expected to stabilize around 27-28%.
items.quote: EBITDA margin is expected to stabilize around 27-28%. PAT margin is expected to stabilize at around 18-19%.

items.statement: Targeting around 25% EBITDA margin.
items.quote: We are targeting around 25% margin.

items.statement: Pipeline of about Rs. 12,000 crores spread over next 5-6 years.
items.quote: So, projects are in pipeline. We have a pipeline of about Rs. 12,000 crores spread over the next 5-6 years.

items.statement: Filmistan project expected GDV of Rs. 3500 crores.
items.quote: Based on current estimates and subject to final approvals and design configurations, expected GDV of the project is Rs. 3500 crores.

items.statement: Filmistan project estimated cumulative bottom-line contribution of Rs. 1000-1200 crores over next 3-5 years.
items.quote: Estimated cumulative bottom-line contribution over next 3-5 years Rs. 1000-1200 crores.

items.statement: Signed MOU for cluster redevelopment of 9 societies at Ashok Nagar, Kandivali East with GDV projected of Rs. 1100 crores.
items.quote: Additionally, I am delighted to share that last evening we signed an MOU for securing the rights for cluster redevelopment of 9 societies at Ashok Nagar in Kandivali East having an estimated RERA carpet area of 3.25 lakh square feet with a GDV projected of Rs. 1100 crores.

items.statement: Filmistan project under approval, targeting launch by financial year-end.
items.quote: The project is under approval currently and we are looking at launching it by this year-end, financial year-end.

items.statement: Pre-sales in May consistent but slightly slow due to war, fuel prices, and global economic situation.
items.quote: Consistent only. They are a little slow because of the war impact and the fuel prices impact and the global economical situation.

items.statement: Q4 historically shows better sales than Q1 in real estate.
items.quote: And Q4 and Q1, historically Q4s are always showing better sales than the Q1 in real estate.

items.statement: One-time exceptional accounting impact of Rs. 182.17 crores from write-off of tenancy rights.
items.quote: As a result of this structuring exercise, the tenancy rights recorded in Filmistan Pvt. Ltd. have been written-off, adjusted, resulting in one-time exceptional accounting impact of Rs. 182.17 crores in the consolidated financial statements for the period.

items.statement: Filmistan project cost will reduce going forward due to one-off cost considered this year.
items.quote: So, whatever we have considered in this year as a cost, it will reduce the project cost for the Filmistan project going forward.

items.statement: Thane and Filmistan projects and two cluster redevelopment projects will make growth exponential.
items.quote: Yes, Thane and Filmistan projects and other two cluster redevelopment projects will make the growth exponential.

items.statement: 200 KLPD grain-based distillery to commission by June 2026, adding 60 million liters annual ethanol capacity.
items.quote: we are progressing well on our 200 KLPD grain-based distillery, expected to commission by June 2026, adding approximately 60 million liters of annual ethanol capacity.

items.statement: Commissioning trials for grain-based distillery to start next month.
items.quote: we are going to be doing our commissioning trials next month for the grain-based facility.

items.statement: Bio-based chemicals to show stronger results starting this quarter due to debottlenecking and improved competitiveness.
items.period: this financial year, this quarter onwards
items.quote: we are now finding that market penetration to take place in this financial year beginning with this quarter onwards.

items.statement: TNBC out-licensing expected in 2-3 years; CDSCO application next quarter.
items.quote: we hope for a timeframe of 2 to 3 years.

items.statement: DME pilot plant research to take another 3-6 months before further clarity.
items.quote: The process of research on the pilot plant should take a process of another 3 to 6 months.

items.statement: Ethanol net realizations: B-heavy molasses ~60+, juice ~65+, maize ~72.
items.quote: the net realization from B-molasses, I think, it is about 60-plus. At juice to ethanol, it is about 65-plus and for maize to ethanol it is around 72.

items.statement: Government draft standards for E85 and E100 to create greater ethanol demand in future.
items.quote: they have also notified draft standards of E85 and E100 and beyond E20. So, you are looking at a larger ethanol blend as we go forward and that would create a greater demand in the future.

items.statement: Bio-based chemicals demand uptick expected this financial year as fossil-bio price gap narrows.
items.quote: we are definitely seeing an uptick in demand this financial year.

items.statement: Specialty chemicals share of bio-based chemical revenue rose to 61% in FY26 from 58%.
items.quote: The bio-based chemical segment performance improved with an increase in percentage of specialty chemical to 61% compared to 58% Y-o-Y against total revenue from bio-based chemicals.

items.statement: Ethyl acetate production will be ramped when margins are attractive, alongside specialty chemicals strategy.
items.quote: if there is an opportunity to do ethyl acetate business if margins are there, we will do that.

items.statement: West Asia crisis caused raw material supply issues and higher freight costs, affecting chemicals segment.
items.quote: The West Asia crisis has also created some supply issues for some of our raw materials and has also increased freight costs.

items.statement: Margin pressure from higher sugarcane prices without corresponding sugar MSP or ethanol price increases.
items.quote: the government had announced a increased price of sugarcane for the last crushing season and did not increase the MSP of sugar and neither did they increase the price of the ethanol blend. So that created margin pressure in the business.

items.statement: FY26 ethanol sales ~98 million liters; EBP remains main outlet for ethanol growth.
items.quote: we have sold approximately 98 million liters of ethanol, equivalent across the ethanol blending program, ENA, and other grades.

items.statement: Highest ever cane crushing of 2.5 million tons in 2025-2026 season.
items.quote: During the 2025-2026 crushing season, we achieved our highest ever cane crushing of 2.5 million tons.

items.statement: FY27 revenue growth guided at 20% to 22% and EBITDA margin around 11%
items.quote: So, we believe that full year we will do 20% to 22% growth, which is good and we are confident that the execution cycle will remain.

items.statement: FY27 new order intake guided at INR10,000 crores to INR11,000 crores
items.quote: This year guidance is INR10,000 crores to INR11,000 crores for new orders to come in, which we are confident that within domestic, international, and all our four business verticals, we will achieve that.

items.statement: Unexecuted order book including L1 at INR16,361 crores, providing over two years revenue visibility
items.quote: More importantly, we ended the year with an unexecuted order book including L1 of approximately INR16,361 crores from a level of INR14,551 crores last year.

items.statement: Board approved additional INR203 crores capex for construction equipment and productivity; Phase 1 capex to complete by H1 FY27
items.quote: Our Board has approved additional capex of INR203 crores in our Board meeting on 26 May 2026, that is yesterday, towards looking at improving our construction productivity, construction equipment.

items.statement: Tower capacity to reach 1,96,000 MTPA and conductor capacity to double by Q2/Q3 FY27
items.quote: By end of H1 this year, we will finish both Phase 1 of capex which was announced in IPO in May '25. This would further lead to increase in tower capacity to 1,96,000 metric tons and conductor capacity will double.

items.statement: FY26 EBITDA margin 11.92% within guided 11.5%-12%; FY27 guided at ~11% due to geopolitical and supply chain risks
items.quote: Keeping due prudence and caution, we have given a guidance around 11% and if things stabilize and situation changes, we see an upside going forward.

items.statement: ~30-35% of orders have price variation clauses allowing cost pass-through; guidance factors in commodity inflation
items.quote: So around 30% to 35% of our customers are with price variation, which means that we can pass through these price increases.

items.statement: Domestic bid pipeline INR80,000-1,00,000 crores; international pipeline ~INR50,000 crores; demand strong but supply chain disrupted
items.quote: The bidding pipeline has actually not diminished and we are very happy at least the India bidding pipeline as per government announcement is very good. We're looking at INR80,000 crores to INR1,00,000 crores of new opportunity potential where we can participate.

items.statement: Geopolitical tensions causing supply chain delays, logistics issues, and cost inflation; revenue deferred not lost
items.quote: So, as I've been mentioning on the call, that today the geopolitical situation is delaying things, it is uncertain and our guidance therefore is 20% and if things improve, we will definitely improve it to 22% and more.

items.statement: Dividend of 100% (INR2 per share) recommended for FY26
items.quote: Lastly, our Board of Directors recommended a dividend of 100% on equity share capital . That is INR2 per equity share for the financial ended 31st March 2026.

items.statement: Net debt reduced to INR274 crores (INR181 crores ex-IPO); working capital days improved to 81 from 91; operating cash flow INR817 crores
items.quote: Net debt reduced by INR80 crores, that is 30% reduction year -on-year. Our finance cost to operating revenue ratio has improved by 55 bps during the year.

items.statement: ROCE at 25.79% for FY26, consistently over 24% for three years; target to maintain ~11% EBITDA margin steady state
items.quote: Our capital efficiency metrics also remain healthy. Return on capital employed or ROCE has remained consistently over 24% over the last three years and for the year, it is an impressive 25.79%.

items.statement: Power T&D ~90% of revenue; domestic ~50%, international ~50%; Bangladesh ~3-4% of order book, Africa ~20% of global order book
items.quote: Oh, it is around 90% is Power T&D and the rest 10% is our other businesses?

items.statement: CWIP of INR65 crores for tower expansion to 1,96,000 MTPA and conductor expansion to 49,500 km; to capitalize by Q2 FY27
items.quote: So basically, this CWIP is pending for capitalization of 1,72,000 to 1,96,000 capacity expansion in tower, and similarly the part of execution at site is taking place for the conductor expansion, which is from 24,000 kilometres to 49,500 kilometres.

items.statement: Labour availability a challenge due to infrastructure boom; managing with training and loyalty programs
items.quote: So, this question is a demand -supply question. With the infrastructure boom in India and the number of jobs and the government expenditure planned, obviously labour is in X amount available and therefore you have to have the loyal incentive programs for such labour to make sure that they stick with you.

items.statement: Maintains FY27 revenue growth guidance of 8-12% if conditions normal, may moderate to 4-8%.
items.quote: That is still the situation if things return back to normal. But in current situation, it is going to be a speculation to say what we will land in. So we have to wait and watch. Certainly, we will have a positive growth that will happen this year. 8% to 12% can become probably 4% to 8%, but these are all speculation.

items.statement: Targets revenues of INR3,500-4,000 crores by FY30, exceeding earlier target.
items.quote: we remain confident of achieving revenues of around INR3,500 crores to INR4,000 crores by FY ‘30, exceeding our earlier target.

items.statement: Targets EBITDA margin improvement in FY27, will not decline from 10.8%.
items.quote: On profitability, we continue to target EBITDA margin improvement during FY ‘27, supported by our continued focus on localization, operating efficiencies, value-accelerated product mix, and disciplined cost management initiatives.

items.statement: FY27 capex planned at INR130-140 crores, more towards INR130 crores.
items.quote: Yes, we confirm that amount, more on the INR130 crores than INR140 crores, but we will be in that range. As of now, everything is confirmed.

items.statement: Commodity cost pass-through to customers typically takes about 3 months.
items.quote: So usually, as majority of our agreements with customer foresee an adjustment over a period of 3 months. Then there are of course some exceptions here and there, but you can take 3 months as a most common and average timing for that.

items.statement: Four-wheel drive tractor market expected to reach 40-45% of total in 3-5 years.
items.quote: And we expect that another three year to five year, it should be almost 40% to 45% of the market.

items.statement: Domestic tractor industry expected to grow mid-teen, but four-wheel drive transition to outpace market.
items.quote: Now, the expectation from industry is the single digit, somewhere in mid-teen where will be a growth, that too when the industry has peaked this year to around 1.2 million tractors.

items.statement: West Asia geopolitical situation may impact production and supply in H1 FY27, possibly H2.
items.quote: Any sustained rise in energy prices or supply chain volatility could lead to some production and supply-related impact, especially in H1 FY ‘27 and potentially extend to H2 if the situation persists longer than anticipated.

items.statement: TBH business on track to reach INR30 million revenue by FY29.
items.quote: So that is happening in the subsequent year and maybe by ‘29 we will have that INR30 million revenue from the TBH business. So that is in track at the moment.

items.statement: Secured bull gears nomination worth INR150 million annually starting FY28.
items.quote: During the year, we secured a business nomination for a major OEM for bull gears, valued at approximately INR150 million annually starting FY ‘28.

items.statement: Signed engineering services agreement worth INR175 million with Montra Electric for electric transmissions.
items.quote: During the year, we signed an engineering services agreement worth approximately INR175 million with Montra Electric for the industrialization and supply of electric transmissions for tractors.

items.statement: Raw material localization at 78% in FY26, targeting 86-88% in 2-3 years.
items.quote: Raw material localization stood at approximately 78% during FY ‘26 and we remain on track to increase this to nearly 86% to 88% over the next two to three years.

items.statement: Turkey higher horsepower transmission program SOP expected in FY27, Indian customer by FY28.
items.quote: We expect SOP, Start of Production, for the Turkey program during FY ‘27, while the Indian customer program is expected to enter production by FY ‘28.

items.statement: Board recommended final dividend of INR6.75 per share for FY26, 30% payout.
items.quote: On the dividend front, the Board of Directors has recommended a final dividend of INR6.75 per equity share for FY ‘26, resulting in a payout ratio of approximately 30%, subject to shareholder approval.

items.statement: Expects 20% growth in brokerage and client base, and 20-25% growth in algo trading and delta hedging income.
items.quote: We expect around 20% growth in brokerage and the cliental and around 20% to 25% growth in the algo trading and delta hedging income.

items.statement: Full year revenue around INR40 crores for FY27.
items.quote: March 27, it is a full year around INR40 crores.

items.statement: Invested approximately INR5.40 crores in computer software and technology enhancement during FY26.
items.quote: During FY26, we continue to strengthen our technology and operational infrastructure through investment of approximately INR5.40 crores towards computer software system and technology enhancement initiative.

items.statement: Cumulative technology infrastructure investment over last two years is INR7.5-10 crores.
items.quote: It is around INR7.5 crores to INR9 crores. I don't know exact figure, but it's more than INR7.5 crores. It is between INR7.5 to INR10 crores.

items.statement: Plans to reduce cash market investment by another INR50 crores, capping at INR50 crores.
items.quote: And nowadays we have reduced also the investment in shares to the extent of INR50 crores and we planning to reduce investment in shares of another INR50 crores. Means we will invest in stock market, means in a cash market not more than INR50 crores from this year.

items.statement: SME exposure reduced to 30% of last year, around INR20-25 crores.
items.quote: Compared to last year, it is 30% only.

items.statement: Unrealized profit of INR4.33 crores from SLBM transactions expected to realize in coming quarters.
items.quote: Additionally, unrealized profit of INR4.33 crores from SLBM transactions has not been recognized in financial statements and is expected to realize in the coming quarters.

items.statement: Booked loss of INR18-20 crores from old cash market investments.
items.quote: There are basically what the investment made in cash market one and half year before from that shares we booked the loss to the around of INR18 crores to INR20 crores.

items.statement: Started commodity arbitrage, gross profit around INR12 crores.
items.quote: We have made the arbitrage means profit in commodity markets stood around INR12 crores gross profit in commodity market in arbitrage.

items.statement: Onboarded Kotak Mutual Fund, Bank of India, RBL Bank, and 8-10 FPIs; expects to empanel with SBI, LIC.
items.quote: We have just onboarded the Kotak Mutual Fund, Bank of India, and RBL Bank and the few FPI around 8 to 10 FPIs we have started. And from this year, we have also started our research division and so we expect to empanel with the SBI, LIC and big institution.

items.statement: Started ETF market making with Kotak Mutual Fund; plans to add 2-3 more mutual funds.
items.quote: We are also started market making of ETF with Kotak Mutual Fund and we plan to start with another two or three mutual funds.

items.statement: Plans 8-12 franchise branches per year, cautious due to compliance risks.
items.quote: That branch expansion we expect not much, but every year about 8 to 10 branch, branch or franchises say. It is not exactly branch, it's a franchisee. 10 to 12 branch every year minimum we want to start because in a branch expansion, there is a very risky proposal because nowadays there is a compliance is a much more ha

items.statement: Active client base around 12,500; added 2,500 in H2; ARPU INR5,000-6,000.
items.quote: So current active base is -- currently active base is around 12,500 clients, plus 2,500 clients is added in this half year.

items.statement: Recent SEBI derivatives circular has short-term volume impact but good for long-term market fundamentals.
items.quote: From the recent circular, we think there is a short-term impact on our volume, but we think it is good for the overall market condition in long term because the retail traders who lost their money in short term trading, they save the money and they invest.

items.statement: Barwasni expansion capex nearly complete; INR76 crores spent, INR8-10 crores additional expected.
items.quote: Till date we have done around INR76 crores and additional will be around INR8 crores to INR10 crores.

items.statement: Barwasni plant capacity being increased 30-40%, operational by end of FY27 (Q3-Q4).
items.quote: Yes, so the capacities we are almost increasing by 30% to 40% in that plant. And there are some compliances, some licenses which are in pipeline. The construction phase is almost over.

items.statement: Raw material requirements for Q1 FY27 largely secured; Q2 FY27 may see procurement and input cost impact.
items.quote: While our raw material requirements for Q1 FY27 are largely secured, prolonged volatility may affect procurement cycles and input costs during Q2 FY27 as well.

items.statement: El Nino may impact Q2 FY27 demand in South India, but cotton acreage increase and biologicals/nutrients portfolio should counter.
items.quote: Yes, the impact may be seen in Q2 in South of India, because of this El Nino.

items.statement: Exports may see some impact in Q1 FY27, gradually stabilizing with Q2 FY27 expected better.
items.quote: In some countries, yes, the things will be favorable, but overall, I feel that, Q1 may have a little impact of on the export side. Gradually stabilizing, Q2 will be better in terms of overseas business.

items.statement: Specialty products launched in last 3 years contributed ~16% of FY26 revenue; 3 new specialty products planned for FY27.
items.quote: Yes, so Ankit, see last you can say that last 3 years new products which have been specialty products in FY26 they contributed to around 16% of the total revenue.

items.statement: Working capital cycle in industry is 200-220 days; incremental debt for growth to be managed via internal accruals, bank debt, and creditor support.
items.quote: See, considering the industry -- see we have the working capital cycle of around 200 to 220 days in our industry. This is the industry working cycle.

items.statement: Expects to execute 70-75% of current order book in FY27, implying ~INR 2,000 crore revenue.
items.quote: We hope to continue and achieve maybe 70%, 70%, 75% of this order book in the current year.

items.statement: Targets 40-45% revenue growth in FY27, lower than FY26's 200-250%.
items.quote: We expect to grow by around 40%-45% this year as well.

items.statement: Overall margins expected between 8-11% depending on raw material prices and war situation.
items.quote: So we would say somewhere between 8% to 11% is where we should lie in terms of overall margins.

items.statement: BESS PBT margins expected at 14-15%, better than solar.
items.quote: So BESS typically has better margin profile compared to solar. So I would say somewhere between 14% to 15% is what we should expect.

items.statement: 1.2 GW solar cell line commercial operation targeted by June 2027.
items.quote: The commercial operation is targeted by June 2027.

items.statement: BESS manufacturing facility capex was INR 55-60 crore, already spent and under trial.
items.quote: Sir, capex is close to about INR55 crores to INR60 crores.

items.statement: Current order book ~INR 2,800 crore: INR 1,674 crore solar EPC, INR 1,136 crore BESS.
items.quote: So in terms of guidance, my order book currently stands at about INR2800 crores.

items.statement: Targets 60:40 BESS to solar EPC revenue mix.
items.quote: We are targeting a 60-40 BESS to solar EPC revenue mix, which will allow us to participate meaningfully in the country's rapidly expanding storage ecosystem, while building a more diversified and resilient revenue base.

items.statement: BESS revenue expected INR 800-1,000 crore in FY27 vs zero last year.
items.quote: So in the current year, my last year my BESS revenue was zero. It should go to about, maybe close to about INR800 crores to INR1,000 crores this year.

items.statement: Solar EPC revenue expected to remain flat at ~INR 2,000 crore in FY27.
items.quote: My EPC revenue was close to about INR1,250 crores this year. It should remain fairly constant at around that level, so maybe INR2,000 crores.

items.statement: Copper up 40%, aluminum up 50%, steel up; raw material headwinds may impact margins.
items.quote: To give you an example, copper compared to October 2025, copper is maybe up by about 40%. Aluminum is up by about 50%. There's been an increase in the steel prices.

items.statement: ALMM cell shortage expected in short run (6-12 months), may delay some projects.
items.quote: In the short run I think maybe 6 to 12 months, we could face a shortage of solar cells.

items.statement: PPA cancellations by PSUs/DISCOMs due to connectivity and BESS scaling issues; resolution expected by FY28.
items.quote: Yes, that is a very, that is correct. And that is a problem that people are facing that PPAs are not getting signed after they become the L1 bidders in those bids.

items.statement: No plans to expand module or cell capacity beyond current lines.
items.quote: So at present, we don't have any intentions of increasing the capacity in our module line or cell line.

items.statement: EBITDA margin guidance maintained at 22% to 23% range for coming quarters
items.quote: I still want to reiterate that the EBITDA range would still remain in the 22% to 23% range.

items.statement: R&D spend guidance of INR5 billion over nine quarters FY26, FY27 and Q1 FY28 remains high confidence and on track
items.quote: We had mentioned previously that for the nine quarters FY26, FY 27, and Q1 of FY 28, our ta rgeted expected R&D spend is INR5 billion, INR500 crores. That remains high confidence; we are on track to achieve the R&D spend guidance for this nine -quarter cycle

items.statement: Capex guidance of close to INR300 crores across various sites for next couple of years
items.quote: One is that for the next couple of year, we are projecting a capex of a close to INR300 crores across various sites.

items.statement: Pithampur facility ramp-up expected to reach decent capacity utilization within 12 to 18 months post FDA inspection
items.quote: So, we will go as per our plan because, from a quality and standpoint also we want to ramp it up carefully. So, as soon as we get approval done, we have tech-transferred enough products for them to start manufacturing those products and reach a decent capacity utilization within 12 to 18 months.

items.statement: 24 products under FDA review signaling robust pipeline for growth into next year
items.quote: The current number stands at 24 products which are under FDA review, which again signals a very robust pipeline for growth as we move into the next year.

items.statement: Gross margins slightly declined due to increased reliance on outsourced manufacturing to meet higher than anticipated demand
items.quote: So, in light of that, you know, we have seen a slightly slight decline in gross margins, which is because of our own manufacturing, internal manufacturing constraint and we had an increased reliance on the outsourced manufacturing.

items.statement: Expect greater reliance on outsourced manufacturing for at least a couple more quarters until Pithampur comes online
items.period: at least a couple of more quarters
items.quote: So, we do expect a greater reliance on outsourced manufacturing for at least a couple of more quarters. And we hope, and you know, I will give an update also on the Pithampur facility and it coming online, but as of now, at least we feel the sustained demand and increased demand we will have to cater to it through outsourced manufacturing.

items.statement: Demand has been very broad-based across portfolio including established products and new launches
items.quote: Yes, so Harsh, demand has been very broad-based, and I don't think there is a single product or two products. We have seen business across products which have been in the market for a few years, and we have seen product demand for even products we have launched.

items.statement: Specialty portfolio contributed around 33% of gross profit for the quarter
items.quote: If we look at the specialty portfolio, it contributed this quarter around 33 % of the gross profit for the quarter.

items.statement: EBITDA guidance of 22-23% factors in ESOP expenses, Arinna-related expenses, Pithampur-related expenses, and raw material logistics cost escalation from geopolitical turmoil
items.quote: Yes, Tushar, you're right.

items.statement: Arinna acquisition partly funded through debt and partly through IPO proceeds; maintaining war chest for further inorganic opportunities
items.quote: So, also as I mentioned, partly we have this Ar inna acquisition partly we funded through debt, partly through this IPO proceed. At the same time, we're also keeping a also keeping a war chest for any interesting inorganic opportunity as we had stated in our RHP strategy document

items.statement: Board recommended dividend of 150% (INR1.5 per share) amounting to 10% payout ratio
items.quote: In line with what we have done even as an unlisted company, the board has recommended a dividend of 150%, which amounts to INR1.5 per share. This amounts to a 10.0% payout ratio.

items.statement: Board approved ESOP pool creation subject to shareholders' approval; P&L impact factored into EBITDA guidance
items.quote: the board has approved a proposal to create an ESOP pool, which obviously is subject to shareholders' approval. So, this definitely allows us as we go towards the next growth stage of the company, to attract and also retain great talent within the company. Also, just to factor in, the P&L impact of this has been factored in the EBITDA guidance.

items.statement: Arinna Lifesciences acquired at enterprise value of INR200 crores for 85% stake to build CNS platform in India
items.quote: In terms of deal contours, this was an enterprise value of INR200 crores on a cash and debt-free basis. We acquired an 85% stake in the company.

items.statement: R&D productivity improved to 5.9x for FY26 over FY23 period
items.quote: And for the most recent three-year slot, which is FY26 over FY 23, our revenue increase or the incremental revenue was 13.46 billion as against R&D spend of nine quarters of 2.26 billion. So, that is a 5.9 x multiple on that R&D spend.

items.statement: Net working capital days of 126 days is the expected range going forward
items.quote: So, Tushar, I would say that this is the kind of range you can you can assume.

items.statement: Aims to scale manufacturing contribution to 50% of turnover in next two to three years.
items.quote: Currently, 23% of our revenue comes from the manufacturing capabilities, but in the next two to three years, we want to scale the manufacturing contribution to turnover to 50%, with overall increase in turnover also.

items.statement: Plans to increase total capacity to 18,000 metric tons in phases over next 12-18 months.
items.quote: Basically, we are looking at total capacity of 18,000 metric tons including all the current capacity and this we are going to increase in the phased manner in the next 18 months.

items.statement: Expects polymer additives margins at 40%, higher than current manufacturing margins of 30%.
items.quote: Currently, in terms of the manufacturing margins, we are standing at 30% approximately, whereas from polymer additives, we feel that the margins would be 40%.

items.statement: Current order book is Rs. 55 crores, with Rs. 42 crores from government and rest private.
items.quote: Currently, order book is around about Rs. 55 crore and it depends upon the customer.

items.statement: Sees strong demand for polymer additives due to geopolitical sourcing issues, with trials ongoing with five customers.
items.quote: It is just because of this geopolitical scenario, a lot of manufacturers are queuing up or asking us to deliver the product so that they can test and start sourcing it from us in a big way.

items.statement: Raw material price increases impacted margins, with prices rising from January onwards.
items.quote: It is because of the increase in the prices of raw materials. And as I have said prices have increased specifically, from January onwards, the prices of raw material have increased.

items.statement: Aims to maintain growth momentum seen in last five years for next two years.
items.quote: I think we are going to maintain the momentum which we have maintained in last five years.

items.statement: Polymer additives plant to be fully operational in 3-6 months, contributing to FY27.
items.quote: So, maybe in next three to six months, we will be having full capacity running for this polymer additives plant. And so, this will contribute in the Financial Year ‘27 and the margins are going to increase once this product will be added because this is one of its kind of product and unique product in India.

items.statement: No discounts planned for halogen-free flame retardants; focus on quality and trust.
items.quote: And again, we don’t need to offer discounts, we need to give the quality, we need to compete with the foreign suppliers and we need to build, we need to win the trust of our buyers.

items.statement: Capex to be funded via bank credit lines and IPO proceeds.
items.quote: We have the credit lines available for CAPEX from the banks also. And we have some part of the IPO proceeds which we have raised for CAPEX. So, we will utilize both for taking our capacity to next level to 18,000 metric tons.

items.statement: Plans to file three patents in next six months for polymer additives.
items.quote: There are three patents which we are going to file in next six months already because of this patent infringement and various related issues which we are trying to check it from our lives. But in next six months, we will try to file three patents.

items.statement: Targets cable & wire and electrical equipment first, then EV batteries for flame retardants.
items.quote: This flame-retardant is being used in various industries, but currently, we are focusing on cable and wire and electrical and electronics equipment. Once we cater to these two segments, then we will target EV batteries also.

items.statement: Working capital cycle is 110 days, aiming to reduce for better cash flow.
items.quote: Currently, working capital cycle is of 110 days. We are trying to reduce this working capital cycle because it will improve in cash flow also in the organization.

items.statement: Consolidated revenue growth of 45% to 50% and doubling of operational EBITDA expected in FY27
items.quote: At a consolidated level, we are expecting approximately 45% to 50% top -line revenue growth. More importantly, this growth is highly efficient. We project doubling our operational EBITDA, proving immense operating leverage embedded in our current business model.

items.statement: Aerospace segment revenue growth of 25% to 30% with EBITDA margins maintained at 20% at segment level in FY27
items.quote: First, is to continue to grow aerospace revenues profitably. We have the order book, the capacity and the customer relationships to support this, which should deliver 25% to 30% revenue growth, with EBITDA margins maintained at 20% at the segment level.

items.statement: Consumer segment revenue growth of 125% to 150% and EBITDA break-even by Q4 FY27
items.quote: On consumer, we see a revenue growth of about 125% to 150%. And Q4 FY27 will be the quarter wherein we will hit EBITDA break - even.

items.statement: Consolidated PAT break-even expected by H1 FY28
items.quote: However, as our consumer volumes ramp -up and our aerospace segment continues its strong performance, we fully expect to see consolidated PAT hit break-even by H1 FY28.

items.statement: Planned capex for FY27: INR160 crores for aerospace and INR500 crores for consumer segment
items.value: INR160 crores aerospace, INR500 crores consumer
items.quote: On Capex: In our aerospace segment, we have planned about INR160 crores approx. And in our consumer segment, we have planned about INR500 crores approx for the full year FY27.

items.statement: MoU with Tamil Nadu for INR1,900 crores over 10 years for vertically integrated aerospace ecosystem at Hosur
items.quote: In February 2026, we signed an MoU with the government of Tamil Nadu to invest INR1,900 crores for 10 years for a new vertically integrated aerospace manufacturing ecosystem within a new aerospace and defense park at Hosur, across 250 acres in the SIPCOT Shoolagiri Industrial Park.

items.statement: MoU with Karnataka for INR2,856 crores over 5 years across Belagavi and Hubballi clusters
items.quote: And in March 2026, we signed a second MoU with the government of Karnataka, committing investments of INR2,856 crores over five years across our existing clusters in Belagavi and Hubballi.

items.statement: Aerospace order book stands at USD $889 million
items.quote: As a result, our order book in aerospace stood at robust USD $889 million.

items.statement: Consumer capacity utilization target of 40% to 50% by end of FY27 from current 23%
items.quote: Our primary focus this year will be driving capacity utilization from 23% today to a target of 40% to 50% by the year end.

items.statement: Added 433 new aerospace parts in Q4 FY26, total portfolio now 5,654 SKUs, up 26% year-on-year
items.quote: We added 433 new parts in Q4 alone, taking our total aerospace portfolio to 5,654 SKUs, with a 26% increase in the portfolio since last year.

items.statement: West Asia crisis caused supply constraints and logistics cost increases; inventory built up 4-6 weeks ahead; working capital days rose to 151 from 132
items.quote: We are bringing inventory almost four weeks to six weeks ahead of the time, so that we don't have any p roblem in delivering to our customer commitments in aerospace predominantly. This is mostly on the aerospace

items.statement: Hasbro revised sourcing strategy and will stop placing POs; impact not material as other strategic customers will absorb capacity
items.quote: Hasbro has informed us that it has revised manufacturing and sourcing strategy and told us they will stop raising POS with us. While this decision was unexpected, it will not impact the overall growth of the business.

items.statement: FY27 capex to be funded through borrowings and internal accruals
items.quote: Essentially, for FY27, we will leverage borrowings and also some bit of internal accruals to fund the planned capex.

items.statement: Management is targeting 30% growth but expects 14-15% as more realistic.
items.quote: We are shooting for 30% growth. Now will 30% happen? It's going to be a tough call. So historically, last couple of years, we've done 14%, 15%. I'll put my money more on that than on the 30%.

items.statement: Pipeline is at an all-time high of USD 25 million, up from USD 5 million six months ago.
items.quote: Vikas, the pipeline that we have today is in the region of USD 25 million. It's the highest we have ever had.

items.statement: Offering 25-30% cost reduction to customers for vendor consolidation.
items.quote: So we go to our existing customers and say, okay, we know you have x number of suppliers. Let us consolidate with us, and we'll give you a 25% to 30% price cut or a cost reduction.

items.statement: Outcome-based billing currently about 10% of revenue, pushing to increase.
items.quote: Outcome-based today would be I would say, maybe about 10% only. And the rest is all time and material because historically, that is how this industry has grown and evolved, and that has been the traditional model.

items.statement: Customer decision-making delayed due to AI noise, but pipeline strong; expecting pickup in Q1/Q2 FY27.
items.quote: Now quarter 1, quarter 2 this year, we're really expecting decision-making to pick up. As soon as it does, you will see growth pick up.

items.statement: AI may cause cannibalization in contracts but total spending not affected; margins to improve long-term.
items.quote: You will see cannibalization in contracts. In total spending, you will not see cannibalization because whatever the customer is saving on a particular renewal of a contract, they will spend on some other work.

items.statement: 95-98% of growth to come from existing customers, focusing on top 20 accounts.
items.quote: 95% to 98% is from existing customers, the growth. And that trend will continue, and that is the focus.

items.statement: Headcount growth will not be linear to revenue due to AI and outcome-based delivery.
items.quote: So there will be increase in headcount. It will not be proportionate to revenue growth. That's the expectation because of AI, because of the use of human and agents.

items.statement: Acquisition appetite maximum top line of INR 100 crores, actively looking.
items.quote: So if we buy anything, it will be, I would say the maximum would be a top line of INR 100 crores. That would be the maximum appetite we would have.

items.statement: Hiring Chief Growth Officer for UK/Europe joining end of June.
items.quote: And we have a Chief Growth Officer for U.K. and Europe joining us end of June. That's the big investment that we are seeing in the front end.

items.statement: FY27 capex of INR 300 crores: INR 200 crores for new capacity enhancements and INR 100 crores to complete optic fiber preform expansion
items.quote: I said capacity enhancement is about INR 200 crores. Additionally, the plan of expansion on the optic fiber, optic fiber cable side, which we had announced 2 years ago and which is ongoing, there is a balance of about INR 100 crores to be spent because like I said, the expansion to 8 million kilometers of fiber will get over in July or August, so all that will cost another INR 100 crores, so total

items.statement: FY26 capex spend was INR 240 crores including JV infusion with Sumitomo
items.quote: Overall, we have spent about INR 240 crores last year, including infusion into the JV with Sumitomo.

items.statement: EHV JV with Sumitomo started FY26 with order book of INR 380 crores and turned profitable with INR 21 crores profit on INR 450 crores revenue
items.quote: We started the year with an order book of about INR 380 crores and so I think we have turned around the one corner.

items.statement: Communication cables EBIT margin was ~6% in FY26; expects improvement in FY27 subject to supply chain constraints
items.quote: This year, we ended the year with about, I think EBIT numbers was about 6%. I think we should do better than that.

items.statement: Preform internal production expected to yield 5-10% cost advantage over market once operations stabilize
items.quote: depending on how quickly we are able to stabilize the operations, I think we should be better than market by anywhere between 5% and 10% because the preform seller is also making some money.

items.statement: Electrical cables retail-to-project mix shifted from 80/20 to ~67/33
items.quote: I think in the past our retail to project ratio would have been, 80/20. Now, probably it's around two-thirds, one-third.

items.statement: Solar cables nearing capacity utilization; planning capacity increase
items.quote: Solar cables, which we introduced last year in the fourth quarter, have been very well accepted, and we are nearing capacity utilization at this point in time. We are looking at increasing the capacity going forward.

items.statement: Agricultural applications volume down 15-16% in FY26 due to monsoon impact
items.quote: Agricultural applications was one area where there was an issue. The pre-seasonal monsoon plus continued monsoon both impacted the volumes. It was down by about 15%-16%.

items.statement: Electrical segment had ~14 price increases in FY26; effective price hike ~24-25% across most SKUs
items.quote: We had, during the year, close to 14 price changes, all upwards. And the effective price change at the market was about 24%-25% in most of the SKUs, this is on electrical.

items.statement: Middle East disturbances and INR depreciation increased RM costs and inventory by ~INR 300 crores at FY26 end
items.quote: If you looked at our balance sheet numbers, the inventory is up by about INR 300-odd crores, so part of that investment has gone in there.

items.statement: Supply chain constraints for germanium and fiber raw materials from China/Europe due to defense demand and export restrictions
items.quote: Both have put serious restrictions on exports from their side because they themselves have extremely high demand. And the fact that it can be used for defense purposes is, I guess, worrying most people so to be able to predict which way things will move at this point in time is kind of difficult.

items.statement: No guidance given for FY27 due to volatile geopolitical situation and supply chain uncertainty
items.quote: I actually do not give out any guidance, especially in a situation like today, where you do not know whether the war is ending tomorrow because you keep hearing that today is ending, no but it's not ending. And tomorrow, I have an agreement, no, I don't have an agreement. So, it is a very volatile situation.

items.statement: Preform plant commissioned mid-March; expects 3-4 months to stabilize; benefits from Q3 FY27
items.quote: The preform part of it, like I mentioned, we commissioned it in March. For any plant with this technology to settle down, which takes about 3 to 4 months. I expect that benefit to kick in from the earliest I can talk about the end of quarter 2 or maybe quarter 3.

items.statement: Fiber draw capacity expansion to complete by July; 8 million km capacity available from Q3 FY27
items.quote: The fiber draw capacity, which will get increased will get commissioned towards the end of quarter 2 so any benefit that we would get from that will only be after that, so the second half provided there are no other hiccups on the supply chain part should be much better than last year.

items.statement: Export revenue grew from INR 30 crores to INR 52 crores in FY26; targets 2-3% revenue share in 2 years
items.quote: Earlier '24- '25 export performance was, just around INR 30 crores which went up to INR 52 crores this year. We are looking at much higher numbers for the current fiscal. The team is a completely new and is better prepared, I think we should be able to show a larger revenue share from the export side. Until last year, the revenue share was, let's say, about 0.5% to just under 1%. I see it climbing

items.statement: Central India cement industry to grow at least 7-7.5% this fiscal.
items.quote: I'm sure that this fiscal in central, the industry will grow at least by 7%, 7.5%.

items.statement: Company volume growth to be in line with industry growth in the region.
items.quote: We shall be in line with the industry growth in our region.

items.statement: Next quarter costs to rise by INR100-150 per ton, expected to be passed on.
items.quote: we anticipate that in the near term, the next quarter, our costs would be impacted by anywhere between INR100 to INR 150 a ton, given our fuel mix and other things.

items.statement: Cost impact of INR100-160 per ton expected to be passed on to market.
items.quote: what we are looking at is about anywhere between INR100 to INR160 a ton, which we are confident can be passed on.

items.statement: Setting up Khandwa blending unit with INR130 crore investment, adding 35,000 tons per month capacity.
items.quote: we are setting up, and you might have seen in media, a blending unit in Khandwa. This is expected to give us about 35,000 tons of extra cement from the unit. That is immediate, that project is on right now as we speak. And we are investing around INR120 crores, INR130-odd crores -- you can take about INR130 crores in t

items.statement: Total capex for FY27 around INR100 crores, FY28 around INR120 crores.
items.quote: for the fiscal year '26, '27; it will be around total INR 100 crores. And next year, subsequently, it's really around 120.

items.statement: Premium products share at 52% of trade volumes, up 9% YoY.
items.quote: we have achieved a number of 52%. So 52% of our total trade volumes come from premium products, which is up by 9% on a year-on-year basis.

items.statement: Clinker consumption ratio around 60-61%, targeting reduction of 50-100 bps.
items.quote: our clinker consumption ratio is around 60%, 61% of the cement. And I think we will be able to reduce at least maybe 50 basis point to maybe 100 basis points in cement.

items.statement: Upcoming Uttar Pradesh elections to boost cement demand in Central India.
items.quote: the upcoming elections in Uttar Pradesh is going to provide a lot of impetus to cement demand in Central India.

items.statement: Geopolitical West Asia conflict causing uncertainty in pet coke and fuel prices.
items.quote: The geopolitical developments, particularly the West Asia conflict, is continuing to create uncertainty in global markets and commodity prices, where we already had some impact on pet coke and fuel prices.

items.statement: El Nino and heat wave pose risk to agricultural output, rural demand, and food inflation.
items.quote: The El Nino effect that we are seeing, the heat wave sweeping through the northern part of India and the central part of India, would produce -- would pose a significant risk to agricultural output, rural demand and food inflation.

items.statement: Recommended dividend of INR7 per share for FY26.
items.quote: we did recommend a dividend of INR7 per share in our Board meeting recently concluded.

items.statement: Company is completely debt-free with cash and bank balance of INR4,037 million.
items.quote: We did repay interest free loan of INR 687 million, and the company is now completely debt-free. We have cash and bank balance of INR 4,037 million, and we continue to operate on negative net operating working capital.

items.statement: Company expects moderate growth across segments in FY27 with stable domestic demand but caution on geopolitical impact
items.quote: The company expects moderate growth across segments in the financial year 2026/'27. With stable domestic demand, we remain cautious and continue to closely monitor the potential impact of ongoing geopolitical developments on the broader economy.

items.statement: Domestic demand robust across segments; exports uncertain due to geopolitics; inquiry velocity for data centers picked up since October
items.quote: From a domestic demand perspective, for now, we still see robust demand. We are watching what's happening largely to the economy and everybody else in the country. Commodity prices are increasing, inflation is likely to hit. So we are watching all of that. And that is why that brings us a little bit of caution despite the fact that our demand, inquiries and order book are robust today.

items.statement: Order book building in railways and mining; construction moderate; compressor in down cycle
items.quote: Mining, for the last 2 years, we were not seeing good tenders coming in. The order velocity and the tender velocity was lower. But in the last 6 months, mining has picked up, and so our order book has started building up.

items.statement: Data centers contributed 30-35% of domestic PowerGen revenue in FY26 and ~35% in Q4; non-data center PowerGen also grew high double digits
items.quote: The data center business contribution, so for the full year, the data center business would have contributed between 30% to 35% of our overall power generation domestic revenue, and for the quarter, approximately 35%.

items.statement: Invested over INR1,000 crores in last 5 years on modernization and line output; no major new capex planned, will continue incremental investment
items.quote: In Cummins India Limited, we have invested more than INR1,000 crores. What we have been using it for is continuously modernization of our plants and expanding our line capability, more output from the same line. And that has been happening over the last 5 years

items.statement: Localization content high for data center and CPCB IV+ products; margins not significantly impacted by related party imports
items.quote: The localization content is already very high. We are only importing some of those parts which largely don't have very significant supply chain in India. The most significant components are all localized in India. So that is not a challenge for us. And the content that we put beyond what we buy from related parties as a percentage is also very high. So we do not see these impacting our margins as

items.statement: Pricing largely sustaining across range; commodity inflation passed on with lag; DEF price impact minimal on distribution
items.quote: Pricing is largely sustaining across the range. Of course, in lower ranges, which we call very low cost power products, there always in this market, there has been a lot of price-related competition which continues. Largely pricing has sustained at the levels we have.

items.statement: Geopolitical developments, commodity inflation, supply constraints, labor shortages at suppliers, and potential demand elasticity in lower horsepower segments are key risks
items.quote: We are watching what's happening largely to the economy and everybody else in the country. Commodity prices are increasing, inflation is likely to hit. So we are watching all of that. And that is why that brings us a little bit of caution despite the fact that our demand, inquiries and order book are robust today.

items.statement: Hyperscaler revenue ~INR250 crores in Q4; Colo players driving inquiry velocity; both segments growing
items.quote: Thanks for the question, Mohit, yes there was. So, we had about INR250 crores of value.

items.statement: BESS outlook positive long-term but no local supply chain yet; no contribution visibility yet; customer cohorts not disclosed
items.quote: We do see we are, we have a positive outlook on the BESS business in India. We see it scaling up. We see it becoming part of the overall backup power solution for our customers. As of today, because we do not have very good sales pipeline yet and we are still seeing custom ers evaluate how they want to add a BESS in their overall power solutions, we are not able to share with you what we see as th

items.statement: High horsepower lead time 3-6 months; data center orders placed 6-12 months before site readiness; revenue recognized on installation
items.quote: So the lead time for high horsepower orders, I did answer the data centre lead time earlier, but overall high horsepower portfolio lead time will be between 3 to 6 months.

items.statement: Distribution business growth driven by solutions and services, not pricing; extended warranty schemes for CPCB IV+ assets rolling off warranty
items.quote: led growth is in t he distribution business is very less. In the d istribution business, the growth that we have been building is through the actions we have been taking. So Distribution business is providing more and more solutions to end customers, be it power generation or in railways

items.statement: No product gaps; focus on packing more power into existing products; evaluating opportunities beyond BESS but nothing to share yet
items.quote: We don't see product gaps. What we always endeavo ur to do is pack more power into each of our products. And we continuously work on that. So we didn't have product gaps, we have lots of opportunities to pack in more power into existing products so that they become more value for money for our customers

items.statement: Exports driven by Europe and Asia Pac; Middle East and other markets flat; no change in outlook
items.quote: Exports, we have been seeing markets like Europe and Asia Pac continuing to grow modestly for us. There is nothing specific that has changed. Middle East and other markets actually have not grown as much. So for the last 2 quarters, it has been Europe and Asia Pac, and those are the places where we continue seeing moderate demand.

items.statement: Competition intensity stable in HHP/data center; differentiation via end-to-end solutions, service, predictive maintenance, global knowledge sharing
items.quote: Competition has been there. And as we see that there is growth momentum in the data center and high horsepower range, so there is competition. The intensity has remained the same. Our endeavor is to work with the customers prior to the order coming in , so not just treat a genset sale as onetime asset full but overall provide a solution to the customer during installation commissioning, post insta

items.statement: Private and public CapEx continue to grow with pickup in cement, steel, pharma, data centres, and railways; no slowdown seen currently.
items.quote: We do not see a slowdown in private CapEx yet. We do not see a slowdown in public CapEx yet. And having said that, it is true that there have been major impacts in the last couple of months out of the sharp depreciation of the Rupee and out of the volatility, extreme volatility in commodity prices.

items.statement: Rupee depreciation and commodity price volatility may impact inflation, interest rates, and ordering over next 3-6 months.
items.quote: What impact the strong depreciation of the Rupee will have, the high increases in commodities will have on inflation and consequently on interest rates and consequently on ordering, we are not yet able to foretell. And this is something over the next 3 to 6 months we will be watching very, very carefully.

items.statement: Order backlog increased to INR 450 billion, up 9.3% year-on-year.
items.quote: Order backlog increased to 450 billion compared to 412 billion 12 months ago, yes, on an increase of 9.3%.

items.statement: New orders rose 33% year-on-year to INR 67.3 billion in Q6, driven by Smart Infrastructure and Mobility.
items.quote: New orders moved strongly to INR 67.3 billion, up 33% year-on-year, driven by Smart Infrastructure and Mobility growing double-digit.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin fell 290 bps to 9.7% in Q6 due to higher material costs from commodity prices and FX.
items.quote: EBITDA margin moved from 12.6 to 9.7, down 290 basis points.

items.statement: Material cost as percentage of revenue rose from 69% in Q2 to 74% in Q6; Euro depreciated 18%, silver up 160%, copper up 45%.
items.quote: In quarter 2, the material cost was reported as 69% of revenue. And in quarter 6, the number went up to 74%. When we take a look at the currency, the Euro depreciated by almost 18% versus Q2, from an average 91 INR per Euro to 107 per Euro in Q6.

items.statement: Two price increases announced across DI and SI portfolios; not all stuck, but further increases will continue.
items.quote: There are two price increases that we have already passed on to the customer. Not all of it has stuck, but we continue to try to pass on some parts to the customer.

items.statement: 9,000 HP locomotive project on track: 40 units delivered by March 2026; 80 per year in FY26-27, 100 from FY28-30, 160 from FY30-35.
items.quote: The next 2 years, will require us to deliver 80 locomotives a year, 80 in '26 and '27, and then it will ramp up to 100 from 2028 to '30, before we have to ramp up finally to 160 from 2030 to 2035.

items.statement: Mobility EBIT improved 40 bps to 7.6% in Q6; 6-month EBITDA down to 6.4% due to ethics and business mix.
items.quote: EBIT improved from 7.2% to 7.6%, an increase of 40 basis points. The 6 months EBITDA went down from 8.2% to 6.4% as a result of ethics and also business mix.

items.statement: Data centres one of fastest-growing businesses; order book share estimated at 12-15%; strong hyperscaler ordering and conversion on ground.
items.quote: I think it's in the range of around 12 to 15. As I mentioned earlier, we are not... it depends again. When you look at it in terms of the order book, over there, it would probably be in the range of 12 to 15 or so.

items.statement: MV switchgear and vacuum interrupter plant in Goa nearing completion; DI localization started; Mobility localization ongoing; no specific CapEx guidance given.
items.quote: Our medium voltage and vacuum interrupter plant in Goa is nearing completion, and we should be able to come to commercial production with those expanded capacities already. In DI, there is the first element of some localization that we have started with. In the Mobility, we have continuous localization that is happening.

items.statement: No guidance given for future quarter margins; underlying margins strong but FX and commodity impact unpredictable.
items.quote: We are not giving guidance on the next or the future quarters. For all that we can say, and as going back to Wolfgang's earlier presentation to you, our price, our underlying margins continue to be strong, continue to grow. However, we are unaware and we cannot predict what the impact of foreign exchange and commodity prices will have.

items.statement: Sale of low-voltage motors business on track for completion in June 2026.
items.quote: The sale of the low-voltage motors business is on track for completion in June 2026.

items.statement: West Asia conflict may impact fertilizer demand; commercial buildings mixed; automotive picking up with two-wheelers stronger.
items.quote: We will have to wait and see what the impact of the West Asia crisis is on fertilizers. But chemicals are doing well. Pharma is growing well. Food and beverages is growing well also. Automotive is beginning to pick up. Two-wheelers are doing much better than four-wheelers, but the four-wheelers are also picking up as well.

items.statement: Price increases have a 3-4 month lag effect; two hikes done, will continue but cannot pass full 20% FX and 50-150% copper/silver increases
items.quote: The price increases always have a lag effect. And as I said, these are all short cycle businesses. So, the products that we are supplying today, once we announce a price increase, the impact of that is felt in 3 or 4 months later.

items.statement: One price hike taken prior to March, one post-March; 3-4 month lag before impact kicks in
items.quote: No. One was taken prior to March and one is being taken post-March. But again, as I mentioned, it is a 3 to 4 month time lag before they actually start kicking in.

items.statement: DI business grew 1.5% in quarter, 17% in 6 months; SI volumes up 17.5% in quarter, 23% in 6 months; railways pipeline strong
items.quote: If you see the overall presentation that Wolfgang gave and break that down by the individual segments that we have got over there, our DI business grew at 1.5% roughly, right, in terms of order income. And this is again, short cycle. I do not believe this is a reflection of the private sector CapEx right now. Overall, if you see for the year, for the 6 months, it's growing at 17%.
