items.statement: Private sector CapEx in key segments growing at 8-10% on average
items.quote: So, I would say 8 to 10 on an average percentage growth. And I am talking CapEx in the segments that I spoke about.

items.statement: Data centre wallet share estimated at 10-20% of $100 CapEx; civil work is large part
items.quote: So, my estimation would be in the range of 10 to 20%.

items.statement: Railways pipeline deep and broad: 24,000 km signalling ordered, rest expected by end of next year; large opportunities in electrification and rolling stock
items.quote: 24,000 kms. of signalling has already been done… has already been ordered. We expect the rest to be ordered probably end of next year. But electrification and rolling stock, there are large opportunities that are already in the pipeline, and a good flow that is coming.

items.statement: Examining expansion of mobility factories in Nashik and Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar due to order backlogs and pipeline; will update later
items.quote: So on factory expansions, we are examining the expansion requirements for our mobility factories, both in Nashik as well as in Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar in view of the order backlogs that we currently have, as well as the pipelines that we've seen coming up.

items.statement: Locomotive contract margins blended (delivery + O&M) at similar percentages; absolute margins grow with volume
items.quote: Oh, the margins are blended, the margins are blended. So what you see in the margins coming in for the first 40 locos, for the next 80 the margins in absolute values will be proportionately adjusted, but in percentage values they will be at similar percentages.

items.statement: Government fiscal challenges from oil crisis, rupee depreciation, inflation could impact ordering in 3-6 months; no slowdown seen yet
items.quote: Looking at the future, as I said, I think some of the drivers that the government is going to have to look at is how will the impact of the oil crisis play into the inflationary environment in the country? Will that have an impact on… and the depreciation of the rupee as well? That could give a challenge to the government in balancing the books.

items.statement: Smart Infra 70-75% localized; margin pressure from copper, silver, aluminium commodities not FX; price hikes on short-cycle, negotiation on project orders
items.quote: Yeah, it is largely localized, and I think we are 70 to 75% localized in the smart infra, and we continue to localize the remaining portfolio as well. As Wolfgang mentioned, the real impact in smart infra is not out of foreign exchange. It is primarily out of commodities, which is copper and silver and aluminium, which is used in our factories.

items.statement: India-EU FTA to reduce import costs in some segments; indirect benefit from increased customer production
items.quote: So, yes, import costs for us will go down, particularly in some segments. We are still to evaluate the fine print of the FTA there, but we do believe that import costs in some segments of our business will go down.

items.statement: DI localization not viable without millions volume; only negligible elements like flow meters being localized
items.quote: Look, DI's products are primarily PLCs in terms of the hardware. It's primarily PLCs in terms of the hardware. And PLCs, you need a minimum volume, which runs into millions, to make a factory actually viable.

items.statement: Cash flow lower due to higher inventory (West Asia crisis buffer) and higher receivables/contract assets from revenue growth and mobility milestone billing
items.quote: One is, we increased our inventory levels also based on the West Asia crisis, to safeguard our customers and also be able to continue with manufacturing and supply to our customers. So, this is one reason why our cash is lower than we have seen in the past.

items.statement: Metals/steel slight slowdown in last 1-2 months; unsure if short-term or systemic; cement doing well
items.quote: Some slowdown in metals, in other words, in steel, a little bit. We are not sure whether this is short term or whether this is only for… whether this is more systemic, but there's some slight slowdown in the last 1 or 2 months.

items.statement: 40 locomotives delivered in Jan-Mar quarter; revenue recognized on percentage of completion basis linked to cost inflow
items.quote: No, only delivered Jan to March quarter.

items.statement: Smart Infra split ~30% projects, ~70% short-cycle products; similar to company overall

items.statement: US tariffs and anti-dumping duties severely impacted HPMC exports; business stopped after July.
items.quote: So, that was the one which completely stopped our business. So, this kind of high tariff, most of these importers were not able to sustain.

items.statement: Fermbox contract: they invest Rs.60 crores in equipment, revenue sharing model, expected to improve fermentation utilization.
items.quote: So, the agreement says that Fermbox will be investing a close to amount of Rs. 60 crores in various such equipment which will be placed on oursite, will be owned by them on their books and NBPL is also free to use those products in case they choose by giving them the whatever the charges applicable.

items.statement: Expects FY27 to be stronger than FY26 with growth, but no specific guidance until Q1.
items.quote: we expect to see improved demand visibility across both our businesses to make 2027 a stronger and a more positive year compared to 2026, which is firmly in place.

items.statement: FY27 margins expected to sustain at improved levels.
items.quote: we do expect FY '27 margins to sustain at improved levels.

items.statement: Animal Health on track to build INR500 crores+ business in next 4-5 years.
items.quote: we're still on track with the guidance that we gave you in September to build a INR500 crores plus business in the next 4 to 5 years.

items.statement: FY26 capex INR149 crores for debottlenecking, regulatory upgrades, CDMO capacity.
items.quote: During the year, we have incurred capital expenditure of INR149 crores for debottlenecking, regulatory upgrades, and expanding CDMO capacities.

items.statement: Impairing INR47 crores of multipurpose agrochemical facility, retooling INR250 crores for pharma/animal health.
items.value: INR47 crores impairment; INR250 crores retooling
items.quote: We're impairing INR47 crores and the balance INR250 crores of retooling to build in new lines for our Pharma and Animal Health business.

items.statement: Planned HPAPI manufacturing facility in Pune targeted over FY28.
items.quote: Our next milestone in this journey will be the planned HPAPI manufacturing facility in Pune targeted over FY '28.

items.statement: Pharma order book intact; Q4 lost business expected to return in next few quarters.
items.quote: The Order book is still there. The order book is intact, but for the quarter 4, we have lost the business. But it will come back in the next few quarters, as Manoj said.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 EBITDA margin improved to 20.3% over previous quarter.
items.quote: For the quarter, revenue stood at INR519 crores with EBITDA margins improving to 20.3% over the previous quarter.

items.statement: FY26 EBITDA margin at 12.9%.
items.quote: For FY26, revenue stood at INR1,713 crores with EBITDA margins at 12.9%.

items.statement: Raw material cost pressures from geopolitical developments; customer-supported price pass-through to partially offset.
items.quote: Despite some near-term raw material cost pressures arising from geopolitical developments, particularly the war, which has happened over the last 3 months, we expect customer-supported price pass-through mechanisms to partially offset some of these increases.

items.statement: Solvent prices elevated; pass-through negotiations ongoing with lag effect.
items.quote: So, net-net, we will end up ensuring that there's no significant impact on the bottom line, although for 1 or 2 quarters, especially quarter 1, there could be some marginal impact because by the time the pass-through happens and the negotiations end, there's a lag effect.

items.statement: US FDA warning letter at Bangalore site impacting CDMO growth; resolution expected in next few quarters.
items.quote: We are hoping towards that. I mean that's the whole idea. It's been a year now since the warning letter came about 9 months ago. So, we expect to come out of this in the next few quarters.

items.statement: Full-year FY27 guidance will be given at Q1 FY27 results announcement
items.quote: we'll continue to do that in for FY26 also -- sorry, '27 also in Q1.

items.statement: Million Minds Phase 1 leasing at 60-65% of leasable area, targeting INR 75-77 crore annual rental income
items.quote: we believe that we'll be exceeding that INR72 crores, maybe even towards INR 75 crores or INR 77 crores.

items.statement: Leasing inquiries for Million Minds Phase 1 jumped multifold after May 17 inauguration
items.quote: The number of inquiries of these lease spaces after the inauguration on May 17 has jumped multifold, allowing us to believe that the remaining 35%, 40% of lease spaces should be quickly filled up.

items.statement: FY27 to have 3-4 income streams: lease rentals from Million Minds, Malabar Retreat completion, land monetization, and project sales
items.quote: FY27, as I told in my speeches, would definitely comprise of 3 or 4 very different kinds of incomes for the company.

items.statement: One 91 Thaltej project sale value INR 2,100 crores, cost INR 1,500 crores including land; funded via internal accruals and construction finance
items.quote: One 91 Thaltej has a sale value of INR 2,100 crores and the cost of about -- so include land cost is about INR1,500.

items.statement: Million Minds Phase 2 commercial launch targeted Q2 FY27, residential launch Q3 FY27; Phase 2 construction timeline 3 years
items.quote: Phase 2 is quarter 2. Phase 2 of Million Minds is quarter 2. The residential will be in quarter 3. Actually, the Phase 2 can be even preponed earlier.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 EBITDA margin 80.7%, PAT margin 50%; full year FY26 revenue INR 539 crores, PAT INR 316 crores
items.quote: For Q4 FY 26, the company reported revenues of INR122 crores, registering a sequential growth of 33%. EBITDA stood at INR98 crores with EBITDA margins of about 80.7% and PAT came in at INR 61 crores with PAT margins of about 50%.

items.statement: Malabar Retreat 79% complete, bookings INR 175 crores against INR 450 crores project value; targeting completion and full revenue recognition in FY27
items.quote: Against an overall project value of about INR 450 crores, bookings and sales commitments are there nearly about INR 175 crores, and this has been growing day on day.

items.statement: INR 150 crore LRD loan taken in March FY26 against Million Minds LOIs for construction and acquisition opportunities
items.quote: In the last quarter, the last week of FY 26 that is in March, we have taken about INR 150 crores about loan from -- on based on our leases, which were there LOIs, which were signed.

items.statement: Dividend reduced to 15% (INR 1.5/share) to conserve cash for growth opportunities; Board may restore higher payout if projects progress as planned
items.quote: this time, I think the Board discussed and then came at the 15% because good opportunities are coming up where the cash can be utilized for the growth.

items.statement: Godhavi Township: 411 acres remaining, embedded value expected to exceed INR 14 crore/acre average; monetization ongoing
items.quote: 411 acres, given all that which is happening in that area purely on a value of land itself at the prices at which we have sold can only be increasing beyond that average price of INR14 crores per acre.

items.statement: Estimated free cash flow potential INR 9,950 crores from planned projects at conservative prevailing rates
items.quote: all these numbers, which is coming out in terms of INR 9,950 crores are on a conservative basis.

items.statement: Ahmedabad residential launches up 29% YoY in Q1 2026 (6,745 units); luxury housing fastest-growing segment
items.quote: According to Cushman & Wakefield, residential launches touched about 6,745 units in Q1 2026. This was about 29% higher year-on-year.

items.statement: Land acquisition strategy focused on high-growth corridors; acquired ~7 acres in Q4 FY26; new acquisitions underway in prime locations
items.quote: We have roughly acquired around 7 acres of land during this quarter, last quarter.

items.statement: No revenue recognized from Malabar Retreat yet (completion method accounting); full recognition expected upon FY27 completion
items.quote: Retreat cannot be recognized till the time the entire completion happens. We believe that FY27, the completion will happen and the entire thing would be recognized.

items.statement: Targeting 60 million tons production in FY27 including 1 million ton from Deposit 4 and 0.5 million ton from Deposit 13
items.quote: And in that journey, I think this year we will be targeting 60 million tons, which we hope to achieve.

items.statement: Deposit 4 commercial mining to commence in Q2 FY27 with 1 million ton production this year, ramping to 2 million ton next year and 7 million ton peak capacity
items.quote: We hope to have commercial mining commencing on July, that's in Q2. And this year, I think the guidance would be around 1 million ton out of Deposit 4.

items.statement: Deposit 13 to start in Q2 FY27 with 0.5 million ton this year, 2 million ton next year, targeting 10 million ton initially and 20-21 million ton in 4-5 years
items.quote: Deposit 13, because we are still awaiting some clearances which we hope that we'll be able to commence, start the mine somewhere around in Q2, followed by monsoon. So I don't think that we should be able to, we will be able to do more than 0.5 million ton out of Deposit 13.

items.statement: Tokisud coal mine to hit coal seam by Q2 FY27 with 0.75-1 million ton production this year, peak capacity 2.3 million ton
items.quote: By this month -end or maybe in Q2, we should be able to hit the coal seam and we should be able to now extract coal by Q2. And our guidance for Q2 would be around 0.75 million ton to 1 million ton of coal this year.

items.statement: FY26 capex was INR3,300 crore, targeting INR6,000 crore in FY27 and INR7,000-10,000 crore annually for next 2-3 years to reach 100 million ton capacity
items.quote: This year we expect to capex of around INR6,000 crore s. That is what my own assessment is. And going forward next 2, 3 years it will be in the range of INR7,000 crores to INR10,000 crores every year for the next 2, 3 years.

items.statement: Planning INR2,000-3,000 crore on overseas asset acquisitions in FY27
items.value: INR2,000 crores to INR3,000 crore s
items.quote: But I think overall the capex on acquisition, the back of the envelope calculation is wherever we stand today as of today, we should be spending INR2,000 crores to INR3,000 crore s on acquisition of assets abroad this year.

items.statement: Iron ore standalone EBITDA margin at 42%, targeting 42-43% for FY27 despite range-bound prices
items.quote: So, this will be a range -bound movement around this time also and we expect to have to maintain our EBITDA at around 42 to 43% this year. This is our expectation.

items.statement: Board sanctioned INR3,000 crore for blending yard at Vizag to produce branded iron ore with consistent quality, completion in 2-2.5 years
items.quote: Yes, the board has already sanctioned investment of around INR3,000 crore s for creation of a blending yard. You see, in India no company has ever manufactured or supplied branded iron ore.

items.statement: No demand concerns for 100 million ton production given existing customer expansion plans and low phosphorus ore requirement
items.quote: I don't think demand would be ever a problem for NMDC, especially the quality of ore that we produce, simply because of the phosphorus, the low phosphorus that we have.

items.statement: RINL receivables liquidation expected in 16-18 months at INR100 crore/month, NSL outstanding reduced from INR2,500 crore to INR1,800 crore
items.quote: I guess it should take about a year and a half, max two to liquidate all the entire amount of outstanding. If you see NSL pre -demerger expenses was around INR2,500, it has already been reduced to around INR1,800.

items.statement: Rohne coking coal block (8 million ton peak capacity) to open by end of Q3 FY27, no commercial production this year due to overburden removal
items.quote: open it around late Q3. And this year we don't see, envisage any production out of Rohne because the overburden removal etc etera will have to be carried out once the mine is opened

items.statement: KIOCL pellet plant targeting 3-3.3 million ton production in FY27 and DR-grade pellets (67% Fe) by Q2
items.quote: This year we plan to do around 3 million ton. And we are trying to make again for the first time in India a DR grade pellet. We have already achieved around 66.5 million, sorry 66.5% FE content

items.statement: Slurry pipeline (15 million ton) from Bacheli to Nagarnar and pellet plant at Nagarnar to commission by June/July 2025
items.quote: The 15 million ton slurry pipeline that we are building from Bacheli to Nagarnar and the pellet plant at Nagarnar and the grinding mill at Bacheli, this entire system would get commissioned by this month-end or maybe by around mid-July.

items.statement: Railway doubling completion by December 2025 to increase evacuation capacity from 28-30 to 40 million ton immediately, 50-60 million ton eventually
items.quote: Once it is done and now also you see we are doing on an average more than 20 rakes and on peak around 23, 24, 25, 26 rakes. We have done 30 rakes on an odd day, on a good day. So the capacity of course will increase to around 40 million ton immediately once it is done from the present 28 to 30.

items.statement: Legacy gold mine in Australia curtailed production, focusing on exploration and proving resources for future refinery
items.quote: This year the operations just broke even, but now we have curtailed our production and we are now actually going full hog on exploration and proving of further assets because we have realized that given the gold prices unless you have your own refinery, making it very profitable becomes very difficult there.

items.statement: EC capacity 64.8 million ton, CTO 55.4 million ton, targeting CTO enhancement to 58.8 million ton in FY27
items.quote: Now we have an EC capacity of 64.8, but a CTO of around 55.4. We have asked for an enhancement of CTO in three places to about 3.32, so we'll have a CTO of around 58.8 and which is exactly what we want to do this year.

items.statement: Management is constructively optimistic about FY27 performance and committed to delivering sustainable performance.
items.quote: To conclude, while we are cautious about the near-term environment, we remain constructively optimistic about financial year 2027 performance, and we are committed to delivering a sustainable performance.

items.statement: Company has taken calibrated price increases of 15-18% at consumer level to offset input cost inflation.
items.quote: So roughly around 15% to 18% is the increase . In some categories, it is lesser and some categories, it is more.

items.statement: Cost of goods manufactured expected to increase 15-20% overall including labor and material costs.
items.quote: So we can say around 15% to 20% increase will be there overall on the cost side as on date.

items.statement: Intent to improve overall operating margin beyond FY26's 13.8%, targeting roughly 1% expansion.
items.quote: So we don't expect Q4 will be repeated definitely. But we intend to do better than last year overall operating margin, which is 13.8%. So it should be better, maybe 1% plus.

items.statement: Capex planned at INR 180-200 crores for next year, mix of molds, administrative office, and maintenance.
items.quote: Last year, we incurred around INR130 crores. Next year, we have planned around INR180 crores to INR200 crores.

items.statement: April and May demand better, June to be watched; too early to give firm Q1 outlook.
items.quote: It's too early to say, but April and May were better. May is still going on. And let us see how June goes.

items.statement: Premiumization push: expanding Sparx portfolio from INR 999-1,700 to INR 999-2,800 MRP; focus on women (25%) and kids (5%) categories.
items.quote: Now this time, we have rearranged our portfolio, and we're going to launch more products starting from INR 999 without leaving that base till INR2,800 MRP

items.statement: Men's 70%, women 25%, kids 5% current split; focus on improving women and kids contribution.
items.quote: So, for us, men's contribution is 70%, 25% is women and 5% is kids. So more of our focus will be on women and kids to improve.

items.statement: Cautious on near-term due to geopolitical uncertainty causing inflationary pressure that could affect consumer sentiment.
items.quote: Now going forward, while the momentum exiting FY 26 is encouraging, we must tread with caution due to the uncertain external environment amidst the ongoing geopolitical situation causing inflationary pressure, which could affect consumer sentiment.

items.statement: Volume growth target of 4-5% for next two years, acknowledging EBO expansion impact limited as EBOs are ~10% of business.
items.quote: Next 2 years, I think we have to be cautious. Intent is there, again, around, I think, 4% to 5% definitely, we want to grow our volume.

items.statement: EBO expansion of 100 new stores planned, mostly by December, at INR 30-35 lakhs per store within overall capex.
items.quote: In first half, we will be able to open at least 30%, 40% of the 100. So, by December, most of them should be ready.

items.statement: Ad spend maintained at 4-5% of net sales, shifting focus from TV to digital and performance marketing.
items.quote: So our expenditure is roughly around 4% to 5%, and it varies between brand to brand, whatever the requirement is.

items.statement: Brand revenue mix FY26: Sparx ~40%, Hawaii ~25%, Flite ~35%.
items.quote: So our contribution from Sparx is around 40%; Hawaii is around 25% and Flite is 35%.

items.statement: Network: 420 EBOs, supplying to 70,000 retailers/MBOs, present on e-commerce and quick commerce, exporting to 37 countries.
items.quote: So we have mentioned in our investor report also that we are cur rently supplying to 70,000 retailers/MBO outlets. And EBOs are 420 outlets

items.statement: FY27 revenue growth guidance lowered to 14-15% from earlier 15-20% due to geopolitical conditions
items.quote: we still hope that we can be at the lower or 14%, 15% growth we still hope that we will get.

items.statement: Capex guidance for FY27 includes INR400 crores for defense capacity augmentation to 4 lakh shells, may spill to FY28
items.quote: And other than in our Goodluck Defence and Aerospace, we have a plan to augment our capacity, which has a capital outlay of INR400 crores, but it will be sprawled maybe in this financial year or it may be carried forward to the next financial year also.

items.statement: Adding 40,000-45,000 tons capacity in GI conduit pipes and front fork tubes in FY27, targeting 6 lakh tons total
items.quote: So in the coming financial year, we will be doing almost 40,000 to 45,000 ton capacity addition.

items.statement: Defense EBITDA margin guidance maintained at 30-35% despite FY26 anomaly of 68-70% due to partial year operations
items.quote: In the coming years, what the guidance we have given of 30%, 35%, it will prevail. This is the first year and working for us only for 2, 3 months. That is why you are seeing this dissimilarity in the results.

items.statement: Gross margin improvement to 33% is sustainable, not transitory
items.quote: There is no worry. Gross margin will be sustained. It is a sustainable margin, what we have given.

items.statement: Conduit pipe EBITDA margin 15-20% sustainable, front fork tube 15-16%
items.quote: Conduit pipe is basically for export to USA . It's a highly profitable item with an EBITDA o f around 15%. Ram Aggarwal: And the front fork tube, it will be at the CDW tube and with the EBITDA margin of 15%, 16%, we will continue

items.statement: Solar vertical sales grew 33% in FY26, expect improved utilization with India adding 41-45 GW annually
items.quote: we have improved 33% sales to our solar vertical in this year. India is at 500 gigawatts plus. New capacities are adding every year. W e hope we will improve our utilization in future in this division.

items.statement: Hydraulic tube capacity utilization at 50% in FY26, targeting 65-70% in FY27
items.quote: Basically, what as per our, in the last year, we have come to 50% capacity utilization of the hydraulic tubes. And in this year, we hope th at we will be able to d o it to 65% to 70%.

items.statement: Global artillery shell demand 8-9 million vs 2-3 million supply capacity over next 1-2 years, demand outpacing supply
items.quote: the demand today is 8 million to 9 million shells, whereas the quantity available or quantity to be started in the next 1 or 2 years, it may be 2 million to 3 million.

items.statement: Commodity cost increases passed through with 1-2 quarter lag, using product and market reshuffling to minimize impact
items.quote: However, the other products, yes, there is a price increase of all the consumables, and we are trying to pass it on to the customers, but it is always with a time lag. So it may take 3 months, to 1 quarter to 2 quarters to pass all these increases.

items.statement: West Asia crisis disrupting logistics, may impact exports 5-10%, hoped to resolve in 15-20 days
items.quote: exports because of time duration taken in reaching the consignment, it is taking more ti me. So it may impact some 5%, 10%, but we hope the matter will not be long for 12 months. It may be solved in the next 15, 20 days.

items.statement: No comment on defense IPO plans, matter is on the wheels
items.quote: Basically, on this issue, I will prefer no comments, because it is on the wheels, and we will le t you know when the right time comes.

items.statement: FY27 volume growth guidance: EXIM 8%, domestic 15%, overall 9.5%; conservative due to geopolitical factors, may revise at mid-year review
items.quote: I would like to now give the guidance for this financial year '27. EXIM, I would like to give a guidance of 8%. Domestic, I would like to give guidance of 15%. Overall, will be 9.5%.

items.statement: FY26 capex was INR1,085.20 crores; FY27 capex budget approved at INR945 crores, may increase at mid-year review
items.quote: Capex achieved in last financial year was one of the highest, which is INR1,085.20 crores. And in this financial year, yesterday, Board of Directors have approved a capex budget of INR945 crores.

items.statement: EBITDA margin maintained at 24-25% range; FY26 EBITDA 24.33%, FY25 24.9%; rail freight margin improved from 25.65% to 27.16%
items.quote: All I can tell you is we will maintain the EBITDA level between 24% to 25% as we have been doing till now. In fact, last financial year also, we had an EBITDA of 24.33% in FY26.

items.statement: Bharat Container Shipping Line (BCSL) MOU signed with 30% stake; targeting top 10 global shipping line by 2047 per Amrit Kaal Vision
items.quote: During the financial year, CONCOR signed MOU for Bharat Container Shipping Line, in which we have a 30% stake. We are one of the majority partners of Bharat Container Shipping Line.

items.statement: Will share haulage savings from double-stack upper deck (50% haulage charge) with customers via competitive tariffs to attract road-to-rail shift
items.quote: So we'll be having some savings on 40-feet containers. So we will be coming out with a very competitive tariff that will be light cargo, which is at present moving by road

items.statement: EXIM volumes recovering from May after weak March-April due to West Asia crisis; domestic demand improving with gunny bales and Morbi tiles revival plus bulk cement traction
items.quote: But from the month of May, we are again seeing an upsurge in our volumes, which is a good indication. Container Corporation of So probably the other markets like U.S. and Europe and Far East, they are now contributing a lot

items.statement: Tank container fleet at 500, adding 200/month; Board approved 2,000 more plus earlier 1,000; targeting 1 million tons bulk cement in FY27; food grain container trials successful
items.quote: Yesterday, I'm glad to inform you, Board of Directors further approved the procurement of 2,000 more tank containers, apart from 1,000 tank containers approved earlier.

items.statement: West Asia crisis impacted March-April volumes; gunny bales hit by jute supply disruption from neighboring country; Morbi tiles affected by gas shortage; geopolitical uncertainties persist
items.quote: Domestic actually affected very adversely because of the disturbance in our neighboring country because of that, we could not get the supply of jute. And this Gunny Bales were the major domestic loading commodity in Eastern India.

items.statement: WDFC-JNPT connectivity commissioning by June 1, 2026; double-stack trains to run NCR-JNPT; JNPT rail coefficient target 18-19% in FY27, 30-35% in 3 years
items.quote: DFC connected to -- connectivity to JNPT will be commissioned by 1st June 2026, so we are quite ready. And last week, I had a meeting with top management of DFC Corporation, and they are quite optimistic that this -- from 1st June, they will be able to run double stack trains to JNPT.

items.statement: FY26 handling volume 5.58M TEUs (+9.6% YoY); EXIM 4.21M TEUs (+8%), domestic +14.6%; Q4 originating: EXIM 549,273 TEUs, domestic 129,065 TEUs
items.quote: Despite these challenges, our company, Container Corporation achieved ever highest throughput of 5.58 million TEUs in FY26, which was a growth of 9.6% in which EXIM growth was 8% and domestic growth was 14.6%.

items.statement: Market share: EXIM 53.9% (down from 55.2%), domestic 55.9% (down from 57.6%), overall 54.5% (down from 55.9%); deliberately avoided low-margin business
items.quote: Last year, in EXIM, it was 55.2%. This year, it is 53.9%. Domestic last year was 57.6%. This year, it is 55.9%. Overall, last year, it was 55.9%. This year, it is 54.5%.

items.statement: Dividend: INR1/share interim for Q4, total FY26 dividend INR8.6/share (172% of par value)
items.quote: I'm glad to announce that Board of Directors have approved the dividend of INR1 per share of par value INR5 for -- that is interim dividend for quarter 4. This made the total dividend of INR8.6 per share, which is 172% of the par value of share.

items.statement: Other expenses increased to INR358 crores for FY26 (avg INR70-80 crores/quarter); driven by maintenance, AMCs, DR site, CSR; recurring not one-off
items.quote: So there has been some increase in our maintenance expenses and the AMCs which are payable for our contracts because we have also set up a DR site last year.

items.statement: No further closure or exceptional losses expected from discontinued operations or business exits.
items.quote: The simple answer is no. But even if you break down the exceptional items in this year, one of the big items which is sitting is consequent to the new labour codes, which are announced by the Government of India.

items.statement: OTTplay subscriptions stopped from April 1; residual servicing may cause marginal FY27 losses.
items.quote: If the unit economics of that is not working out, there might be marginal losses, etc., which will basically come into the P&L for FY 2027, but that will be a very small number.

items.statement: Shutting OTTplay contracts will have some cash impact but marginal P&L effect.
items.quote: So those will basically tantamount to cash flow. So, there will be some cash impact to shut down these contracts. But from a P&L perspective, there will be a very marginal impact of some residual subscribers, who purchased their subscriptions in March and might go up until September, but that will be a very small numbe

items.statement: No plans to return cash to shareholders; Board prefers investing in core and digital businesses.
items.quote: Well, there is none so far.

items.statement: AFE assets will be sold at earliest opportunity to maximize value; not long-term holds.
items.quote: The simple answer is yes. We are not holding these assets for the very long term. Of course, it doesn't mean that we will flip the assets within months. But at the earliest opportunity, when we think we can maximize the value for the organization, we will sell these assets.

items.statement: Other income fell INR 50 crore due to mark-to-market losses on treasury; expected to recover.
items.quote: That is what is impacting other income to the extent of INR 50 crore in the full year. Of course, there are various other small reasons, but that's the chunk of the reason which is happening there.

items.statement: Assetvault investment is non-cash AFE; no cash invested, brand AasaanWill.
items.quote: On Assetvault, you are right, the revenue is pretty small at this point in time. But as explained earlier, it's again an AFE investment. It's not a cash investment, it is our AFE investment, and there are certain marketing plans that, that company has for the market of India, where we would like to give our marketing p

items.statement: Radio: surrendered six loss-making frequencies; all remaining frequencies profitable.
items.quote: On Radio, we did an entire portfolio review where all the five loss-making frequencies now and one loss-making frequency earlier totalling to six loss-making frequencies - those are the frequencies that we've surrendered back to the Government of India. All existing frequencies are profitable frequencies and obviously

items.statement: Radio sector under pressure; will keep reviewing closely.
items.quote: Now, however, as I explained in the webinar, Radio as a sector is under a lot of pressure, but we will keep on reviewing this on a very close basis.

items.statement: No specific revenue or earnings guidance provided.
items.quote: As per usual practice, we do not provide specific guidance on revenue or earnings projections.

items.statement: Circulation revenue up 4% overall; realization per copy marginally up; copy share increased.
items.quote: Well, overall circulation revenue is plus 4% between English and Hindi. I would say realization per copy is slightly flat here and there, but there's not a huge amount of variance in circulation revenue.

items.statement: Expect a better year in FY27 barring unforeseen geopolitical events; strong momentum in US scaffolding and stable drum closure demand
items.quote: So barring unforeseen new geopolitical events that can create supply challenges, demand challenges, we expect a better year going ahead.

items.statement: Steel prices increased ~25% over last 3 months but fully passed on; aluminum cost managed via backward integration
items.quote: Steel prices have increased by almost 25% over the last 3 months, but we've been able to pass them on.

items.statement: US scaffolding demand recovered strongly in March quarter and sustained into June quarter driven by AI/tech infrastructure investment
items.quote: We are seeing a strong momentum even going forward into the June quarter across -- and this is mainly driven by investments in AI and tech ecosystem-driven infrastructure, which is leading to increased demand uptake of scaffolding.

items.statement: Scaffolding and formwork revenue split roughly 50-50 in FY26 at ~INR680 cr and ~INR660 cr respectively
items.quote: Yes, it is roughly -- this year, it was roughly 50-50. So INR1,342 crores. I think about INR680 crores or so was scaffolding and about INR660 crores or so was formwork.

items.statement: Minor debottlenecking adding 10-15% scaffolding capacity in FY27; next formwork expansion phase end of FY27/early FY28 costing ~INR150 cr
items.quote: That may be about INR150 crores...

items.statement: Mach One order book exceeds 4.5 lakh sq meters, covering 6+ months of current production capacity
items.quote: Even today, we are sitting on order books in excess of 4.5 lakh square meters, which is more than 6 months actually of our current production capacity.

items.statement: Engineering services revenue growing 8-10% per quarter from INR80 cr base; bottom line growth slower due to AI investment
items.quote: Currently, it is INR80 crores a quarter. So it cannot jump from there to INR120 crores in one quarter or so. But the way it is growing, it is growing at about 8% to 10% every quarter.

items.statement: Tariffs on scaffolding (50%) and drum closures (27.6%) under Section 232 now apply globally; China faces additional 25%, creating level playing field
items.quote: Scaffolding is 50% because we fall under Section 232 and drum closure has now also been added under Section 232, and it's 25% -- 27.6% to be precise.

items.statement: Mach One volumes soft due to slow real estate project execution despite strong order inflows; utilization at 60-70%
items.quote: As far Mach One is concerned, our capacity utilization is quite low. We are operating at about 60% to 70% capacity utilization, mainly because of slow site mobilization.

items.statement: FY26 capex of INR110 cr was maintenance/debottlenecking across divisions, not capacity expansion
items.quote: Those were all normal capex that happens debottlenecking various factors. There are no specific project related across all the divisions, it was there for improvement.

items.statement: Yarn business at ~10% EBITDA margin; Q1 FY27 to improve on better cotton spreads despite high depreciation
items.quote: EBITDA, we are doing about 10% on EBITDA level. And I think it will in the quarter 1 of this financial year, it will improve by on account of the yarn spread being better.

items.statement: Fabric division restructuring under evaluation including possible processing house shutdown; no margin guidance for FY27
items.quote: We are very seriously looking at restructuring the fabric division.

items.statement: Plastic drum closures sold INR35 cr in FY26 with margins better than metal closures; no capacity addition needed
items.quote: We have sold plastic drum closure about INR35 crores in the complete year. Yes. And the margin is, if not better. It is -- actually, it is more than the drum closure margin.

items.statement: Forex gain of INR20 cr in Q4 FY26 (INR46 cr full year); benefit retained as no imports require sharing with customers
items.quote: The forex for the quarter was INR20 crores.

items.statement: Scaffolding utilization at ~90%; formwork extrusion at 100%; Mach One at 60-70% due to site delays
items.quote: Scaffolding we would be operating probably at about 90% and Mach One is variable up and down because our capacity is actually much more, but our actual production and dispatch is lower because it's determined by site conditions.

items.statement: Both top line and bottom line will be positive; results visible from Q1; decent growth expected in FY27.
items.quote: I can say that both top line and bottom line will be positive. The results will be visible from the first quarter itself.

items.statement: Capex requirement going forward largely nominal, INR25-30 crores maintenance capex after FY27 projects.
items.quote: Therefore, our capex requirement going forward remains largely nominal or in the range of INR25- INR30 crores, which we call as a maintenance capex once we complete our projects in the year FY27.

items.statement: Expects small increase in gross and EBITDA margins in FY27, but difficult to quantify.
items.quote: It is difficult to comment at this moment that we'll be able to increase it by how much percentage. But yes, there will be a small increase.

items.statement: Took two price increases in April; first well received, second faced issues, may take another in June.
items.quote: Yes, we have taken two price increases in the month of April, and they were quite successful.

items.statement: Crop activity expected to improve in June as monsoons hit; May sluggish due to heat.
items.quote: The crop activity, though, is expected to improve in the month of June as the monsoons hit the Indian coastline.

items.statement: Premium segment currently 60-63% of B2C; vision to reach 60-70% in next 4 years.
items.quote: At this moment, they are contributing roughly about 60% to 63%. So it's my vision to take it to 60%- 70% in next 4 years.

items.statement: Exports to grow from ~5% to 10% of revenue in next 2-3 years, driven by CDMO.
items.quote: I see it growing up to 10% in next 2 to 3 years.

items.statement: Kaeros expected to double sales in FY27; contribute 5-8% to IIL volume.
items.quote: So, we should be at least doubling these total sales of Kaeros in this fiscal.

items.statement: Prolonged geopolitical tensions may keep raw material prices elevated and impact business.
items.quote: We'll remain mindful that prolonged geopolitical tensions may continue to impact business conditions and keep raw material price elevated for some time.

items.statement: El Nino impact and crop mix change, particularly in dry crops, are risks.
items.quote: We'll also take care of the evolving global supply chain conditions, the El Nino impact, crop mix change, particularly in the dry crops.

items.statement: Target to reduce interest cost by at least 25-30% in FY27.
items.quote: But internally, there is a target that we'll reduce it by at least 25%, 30%.

items.statement: ICS plot program to double to over INR60 crores, expanding to maize and cotton.
items.quote: So last year, we made about more than INR30-odd crores. And this year, we are going to double this number.

items.statement: Copper and fertilizer project to be operational from FY28, with revenue of around Rs 40,000 crore plus in that year.
items.quote: So, it would be downstream products, then the refinery would be operational, secondary product line operation. All will be operational in 2027-28 and we continue to have, based on the pricing, somewhere around 40,000 crores plus revenue in this year as well.

items.statement: Capex plan: Rs 4,500-5,000 crore by March 2027, another Rs 5,000 crore next year, and Rs 2,000-3,000 crore by March 2029.
items.quote: And the capital investment this year, by end of March 2027, will be at least close to Rs.4,500 to Rs.5,000 crores. Again, in the next year, as per the current plan, will be almost equivalent, another Rs.5,000 crores. And then we have another Rs.2,000 to Rs.3,000 crores by March 2029.

items.statement: Standalone dyes business targets 10-15% EBITDA margin, aiming for 12% this year.
items.quote: I think we would target somewhere between 10% to 15%. So, if we are at 12% during this year, we will be happy.

items.statement: Standalone revenue expected to cross Rs 1,000 crore in FY27, with 20% growth.
items.quote: So, the target is to cross Rs.1000 crore. So, we are expecting (+20%) growth this year. So, hopefully, we will cross Rs.1000 crore in this financial year. On a standalone basis.

items.statement: Government incentives: expected Rs 3,000-3,500 crore over 10 years, 30-35% of eligible capex.
items.quote: But we would receive roughly 30, somewhere between 30 to 35% of eligible CAPEX over a period of 10 years, right? And in absolute number, would be in the range of Rs.3,000 crores to Rs.3,500 crores to be received yearly within a period of 10 years from the date of commercial and operation beginning for both the plants.

items.statement: Dyes intermediates outlook improving due to China supply tightening from environmental measures, supporting realizations.
items.quote: The outlook for Dyes Intermediates is becoming more constructive. China's supply of key intermediates has tightened due to environmental compliance measures and production containments, which is expected to support industry dynamics and improve realizations for Indian producers going forward.

items.statement: Fertilizer trading to start from next quarter; copper trading not yet commenced.
items.quote: And the company would start trading fertilizers during this year, this financial year. So, fertilizer distribution would start probably from next quarter onwards within this year as well for the trading part of the company.

items.statement: No dividend declared for this year; board decided to retain cash for growth.
items.quote: But this year, the dividend has not been declared and is not going to be declared. I would be certain and clear for that.

items.statement: Civil construction for copper and fertilizer project 25-30% complete.
items.quote: The civil construction for the entire site, including all the units, would be till now close to 25% to 30%.

items.statement: FY27 standalone revenue expected to increase 10% to 12%
items.quote: Looking ahead, on a standalone basis, we expect FY27 revenue to increase by 10% to 12%.

items.statement: Opening order book for FY27 is about INR7,000 crores after excluding cancelled orders
items.quote: The opening order book for the year is about INR7,000 crores, after excluding 2 orders worth about INR550 crores that were cancelled during the year.

items.statement: New orders of INR1,400 crores booked in first two months of current quarter
items.quote: In the first 2 months of the current quarter, we have booked new orders totaling INR1,400 crores.

items.statement: Manufacturing EBIT margin guided at 12% to 13% for FY27
items.quote: We are reasonably confident that 12% to 13% is going to be maintained.

items.statement: Project business EBIT margin expected to improve to around 5.5% in FY27
items.quote: We should be closer to 5.5% for FY27.

items.statement: FY26 capital expenditure was INR153 crores; additional INR25 crores approved for Muzaffarnagar steel castings plant
items.quote: expenditure during the year is INR153 crores. With this capacity buildup underway, let me now turn to our expectation for FY27

items.statement: Inquiry pipeline and order booking outlook remains strong in domestic and export markets
items.quote: Looking ahead, the inquiry pipeline and order booking outlook remains strong in both domestic and export markets.

items.statement: Input cost increases in steel forgings, castings, chemicals, imported materials, gas shortages raising fuel costs, logistics costs up
items.quote: However, we are seeing increases in several input costs, including steel forgings, castings, chemicals and certain imported materials. Gas shortages have raised fuel costs; however, there has been no disruption to manufacturing operations. Export and import logistics have increased and transit times have also lengthened.

items.statement: Most increased costs expected to be absorbed through normal contingency provisions
items.quote: As of now, most of the increased costs are expected to be absorbed through normal contingency provisions.

items.statement: Major revenue growth in FY27 expected from manufacturing segment (~INR500 crores), project business growth 3-4%
items.quote: So the major increase is going to come from the manufacturing segment. So, we are expecting 10%, about INR500 crores or around that much is going to come from the manufacturing segment. And there will be some growth, maybe 3%, 4% for the project business, as well.

items.statement: Export order book stands at INR1,450 crores as of 31st March 2026
items.quote: Our export order book is also about INR1,450 crores as on 31st March 2026.

items.statement: Export revenue expected to exceed INR1,100-1,200 crores in FY27
items.quote: The export revenue of this INR1,100 crores, INR1,200 crores, I'm sure it's going to be a little more than that during the current year.

items.statement: Geopolitical developments have not affected existing order bookings; currency risk hedged via forward covers and confirmed LCs
items.quote: Current geopolitical developments have not affected existing order bookings. However, we are seeing increases in several input costs, including steel forgings, castings, chemicals and certain imported materials.

items.statement: Isgec Hitachi Zosen FY26 revenue INR672 crores, PBT INR103 crores; FY27 expected slightly better with revenue closer to INR700 crores and profit INR100 crores plus
items.quote: We are expected to do slightly better than this. So we are hoping that revenue could be closer to INR700 crores. And the profit should be in the range of INR100 crores plus.

items.statement: Cavite Biofuels Philippines plant running at 70-75% capacity, expected to reach 85-90%; depreciation expected ~INR150 crores in FY27
items.quote: I think even today, it is running at 70% - 75% capacity, and we are expecting the capacity to be running at close to 85% - 90% for the rest of the year, except for maybe 1 - 1.5 months when the rains are really excessive. These depreciation cost, foreign exchange fluctuation, we really don't know for CBPI as a standalone unit. But depreciation this year was INR170 crores. Next year, we expect it i

items.statement: Net borrowings reduced to INR476 crores from INR836 crores; no working capital borrowings; cash and equivalents INR241 crores as of 31st March 2026
items.quote: The consolidated net borrowing position has improved substantially during the year. Net borrowings as on 31st March 2026 are INR476 crores compared to INR836 crores last year.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 expected to be better than Q4 FY26 with higher prices and output of ~80,000 tons vs normal 65,000-67,000 tons
items.quote: First of all, as I said, Q1 is looking definitely better than Q4 of FY '26. Q1 FY '27 is definitely looking better. Prices have moved up a little bit more, and the higher output comes into play.

items.statement: Q2 FY27 expected to be around same as Q1 as of now
items.quote: As far as Q2 of the quarter is concerned, which is July to September, in another 15, 20 days, we will start getting a flavor of what the price will be like. We expect it to be around the same as Q1 as of now.

items.statement: FY27 capex planned at ~INR450 crores for Kalinganagar, Ethanol and underground mines; FY28 major portion of ~INR700 crores for mines
items.quote: Total amount of INR450 crores planned towards capex. From that , major portion of in vestment will be through our internal accruals. But we still have unutilized term loan of approximately INR170 crores, which we can use.

items.statement: For FY '28, other than the routine capex, primarily the balance portion of the mines will be there, which will be to an extent of approximately INR700-odd crores.
items.quote: For FY '28, other than the routine capex, primarily the balance portion of the mines will be there, which will be to an extent of approximately INR700-odd crores.

items.statement: Targeting 60-40 export-domestic split by late FY27; existing international customers interested in additional tonnage; aiming to allocate ~200,000 tons domestically
items.quote: Our existing long -term customers internationally are interested in additional tonnage, have reached out to us for additional tonnage. So we will be looking to allocate some tonnages there. And we believe domestically, the economy is growing, stainless steel production is growing, per capita consumption is increasing, and there is space in the market for us to make our presence felt.

items.statement: Current domestic prices INR118,000-120,000/ton, export realizations >INR120,000/ton; Q1 FY27 margins higher than Q4 FY26
items.quote: In fact, currently, I would say domestic prices are in the INR118,000 to INR120,000 a ton mark, which is a little bit higher than what we have seen in Q4 of FY '26. Indian Metals & And even export realizations are in excess of INR120,000 a ton

items.statement: Weighted average EBITDA cost reduction of INR3,000-4,000/ton expected when full KNR 1&2 complex operational; steady-state from Q4 FY27
items.quote: When entire KNR complex comprising 1 and 2 is up and running is where we are looking at a weighted average reduction in EBITDA cost by INR3,000 to INR4,000 on account of better logistics.

items.statement: Hybrid renewable energy at grid parity with stable rates for 25-29 years; coal linkage pricing ~INR400-500/ton cheaper from H2 FY27
items.quote: But I would also like to point out that what we are seeing in terms of the fresh coal linkages that we are bidding for, and those benefits will start flowing probably from Q3 of this year that coal sourcing through linkages is also the pricing is going to be about INR400 to INR500 a ton cheaper.

items.statement: Stainless steel demand growing 2-3% globally to 64.157M tons in CY2025; ferrochrome output down 9.4% to ~16M tons supporting prices; India stainless production and demand moving up
items.quote: Stainless steel demand continues to be good, although growth has been about 2% to 3%, but there has been a sharp to 64.157 million tons in the calendar year 2025, globally speaking. But there has been a decline in ferrochrome output globally by about 9.4% to just short of 16 million tons.

items.statement: KNR 2 running at ~6,000 tons/month in Q1 FY27; KNR 1 cold trials from May 30, furnaces switching on ~July 10-15; Ethanol project pre-commissioning July, commissioning Q2 FY27
items.quote: As far as the ongoing first quarter of FY '27 is concerned, all furnaces are running smoothly, and we are getting approximately 6,000 tons a month output, but more on that later.

items.statement: KNR 1 cold trials and pre-commissioning from May 30, switching on furnaces around July 10-15; Ethanol project pre-commissioning in July, commissioning in Q2 FY27
items.quote: We are initiating col d trials and pre -commissioning activities from 30th of May onwards, which will continue through June and slight delay of 10 or 15 days in terms of switching on the furnaces, and that is on account of two things.

items.statement: South African power tariff reduction to $0.62 may increase ferrochrome output but likely offset by reduced Chinese production; net-neutral for chrome units
items.quote: What we broadly believe is that from a chrome units perspective, it will, by and large, be sort of neutral in the sense that if ferrochrome production picks up in South Africa as a result of these -- if $0.62 is finally approved, I believe, first of all, it will come with certain conditions like upside sharing and all sorts of things.

items.statement: Forex hedging policy at 25-30% of net exposure; Q4 saw INR28 crores notional MTM loss on hedges due to rupee depreciation from 89.9 to 93.65; actual loss only INR3 crores
items.quote: Now for the accounting purposes, this difference has to be shown as a provision or what we call as a notional loss in the books, though it may not be the actual loss. Whatever we have booked for next 12 to 18 months, under mark to market accounting, we are showing it as a notional forex loss amount, which you see in the investor deck, I have said about INR28 crores of that is actually the notional

items.statement: Mining capacity target 10 lakh tons in FY27, eventually 12 lakh tons from underground (6+6); ore inventory to normalize from FY27
items.quote: FY '27, the target is for 10 lakh tons. We will be at the 10 lakh ton mark for a couple of years, and then we will gradually take it up to 12 lakh tons. The eventual plan, which is what we are spending that close to INR1,000 crores for is to sustain output at 12 lakh tons per annum and entirely from underground.

items.statement: Hybrid renewable portfolio 135 MW (70 MW JSW from July 2026, 65 MW Enfinity from June 2027); targeting 35-40% renewable energy share by FY28
items.quote: 70 megawatts signed up with JSW Energy, which is expected to flow in July or so of this year. And we had another agreement for 40 megawatts, which we cancelled on mutual discussions with the developer. And instead, we have tied up with Enfinity Global for 65 megawatts of hybrid renewable energy, which will come online June of 2027.

items.statement: KNR 2 partially built 33 MVA furnace (50,000 tons) targeting commissioning ~June 2027 pending environmental clearances
items.quote: So we are just trying to figure out the time lines. But we would hope to target commissioning around June 2027. But that is something we need to get a little bit more clarity about the environmental clearances, etc.

items.statement: No further closure or exceptional losses expected from discontinued operations or business exits.
items.quote: The simple answer is no. But even if you break down the exceptional items in this year, one of the big items which is sitting is consequent to the new labour codes, which are announced by the Government of India.

items.statement: Marginal residual OTTplay losses expected in FY2027 from servicing existing subscriptions.
items.quote: If the unit economics of that is not working out, there might be marginal losses, etc., which will basically come into the P&L for FY 2027, but that will be a very small number.

items.statement: Advertising yields expected to be sustained at current levels or above, though competition may react.
items.quote: Well, to an extent, yes, but I won't do a carte blanche on that because there's an immediate reaction, which always comes from the competition. But our hope & prayer and even the plan that we have set out for ourselves – though we don't give forward guidance – is to keep our deals at a certain level and above not below

items.statement: Radio segment margins under pressure; all remaining frequencies are profitable after surrendering loss-making ones.
items.quote: Now, however, as I explained in the webinar, Radio as a sector is under a lot of pressure, but we will keep on reviewing this on a very close basis. But right now, all the frequencies or all the stations which were not turning in a profit, we've already surrendered those frequencies.

items.statement: Advertising revenue growth driven primarily by yield improvement, not volume.
items.quote: So, the simple answer is, the lever for the growth in revenue is primarily yields, volume s have been by and large flat, which have tracked the industry. So , it's basically pricing.

items.statement: Circulation realization per copy increased marginally; copy share increased in some markets.
items.quote: It has , but marginally because the constraint there will be competition. But you are right our realization per copy has increased.

items.statement: Print advertising revenue grew 10% in Q4 and 8% for full year, led by yield improvement.
items.quote: A bit into the numbers for the quarter, advertising revenue growth of 10% at INR 313 crore, circulation revenue growth of 4% at INR 51 crore, operating revenue at INR 427 crore and operating EBITDA coming at INR 97 crore with a 23% margin.

items.statement: Radio revenue declined due to high base from prior year's event-led revenue and industry-wide issues.
items.quote: The segment revenue declined on account of high events-led revenue which is there sitting in the base. Business continues to be under pressure with subdued margins.

items.statement: OTTplay business discontinued due to challenging space and failure to achieve viable unit economics.
items.quote: However, in spite of our best effort, the space became increasingly challenging, especially since all the big telcos also have a significant presence. Though I must also caveat that we had already segmented our markets not as Tier 1, but Tier 2 and Tier 3 towns, thereby, w e were using a different distribution channel

items.statement: Rising newsprint costs, weak rupee, supply chain disruptions, and geopolitical volatility are near-term concerns.
items.quote: In the near term though, rising newsprint costs, amplified by a weakeni ng rupee and the prevailing global environment of supply chain disruptions, trade policy uncertainty and geopolitical volatility, remains a concern that we are managing with cost discipline.

items.statement: No plans to return cash to shareholders; Board prefers investing in businesses for long-term value.
items.quote: Well, there is none so far.

items.statement: AFE assets will be monetized at earliest opportunity to maximize value; not desperate sellers.
items.quote: The simple answer is yes. We are not holding these assets for the very long term. Of course, it doesn't mean that we will flip the assets within months. But at the earliest opportunity, when we think we can maximize the value for the organization, we will sell these assets.

items.statement: Other income dropped by INR 50 crore due to mark-to-market losses on treasury investments.
items.quote: That is what is impacting other income to the extent of INR 50 crore in the full year. Of course, there are various other small reasons, but that's the chunk of the reason which is happening there.

items.statement: Projects FY27 revenue growth of 10% to 12%, largely volume-led.
items.quote: We project revenue growth of 10% to 12% in financial year '27, largely led by volumes and expect our EBITDA margin to be in the range of 9% to 10%.

items.statement: Plans INR60 crores capex over two years for manufacturing-cum-warehousing at West Bengal Hosiery Park, Kolkata.
items.quote: During FY27, the company will strengthen its in-house capacity by developing manufacturing cum warehousing facilities. And there will be a total outlay of INR60 crores, which will be spent in 2 years' time.

items.statement: Took a 4% to 5% price hike in April; may take another 2% to 3% in June-July.
items.quote: We have taken a price hike of around 4% to 5% in April and we might take another price hike maybe 2%, 3% in June, July, depending on the market condition.

items.statement: FY27 advertisement spend guidance of 6% to 7% of revenue.
items.quote: The advertisement spend for the quarter is around 4%. And the next year guidance would be the advertisement expenses would be in the range of 6% to 7% for FY27.

items.statement: Athleisure grew 20% by volume and 25% by value in Q4, driving gross margin improvement.
items.quote: The main reason is that the athleisure contributes well in this quarter 4, there is a volume growth of 20% in quarter 4 and value growth is 25% for Athleisure.

items.statement: Expects to sustain current gross margin with initial price hike and market acceptability.
items.quote: Yes, with this initial price hike and acceptability in the market, we hope that we will sustain this gross margin.

items.statement: FY27 growth split expected roughly 4-5% each from volume and value.
items.quote: Volume maybe 4%, 5%. Largely it will be a mix of both 4%, 5% each,

items.statement: Faces challenges from higher crude/raw material prices, shipping disruption raising logistics costs, and forex volatility.
items.quote: There is no potential impact on the business, but business is facing some challenges, such as increase in price of crude would lead to the rise in the prices of raw material.

items.statement: Trade discount intensity remains around 12% and will be maintained at same level.
items.quote: We will maintain the same level of discount.

items.statement: Targets 10-12% growth over next couple of years with profitability improving 50 bps annually.
items.quote: So, we target a growth of 10% to 12% for the next couple of years. And with that, every year maybe profitability, should help us increase the profitability by 50 basis points year-on-year.

items.statement: Board proposed dividend of INR3 per equity share for FY26, subject to shareholder approval.
items.quote: In line with this commitment, the Board has proposed subject to shareholders' approval a dividend of INR3 per equity share for financial year '26.

items.statement: Inventory split: raw material 13%, finished goods 54%, work in progress 33%.
items.quote: The split of inventory, the raw material is around 13%. The finished goods is around 54% and work in progress is around 33%.

items.statement: Projecting FY27 EBITDA margin of 13% for full year
items.quote: We are projecting for next year 13% EBITDA.

items.statement: Strong order book secured for next 18 months including large coke oven project
items.quote: I'm happy to report out that we have a strong order book for the next 18 months. We have secured one of the largest coke oven projects with one of the largest industry -- integrated steel players.

items.statement: FY27 capex planned at around INR 150 crores including maintenance and growth capex
items.quote: So, on the capex side, we are looking at INR 150 crores of capex of which, maintenance capex would be around INR 40 crores-50 crores of it.

items.statement: Seeking 1-3% price increases across segments to offset input cost inflation
items.quote: So, let's put it like this that vis-a-vi s our cost increases, we are asking for 1% - 3% of price increases depending on the categories or the segments that we are operating

items.statement: Q4 FY26 adjusted EBITDA margin at 12.1%, full year at 11.9% vs 13.7% in FY25
items.quote: For the full year, adjusted EBITDA stood at INR 477 crores with EBITDA margins of 11.9%, compared to 13.7% in FY '25.

items.statement: Expect improved demand across core end industries in FY27 supporting growth
items.quote: First, improved demand across core end industries; second, progressive implementation of price increases across selected products and customer segments; third, continued cost optimization through recipes, recycling and strategic sourcing programs.

items.statement: Three 4PRO contracts signed in January 2025 to drive high value-added solutions and better realizations
items.quote: We have three 4PRO contracts we signed in Jan only in this year, which will increase later part of the year, the margins also.

items.statement: Goodwill impairment taken on Dalmia assets due to weaker export demand, currency depreciation, capacity additions and inflationary pressures
items.quote: This was driven by a reassessment of medium- to long-term growth expectations, considering a combination of factors, including weaker export demand amid geopolitical uncertainties, persistent currency depreciation impacting raw ma terial costs, increasing industry capacity additions, heightened competition from imports and continued inflationary pressures across key cost categories

items.statement: Restructuring of Dalmia assets complete, no further restructuring required
items.quote: It is complete. No further restructuring is required, and we say this with utmost confidence.

items.statement: Dalmia assets revenue grew 14% to INR 1,153 crores in FY26 with EBITDA margin at 10.8%
items.quote: Revenue was INR 1,153 crores as against INR 1,013 crores of FY '25, so it is a 14% growth in that particular segment and revenue has gone up to 10.8% against 11.5%.

items.statement: FY26 capex of INR 135 crores focused on operational excellence, innovation, capacity, automation and sustainability
items.quote: For FY '26, we have earmarked approximately INR 135 crores of capital expenditure focused on operational excellence, product innovation, selective capacity enhancement, automation and sustainability initiatives.

items.statement: Ended FY26 in net cash position with net debt-to-EBITDA at 0.1x, cash flow from operations up 9% to INR 409 crores
items.quote: As a result, we further strengthened our balance sheet and ended the year in a net cash position, with net debt-to-EBITDA entering to net cash positive at 0.1x.

items.statement: Cement demand softer in Q4 due to seasonal lean period October-January, expected recovery in Q1
items.quote: Q4, there was some cyclic as Azim said, the cement industry is in a lean period from October to December, even January. So that was the reason volume-wise, we were a bit low. But Q1, we should be back with 1,000+ volumes again.

items.statement: High-cost magnesia inventory impacting Feb-March shipments due to energy cost increase in China and freight increases
items.quote: It's offset by high-cost inventory, which is coming up for our basic refractory, primarily fused magnesia and DBM. The high-cost alumina inventory has already been consumed, and we are at a market level pricing. But these magnesia-based pr oducts have gone up because of energy cost increase in China, freight increase, etcetera, which impacted Feb and March shipments

items.statement: Cement revenue share dropped from 13% to 11% due to overcapacity and competition, focusing on de-commoditization
items.quote: Our cement as a percentage of revenue from FY '25 to '26 also dropped because of this over competition. So, in FY '25, we had about 13%. Now it's at about 11%.

items.statement: FY27 volumes expected to double, with capacity utilization reaching 70-75% for billet and TMT.
items.quote: Roughly starting with the next quarter onwards, means it will be almost double, not the it may doubling the capacities will be mostly doubled.

items.statement: EBITDA per ton to remain around INR7,000, with potential improvement from higher volumes.
items.quote: INR7,000 margin. 40,000 to 50,000 tons will be the average. You can double the capacities, I have given the capacities will be doubled. So naturally your profitability and all will be increased.

items.statement: Reheating furnace and refurbishment capex to complete this year, operational by July end, contributing from Q2 FY27.
items.quote: And as far as the expansions which have been done already, they will come into operation by July end.

items.statement: IMR Group investing INR300 crores via share warrants, expected within six months.
items.quote: So, I think it will coming in next six months, we expect this to come in place.

items.statement: Steel demand outlook positive due to infrastructure, housing, and defense spending.
items.quote: Government-led infrastructure development, rising investments in construction and housing, increased spending on railways and defense infrastructure, and continued focus on domestic manufacturing are creating strong long-term demand drivers for the steel industry.

items.statement: Expanding into new markets and segments with new rebar products from reheating furnace.
items.quote: We have started one reheating furnace in our plant, which will enable us to manufacture up to 50,000 tons of new bars.

items.statement: War impact limited to diesel cost; raw materials sourced locally, insulating operations.
items.quote: Actually we are insulated as far as the war part is there. Only for some diesel cost it may have the on the transport, but otherwise we don't have much of impact because our basic raw materials what we procure are all locally only.

items.statement: Debt refinancing to reduce interest cost to around 9%, saving finance costs.
items.quote: Now, we would like to reduce further to the below sub-10% level rate, now around 9%. So, definitely there is going to be some savings on my cost thing, I mean finance cost going forward with this.

items.statement: Empaneled with major projects like Google's AI hub and ArcelorMittal, expecting supply opportunities.
items.quote: Yes, Yes, because basically we are also already empaneled with that the Google partner Adani who is building these things. And most of our supplies will be going from our Simhadri this thing.

items.statement: Planning 1 million ton green steel plant, groundbreaking expected soon.
items.quote: We have entered into an MOUs for making a 1 million ton green steel plant.

items.statement: Debt reduction target to negligible levels using internal accruals and warrant money.
items.quote: It may be from the internal accruals or from the share warrant -- share money. Once we get the money, we take a call on that because we have got some large investment plans also for the plant and -- which will started in phases.

items.statement: Q2 FY27 onwards production and EBITDA to improve significantly with reheating furnace operational.
items.quote: But now we are refurbishing and once the reheating furnace starts from the next quarter, we'll be having a great impact of the in the productions and EBITDA margins going forward in second quarter onwards.

items.statement: Pledged shares to be released after debt refinancing and improved finances.
items.quote: So we feel that when we do the refinancing, all our pledged shares will be released by the banks.

items.statement: Management expects EPS to cross INR 7 in FY27, up from INR 4.36 in FY26.
items.quote: Last year we were 4.36, and I am pretty decent if all things go well, we should be crossing 7 this year.

items.statement: Management expects to add 120-150 corporates per year over the next two years, with potential upside.
items.quote: I think the next two years, we are again just looking to add about 120 to 150 corporates a year, hopefully on a growing trajectory quarter-on-quarter.

items.statement: Management expects to add 150-200 companies this year, depending on market environment.
items.quote: So, we're looking at an addition of anywhere between 150 to 200 companies depending on the market environment and the quantum and the size of the company we are getting.

items.statement: Management expects to grow revenue at same pace as FY25 to FY26, subject to market conditions.
items.quote: We'll just look to grow it at probably the same pace as from FY25 to FY26, subject to market conditions.

items.statement: Management expects decent growth in SME loan book this year, with many proposals in pipeline.
items.quote: I think, there should be good growth in this year. I cannot commit on the numbers right now, but there should be decent growth this year. A lot of proposals in the pipeline.

items.statement: Management expects cost of funds to reduce in near term post rating upgrade, with offers from financial institutions.
items.quote: Not yet, but we are receiving a lot of offers from financial institutions to take funds from them. I think you should hear from us shortly.

items.statement: Gold loan syndication disbursed about INR 375 crores in Q4 FY26 through banking and NBFC partners.
items.quote: we disbursed about INR375 crores during the last quarter through our banking and NBFC partners, including ICICI, HDFC, RBL and Muthoot Finance.

items.statement: Corporate rejection rate is almost 60% due to CIBIL or banking issues, reflecting volatile market conditions.
items.quote: Our corporate rejection rate is almost as high as 60% now. We tend to reject corporates either on the basis of CIBIL or on the basis of banking.

items.statement: Cross-sell disbursements (INR 12 crores) exceeded EWA disbursements (INR 10 crores) in Q4 FY26.
items.value: INR10 crores EWA, INR12 crores cross-sell
items.quote: I would say INR10 crores and INR12 crores. INR10 crores is EWA and INR12 crores cross-sell.

items.statement: Cross-sell primarily includes personal, home, and gold loans; expanding into mutual funds and insurance.
items.quote: So cross-sell primarily right now we are doing personal loan, home loan, gold loan, but we are looking to expand into various other categories as well, including small-ticket mutual funds and insurance.

items.statement: Gross NPA for FY26 was INR 66 lakhs; INR 38 lakhs recovered and INR 23 lakhs written off.
items.quote: So, we had a gross NPA last year, which is including EWA plus our business loan and personal loan of INR66 lakhs. We recovered INR38 lakhs from our NPA pool and remaining as of March 31, we had written off INR23 lakhs.

items.statement: No new customers added to NPA in Q4 FY26; previous university issue fully recovered with overdue interest.
items.quote: Have we added any, have we added any new customer to an NPA? No, we have not added any new customer to the NPA.

items.statement: CRISIL upgraded rating from BB+ to BBB-.
items.quote: I'm very pleased to share that CRISIL has upgraded our rating from BB+ to BBB-.

items.statement: Active EWA corporates about 185; total corporate clients 214 as of March 31, 2026.
items.quote: Active are about 180, 185.

items.statement: Expects GST, tech, and renovation costs to drop to 3.7% of revenue by FY28, expanding EBITDA margins.
items.quote: We expect all these 3 expense heads to reduce to approximately 3.7% of revenue by FY28 and onwards, leading to corresponding expansion in EBITDA margins.

items.statement: Plans to open about 2,000 rooms in FY27, similar to last year.
items.quote: Same click as last year, opened about 2,000 rooms.

items.statement: Expects to open 5,000 rooms annually in 2-3 years, based on current signings.
items.quote: we will be opening 5,000 rooms a year, because that is what we are signing now.

items.statement: Steady-state EBITDA flow-through of 75-80% and PAT margin of 60% for Lemon Tree.
items.quote: on a steady-state basis, hopefully, earlier rather than later, the growth of management fee income will translate to a flow-through of about 75%-80%, on a steady state basis.

items.statement: Plans to spend 1.9% of revenue on renovation in FY27, down from 5.8% in FY26.
items.quote: But renovation will come down to 1.9%.

items.statement: Nehru Place project requires Rs. 700 crore capex, with cash flow over 3.5 years.
items.quote: Nehru Place will, best guess, require Rs. 700 crore.

items.statement: Signed 55 managed and franchised hotels with 4,912 rooms in FY26.
items.quote: In FY26, on the asset-light side, we opened 20 managed and franchised hotels with 1,523 rooms and signed 55 managed and franchised hotels with 4,912 rooms.

items.statement: FY26 net EBITDA margin contracted to 48.1% from 49.4% in FY25.
items.quote: Our net EBITDA margins for FY26 was 48.1% compared to 49.4% in FY25, a contraction of about 126 bps.

items.statement: Adjusted pricing to maintain occupancy premium, keeping rates flat YoY amid demand slowdown.
items.quote: our strategy in April, where the slowdown continued from March going on into May was very clear that we would adjust pricing, so that our occupancy would continue at a premium to the market.

items.statement: Corporate travel slowed due to war and airfare hikes, but retail demand grew, supporting occupancy.
items.quote: Corporate travel is the first that kind of dries up when war happens because it is under the control normally of the CEO or an equivalent CXO and it is a one-person decision. What is encouraging, however is that the retail segment or what I would say, the non-corporate segment has continued growing and we have got more

items.statement: Aims for 65% retail business as portfolio grows to 20,000-25,000 rooms.
items.quote: We are very clear that as we grow to 20,000 - 25,000 rooms operating, we want 65% of our business to be retail, which is direct to us so it is really a C2B business, customers coming to us directly, sometimes through OTAs who are our partners in this endeavour and more and more directly through our website, our loyalty

items.statement: War and economic uncertainty could impact demand, but cost mitigation steps taken.
items.quote: if there is no conclusion, then we have taken the necessary steps to mitigate our cost structure appropriately and I think we will be fine.

items.statement: Warburg Pincus investment and internal accruals enable up to Rs. 3,000 crore deployment in 12-18 months.
items.quote: If I take Fleur and Warburg's investment into account, we have the potential to deploy up to Rs. 3,000 crore in the next 12 -18 months.

items.statement: Demerger expected to complete in 12-18 months, subject to NCLT approval.
items.quote: If that happens earlier, then it will be 12 months from now. If it happens later, then it will be 18 months. So, I am giving you an outer limit.

items.statement: Targets 35% CAGR disbursement growth and FY29 PAT of INR450-500 crores under 3-year strategic framework.
items.value: 35% CAGR; INR450 crores to INR500 crores
