items.quote: Disbursements, we want to target 35% CAGR growth in disbursements, aiming for a profit after tax target of INR450 crores to INR500 crores.

items.statement: Expects loan book to reach INR16,000-17,000 crores by FY29.
items.quote: You can put the number in excel, but I think you should be able to see something like INR16,000 crores to INR17,000 crores easily.

items.statement: Targets normalized credit cost of 2% to 2.5% as old book runs off.
items.quote: And as old book runs out, you would start seeing us stabilizing around 2% to 2.5% credit cost, which is what we're targeting as our yield is about 17% plus.

items.statement: Plans to add about 100 branches over next 3 years with 10-15% productivity gains.
items.quote: This trajectory will be structurally supported by the planned addition of about 100 branches over the next 3 years, expected portfolio level productivity gains of 10% to 15%.

items.statement: April and expected May 2026 disbursements tracking 40%+ year-on-year growth.
items.quote: This trajectory has carried into the current fiscal with April '26 and expected May '26 disbursements reflecting a robust 40% plus year-on-year growth in disbursements.

items.statement: Expects disbursements to continue improving sequentially with branch expansion and customer reach.
items.quote: Going forward, we expect disbursements to continue improving sequentially as we further expand our presence and deepen customer reach.

items.statement: Incremental cost of funds fell 60 bps YoY; overall cost of funds improved to 10.2%.
items.quote: As a result, the incremental cost of funds in Q4 FY26 declined by nearly 60 basis points compared to Q4 FY25, leading to a year-on-year reduction in the overall weighted average cost of borrowings as well.

items.statement: Net interest margin expanded to 8.7% in Q4 FY26 from 5.9% a year ago.
items.quote: This growth was driven by an improvement in net interest margin, which expanded from 5.9% in Q4 FY '25 to 8.7% in Q4 FY '26.

items.statement: Took additional INR326 crores provision on security receipts, raising coverage to about 63%.
items.quote: As a decisive step to derisk the balance sheet from potential future volatility arising from this portfolio, we have taken an additional provision of INR326 crores this quarter.

items.statement: Created INR49 crores management overlay on vehicle finance portfolio due to West Asia crisis.
items.quote: Further, owing to the West Asia crisis, we created a prudent management overlay of INR 49 crores against our vehicle finance portfolio.

items.statement: MHCV disbursement share cut from 57% in FY24 to 31% in FY26; PV raised to 23%.
items.quote: Second, our conscious diversification of portfolio has resulted in MHCV disbursements dropping from 57% in FY '24 to 31% in FY '26. Our passenger vehicle disbursement from 8% in FY '24 has now gone up to 23% in FY '26.

items.statement: Targeting sustainable revenue CAGR of 30% to 35% and PAT of INR945 crores by FY30
items.quote: We are targeting a sustainable revenue CAGR of 30% to 35%, projecting a PAT of INR945 crores by 2030.

items.statement: FY27 revenue guidance of INR8,100 crores; annualized Q4 exit run rate of INR7,650 crores close to guidance
items.quote: Our annualized Q4 exit run rate for revenue of INR7,650 crores is already close to our FY27 guidance of INR8,100 crores.

items.statement: FY30 sales target of INR18,000 crores to INR19,000 crores with nil net debt
items.quote: positioning the company for accelerated growth as we advance towards our FY30 target of achieving sales of INR18,000 crores to INR19,000 crores with a nil net debt position.

items.statement: Conservative PAT margin guidance of 5.25% by FY30, up 75 bps from current 4.5%
items.quote: We have guided for a conservative 5.25% PAT margin by FY2030, which represents an expansion of 75 basis points from current levels.

items.statement: No incremental capex needed until after March 2028; current 1.2 ton capacity at 55% utilization; exploring asset-light rental model
items.quote: Till 2028 March, we don't have any problem of the capacity. And again, we are planning for asset-light model. So, whenever we need, we can go for rental.

items.statement: Gross margin expanded to 8.45% in FY26 from 6% in FY24, driven by 100 bps from lower gold loss, 70 bps from advanced gold, rest from high-margin products
items.quote: From the current year-to-date, our consolidated gross margin stands at 8.45%, up 245 basis points from 6% in FY24.

items.statement: Expect gross margin to expand 60-90 bps from advanced gold and studded jewellery mix; interest cost reduction of 125 bps as debt goes to zero
items.quote: We expect our gross margin to expand by 60 to 90 basis points due to better mix of advanced gold and studded jewellery.

items.statement: Advanced gold model records only job work fees as revenue, improving absolute profit and margins despite top-line deflationary effect
items.quote: Under the advanced gold model, we only record the job work fees as revenue, whereas our traditional model records the entire jewellery value as revenue.

items.statement: No softening of B2B demand despite gold price volatility; stable demand at B2B level; gold exchange schemes at retail increased from 20% to 40%
items.quote: Till now we have not find any lowering of the order or softening of the demand at the B2B level because we are into lightweight jewellery segment.

items.statement: Advanced gold business grew to 11.5% of volumes in FY26 from 5.7% in FY25; exit run rate near 20%; targeting 30% by FY30
items.quote: The exit run date for the advanced gold is close to 20% and the overall average is close to 12%. And we are focusing on overall cash flows.

items.statement: Zero gold metal loan exposure currently; GML facility of INR170 crores sanctioned but unused; hedging 99% via MCX futures
items.quote: We are hedged approximately 99% or something, 0.5% or 0.75% we cannot control that, but you can say 99%.

items.statement: No need to raise external capital; net debt reduction of over 50% in FY27 via land sale and operational improvement
items.quote: We would be reducing net debt by 50% above in FY27 itself through land sale and operational improvement.

items.statement: Promoters moving to zero-salary, dividend-only compensation from FY27; dividends funded strictly from operating cash flows
items.quote: Beginning FY27, the promoters will transition to a zero-salary compensation model, migrating exclusively to a dividend only framework.

items.statement: Appointed M S K A & Associates LLP (BDO International) as statutory auditors; working capital days reduced from 71 to 59 days
items.quote: Our net working capital days have successfully dropped from 71 days for quarter ended March '25 to 59 days for this quarter ended March 26.

items.statement: Exports at 12% of revenue in FY26, targeting 20% by FY30; export model is outright (not advanced gold) with better receivable days
items.quote: We are expecting that this -- the export should be close to 20% of the overall sales is what we are expecting.

items.statement: Land monetization expected by August-September 2025; appointed 2-3 agencies for sale
items.quote: We are expecting it by August end. I think August or September last, we will encash it.

items.statement: Targets FY27 sales volume of 6.5 to 7 lakh tons.
items.quote: With regards to your second question regarding the volume guidance for FY27, we are targeting between 6.5 lakh tons to 7 lakh tons for this ongoing financial year.

items.statement: FY28 volume guidance around 8.5 lakh tons based on 1.4 million ton capacity and 62-65% utilization.
items.quote: As per our capacity if we do a 1.4 million ton capacity and if we take like safely 65% utilization or 62% because 70% is the peak. So, on that basis, I think around 8.5 lakh tons is a conservative number.

items.statement: EBITDA per ton guidance of INR3,500 to INR4,000 for FY27 and FY28 if markets stable.
items.quote: So, if the markets and all, if there is no volatility and if the markets are aligned, the demand and supply, so about INR3,500 to INR4,000 is a very comfortable number.

items.statement: Incremental capex for 1 million ton expansion: INR100 crores in CWIP, INR300 crores remaining, INR75-100 crores in FY27.
items.value: INR100 crores CWIP, INR300 crores remaining, INR75 crores to INR100 crores this year
items.quote: So, for this incremental capex of 1 million tons. So almost INR100 crores is already in CWIP and another INR300 crores will be needed to complete this 2 million ton target, out of which about INR75 crores to INR100 crores we are targeting for this financial year and the balance for the next 2.

items.statement: Plans to add 1 million tons capacity by FY29, reaching 2 million tons total.
items.quote: Under this expansion road map, an additional 1 million tons capacity is planned to be added by FY29, which will significantly strengthen the company's long-term growth potential.

items.statement: Value-added products share to reach almost 50% by end of FY27.
items.quote: So, by FY27, our share of value-added products will be almost 50% by end of this year because the capacity for DFT and this Hindupur facility are mainly into value-added segment.

items.statement: Preferential issue of INR90 crores to promoters for working capital and expansion.
items.quote: So, this preferential issue has been done by the promoters amounting to INR90 crores. And this is part of our planning from 1 million tons to 2 million tons and the requirement of working capital will be met through these proceeds.

items.statement: DFT facility at Sanand Unit 2 Phase 3 to be operational by Q3 FY27.
items.quote: In this respect, I'm pleased to inform that the DFT facility at Sanand Unit 2 Phase 3 is expected to be operationalized by Q3 FY27.

items.statement: APA pipes facility readiness expected by Q4 FY27 for oil and gas segment.
items.quote: Further, the APA pipes facility readiness is expected to be completed by Q4 FY27, which will strengthen the company's preparedness for entering into specialized pipe segments, particularly catering to oil and gas transportation applications and support future growth opportunities in value-added applications.

items.statement: Greenfield Hindupur facility for ERW pipes and solar tubes to be operational by Q4 FY27.
items.quote: The construction activities at the greenfield Hindupur, Andhra Pradesh facility are progressing at a fast pace and we expect the fully integrated manufacturing facility for ERW pipes, specialized solar tubes and other value-added seed products to become operational by Q4 FY27.

items.statement: Chennai facility on track, commissioning this financial year, full benefit in FY28.
items.quote: So, Chennai facility, it is on track. The construction activity is going on. We are hoping that this will also get commissioned in this financial year itself. And the full year benefit, we'll get this in FY28, for our Chennai facility.

items.statement: Capacity additions: 1.5 lakh tons Sanand, 2 lakh tons Hindupur, 1.5 lakh tons Sri City Chennai, 2 lakh tons UP plant.
items.value: 1.5 lakh tons, 2 lakh tons, 1.5 lakh tons, 2 lakh tons
items.quote: Yes, I can give you guidance for FY28. So, we are adding 1.5 lakh tons in Sanand, 2 lakh tons in our Hindupur facility, 1.5 lakh tons at Sri City Chennai and about 2 lakh tons in our UP. plant.

items.statement: External challenges: gas price volatility, availability issues, elevated ocean freight pressuring input costs and export realizations.
items.quote: Volatility in gas prices and intermittent availability issues, coupled with elevated ocean freight costs created temporary pressure on input costs and export realizations across the industry.

items.statement: Optimistic on long-term growth driven by infrastructure, construction, renewable energy, water transportation, and industrial demand.
items.quote: Looking ahead, we remain optimistic about the long-term growth prospects of the steel tubes and pipes industry driven by increasing infrastructure development, growth in construction activities, renewable energy investments, water transportation projects and rising industrial demand across sectors.

items.statement: FY27 revenue growth expected at least 20%.
items.quote: See, for FY27, we see it should be at least more than 20% growth.

items.statement: FY27 EBITDA margin to be higher than FY26; targeting 17% then 18% by FY28.
items.quote: And see, we have been saying that it will be more moving towards 17% and then to 18% by FY28 at EBITDA level.

items.statement: FY27 capex planned at INR90-100 crores.
items.quote: INR90 crores to INR100 crores.

items.statement: Spooling facility capex of INR70 crores, operational by December 2026.
items.quote: In line with this vision, we are now further forward integrating into spooling solutions with a capex of around INR70 crores.

items.statement: Current order book INR450 crores plus INR185 crores LOI from data center.
items.quote: our order book today stands at INR450 crores without LOI of INR185 crores that we have recently awarded by one of the leading data centers

items.statement: L1 in BHEL tenders worth over INR50 crores, expected in 30-45 days.
items.quote: almost more than INR50 crores order we're L1. So that order we will be receiving next 30 days to 45 days’ time.

items.statement: Export revenue share to continue at 30-35% going forward.
items.quote: So, we believe going forward also more than 30%-35% range should continue on the side of export.

items.statement: Spooling business to have higher margins than current business.
items.quote: And see, it would be higher margin-driven business, higher than what we currently earn in our business.

items.statement: Prolonged elevated raw material prices may impact future performance.
items.quote: However, a prolonged period of elevated RM prices may have some impact going forward.

items.statement: Domestic demand robust from power, oil and gas, engineering, chemicals, CNG.
items.quote: from the domestic side we are seeing demand in CNG, power, oil and gas, engineering, chemicals.

items.statement: Seamless capacity utilization 90-95%, welded 60-65% for FY26.
items.quote: seamless was to an extent utilized more than 90%-95% and welded something around 60%-65%.

items.statement: Pricing increased 5-7% in FY26 due to grade mix.
items.quote: Slightly increased, it was slightly increased, 5% to 7%. But again, because of grade mix and all that has also happened.

items.statement: Volume growth guidance of 20% for FY27.
items.quote: 20% guidance, we believe we should achieve on the volume front also.

items.statement: Spooling business expected to generate asset turn of 3x investment.
items.quote: we see a turn of around 3x of investment is expected from this business.

items.statement: Expects 35-40% revenue CAGR over next 3-5 years.
items.quote: I think we are looking at a 35%, 40% kind of a CAGR going forward in the next three to five years that we have been seeing and we continue to stand with that.

items.statement: FY27 EBITDA margin expected between 9% and 10%.
items.quote: I think we will try and keep it closer to double digits. So, between 9% and 10% is what we expect.

items.statement: PAT margin expected to improve 50-100 bps over next two years.
items.quote: I think a 50 to 100 basis points improvement is expected over the next two years.

items.statement: Compressor expansion capex of INR150 crores over next year, already tied up.
items.quote: So, compressor is INR150-odd crores kind of an investment that is going to happen over the next 1 year. That is phase 1 of the expansion. That is already tied up.

items.statement: EMS capex of INR25 crores, tied up.
items.quote: I think there is a INR25-odd crores kind of investment that is happening. That is tied up.

items.statement: AC expansion requires INR40-50 crores investment, likely debt funded.
items.quote: the AC would require about INR40 crores to INR50 crores of investment.

items.statement: Refrigeration expansion in two phases, each INR20-25 crores.
items.quote: I think the first phase would require about INR20 crores, INR25 crores. The second phase again will require a similar kind of number.

items.statement: Compressor capacity to increase from 2.8 million to 6 million by March.
items.quote: the next phase of expansion from 2.8 million to 6 million should happen let us say by March.

items.statement: Compressor margins expected 6-7% this year, potentially double digits in 2 years.
items.quote: the margins are going to stay between 6% and 7% this year. And with the complete -- hopefully the complete stoppage of import from China, this can move closer to double digits in the next 2 years.

items.statement: 10-15% price pass-through achieved across industry due to raw material volatility.
items.quote: between 10% and 15% as a ballpark figure has been passed on overall from manufacturers to brands and from brands to the end consumer.

items.statement: RAC volume growth expected 30-40% in FY27.
items.quote: growth is going to be around 30%-odd, 30% to 40% growth.

items.statement: AC revenue share to reduce to 50-60% as diversification increases.
items.quote: I think AC should remain around 50%.

items.statement: Government allows 40% compressor imports, benefiting local manufacturers like us.
items.quote: the announcement from the government where they have given so-called relaxation for the import of compressors, the reciprocating compressors in the segment that we are in, I think 40% is what they have given us, which is a very good signal for us.

items.statement: INR150 crores debt to be raised in subsidiary for compressor expansion.
items.quote: INR150 crores, of course, is there that is going to come in the subsidiary. And that is the exact amount that is going to be needed in the subsidiary for the first phase of the expansion from 2.8 million to 3 million.

items.statement: FY27 overall top-line growth expected at 18-20%.
items.quote: As I look at FY’27, our growth outlook is positive with an expected 18% to 20% overall top-line growth.

items.statement: EBITDA margin to improve by 0.5-0.75% annually over next 2-3 years.
items.quote: EBITDA margin, on an average, every year we will keep on improving. There will be an improvement in the range of 0.5 to 0.75, in the coming next two three years.

items.statement: Technical plant EBITDA margin to reach 8-10% in 2-3 years.
items.quote: At the optimum level, we can make 8% to 10% EBITDA.

items.statement: Branded formulation expected to grow 20-25% with normal monsoon.
items.quote: So, if there is a regular monsoon this year, then our growth will be managed by 20% to 25% on an average of the brand.

items.statement: Raw material price increases passed on to finished goods with 1-2% lag.
items.quote: It is 1% to 2% where you cannot pass-on. Rest, the cost increases.

items.statement: Technical plant capacity utilization to reach around 75% next year.
items.quote: Going forward, this time, our capacity utilization was 70%. It was 65% to 70%. And next year, it will be around 75%.

items.statement: Technical plant GP margin improved to 22% in FY26 from 19%.
items.quote: So, last year, we have a GP margin of 19%. In current year, we have a GP margin of 22%.

items.statement: Employee expenses to grow 5-8% next year.
items.quote: That will grow around 5%. It will grow between 5% to 8%. Around 5%.

items.statement: FY27 is a year of consolidation; profitable growth expected, no rapid expansion.
items.quote: So, this is the year of consolidation. We will grow this year with one or the other things that are already there.

items.statement: Demand resilient despite price hikes; some hesitancy in commercial vehicles in last 8-10 days.
items.quote: So, we are also positively surprised by the resilience of the demand so far, except for commercial vehicles where we have seen some kind of hesitancy in the last 8-10 days, and some supply challenges in one or the other OEs.

items.statement: After-sales margins around 20% may not be sustainable; focus on 10-year track record.
items.quote: I believe that what we have done on a consistent basis is what one should look at and not overtly look at this margin continuing.

items.statement: No OEM discussions on renegotiating dealer margins; price hikes increase per-unit profit.
items.quote: So far, we have had no discussion with any OEM about renegotiating our margins as such. So, if the prices go up, we tend to make more money per unit.

items.statement: Higher inventory held to benefit from price hikes; one-time gain on existing stock.
items.quote: So, it is a one-time gain for the stock that we are holding, not otherwise. It is a one-time gain. For only the inventory that we would be holding.

items.statement: BYD supplies resumed April onwards; Pune sales and service outlets operational in July.
items.quote: Our Pune Sales and Service outlets will be operational in July which will further increase our market share for BYD in the country.

items.statement: New Mahindra after-sales facility in Hyderabad to start operations in July.
items.quote: Mahindra & Mahindra continues its strong momentum. The sales and service outlets have stabilized and due to the strong after-sales momentum that we are seeing, we are opening a new after-sales facility in Hyderabad which is likely to start operations in July.

items.statement: AI-based calling implemented in call centres; will expand to more use cases.
items.quote: We have started with utilizing AI-based calling in our call centres and will expand to more use cases over time.

items.statement: Targets 40-45% CAGR over next three years with sustainable high-margin growth.
items.quote: We are structurally positioning ourselves to target 40 to 45% CAGR over the next three years while delivering sustainable high-margin growth.

items.statement: Plans to scale capacity utilization to 3,500-4,000 metric tons per annum this financial year.
items.quote: We plan to scale our capacity utilization to 3,500 to 4,000 metric ton per annum by this financial year.

items.statement: Targets EBITDA margin of 12-15%.
items.quote: But still we are trying to increas e our EBITDA margin from we try to maintain it between to 12 to 15%.

items.statement: Expects PAT margin around 5-7% due to B2C spending and global situation.
items.quote: So around roughly PAT will be will be somewhere around 5 to 7% that's what we may reach we will be there.

items.statement: Targets B2C/D2C to reach 10% of revenue in FY27.

items.quote: We further accelerated our value capture efforts and we selected ensuring that we are able to pass on the cost increases to our customers.

items.statement: Energy costs represent 6-7% of revenue for acquired group post-increase
items.quote: So Rajesh ji, this is in the range of 6% to 7%.

items.statement: Commodity production moved to Indian Roha site; Frankfurt site focused on speciality
items.quote: We've already moved some of the commodity products to the Indian Heubach site in Roha and Frankfurt family remains towards speciality coverage.

items.statement: Middle East crisis causing raw material price increases, supply constraints, higher energy and logistics costs
items.quote: The Gulf war situation has definitely impacted our cost base and several raw materials used by one Sudarshan are petroleum-derived and we are facing both price increase and supply constraints.

items.statement: Net debt reduced to INR 755 crores in March 2026 from INR 934 crores in December 2025
items.quote: More importantly, what has happened is that the net debt, which was at INR934 crores in December '25 has reduced to INR755 crores on March '26.

items.statement: Inventory reduced by EUR 29 million in Q4; targeting further EUR 15-20 million reduction
items.quote: We've reduced EUR29 million of inventory in Q4and during this year, we are targeting to reduce EUR15 million to EUR20 million more gradually.

items.statement: RIECO revenue grew 17.5% to INR 268 crores in FY26; EBITDA turned positive to INR 10 crores from negative INR 17 crores
items.quote: For financial year '26, RIECO had reported the revenue from operation of INR268 crores compared to INR228 crores last year, the growth of 17.5% and this increased due to the execution of high-value projects during this year. On the EBITDA we are actually in the rebound and recovery from the negative INR17 crores EBITDA to positive INR10 crores.

items.statement: Management expects ~18% volume growth for FY27 across the full product portfolio, driven primarily by frozen foods and Tetra Recart.
items.quote: Considering the present situation and market scenario or information, whatever update we are getting from customers, we are expecting around 18% volume growth for this financial year.

items.statement: Frozen foods volume grew ~28% in FY26 and is expected to continue strong momentum into FY27 with U.S. and Middle East demand.
items.quote: Frozen foods continued its strong momentum, delivering volume growth of approximately 28% during FY26, supported by increasing demand for value-added products and growing interest from the U.S. market.

items.statement: Spray drying capacity expansion of 120 MTPA at INR 2.5 crores; commercial run targeted for December 2025.
items.quote: Commercial run targeted December. And we are trying to see if we can prepone by 2025 base as the target you are asking. But December month, definitely commercial production likely to start.

items.statement: Pectin plant commercially operational; targeting 50% capacity utilization in FY27 yielding INR 7-8 crores revenue at ~70% gross margin.
items.quote: So INR7 - 8 crores of revenue is what we can actually expect at 50% utilization and the gross margins are approximately around 70%-odd of that.

items.statement: Frozen foods segment carries ~50% gross margin but higher cold-chain costs (10x ambient) reduce EBITDA contribution.
items.quote: The frozen food segment actually has around 50% gross margins.

items.statement: Management does not guide EBITDA margin percentages due to cost-plus pass-through model; focuses on per-ton margin improvement.
items.quote: We are expecting on volume growth 17%. But EBITDA, we won't be able to tell you or we generally don't disclose because our model is cost-plus model where we pass through that.

items.statement: Middle East demand disrupted in Q4 FY26 by geopolitical conflict; expected to normalize over time with pent-up post-COVID demand.
items.quote: We expect demand from Middle East to normalize over time.

items.statement: Internal target: non-mango businesses to contribute 40% of revenue in 4-5 years without degrowing mango business.
items.quote: So, the internal strategy over a period of time is to actually make the other businesses contribute 40% of the total revenue without degrowing the mango business.

items.statement: El Niño impact uncertain; raw material availability not a concern but price volatility is the key risk.
items.quote: Challenge is the price. When there is a mismatch in the demand supply, the price moves, I mean, either direction in a very bad way.

items.statement: PLI scheme: INR 83 crores received to date out of INR 145 crores total; INR 60 crores remaining over next 2 years.
items.quote: We've received around INR83-odd crores. The total that we can actually get under the scheme is around INR145 crores. So INR60-odd crores are remaining.

items.statement: Long-term debt ~INR 71-72 crores; annual repayment ~INR 20 crores from internal accruals; no asset sales planned.
items.quote: Our annual commitment is around INR20 crores. So, we'll be comfortable to pay from our internal accrual, not an issue.

items.statement: Targets annual export revenues of up to Rs 1,000 crore by FY27-28.
items.quote: This is underpinned by a medium-term roadmap to FY27-28 where we are targeting annual export revenues of up to Rs 1,000 crore, supported by deeper penetration in Russia and China and re-entry into the European Union and a measured build-out of our domestic and value-added portfolio.

items.statement: Value-added products were 7-10% of export volume; aims to double that share.
items.quote: As far as our export portfolio is considered, value-added products made up roughly 7-10% of overall volume for the year gone by. And if all export factors remain fairly normal in terms of markets and geopolitics, we are hopeful of doubling that contribution in terms of percentage by volume.

items.statement: Anticipates US exports to scale up significantly in FY27 due to tariff reduction.
items.quote: So, all factors considered, we anticipate that our U.S. exports this year will scale up significantly compared to the last couple of years.

items.statement: New PD Curl control product adds 5-10% incremental EBITDA margin over base.
items.quote: So, in this specific scenario we have seen incremental EBITDA margins in excess of 5% up to almost 10% over and above our base EBITDA.

items.statement: Setting up 1 MW solar plant for captive consumption; part commissioned in Q4, balance soon.
items.quote: The company is in the midst of setting up a one-megawatt solar power plant for captive consumption in its processing division. Part of the project has already been commissioned in Q4 and the balance will be commissioned shortly.

items.statement: Passing some raw material costs to contract farming partners; aims to improve export realizations.
items.quote: So, some amount of the costs are being passed on to our channel farming partners but we intend to pass on better realizations to them by ensuring that at the exports level, we generate better contracts with improved margins.

items.statement: Raw material price volatility and erratic weather are key short-term risks.
items.quote: So, in the short term, I think raw material pricing being volatile across the spectrum is a risk for the sector. And weather also being erratic, I think there are certain reports that there could be intense weather during the rest of the calendar year this year.

items.statement: Optimistic on EU demand in FY27 due to India-EU FTA; expects increased exports.
items.quote: We do remain optimistic with respect to European demand being accessible during the course of the current fiscal. The EU-FTA trade has for the most part resulted in a positive sentiment.

items.statement: Penetrated China with black tiger shrimp, added five customers; plans deeper penetration.
items.quote: We also penetrated a new market in the form of China for a new product range altogether, which is black tiger shrimp. In that context, we have worked with five customers so far in the year gone by and intend to penetrate the market deeper during the current fiscal.

items.statement: Commenced sales to Hyperpure in Q4 FY26 for domestic market with raw frozen shrimp.
items.quote: In this context, we are happy to share that the company has commenced sales to Hyperpure in Q4 of FY2025-26 with the initial plan for the domestic market involving selling of base products such as raw frozen shrimp.

items.statement: Market share in Indian shrimp exports is 0.5-0.75%; feed vertical sub 2%.
items.quote: Our market share as far as Indian exports is concerned is currently about 0.5%. Indian exports for shrimp is typically in the region of around 50,000 to 55,000 crores. And we are ranging between 0.5% to 0.75% currently.

items.statement: No new clients added in US in FY26 due to tariff turbulence; optimistic for FY27.
items.quote: With respect to our other export markets, such as the U.S., we did not add any new clientele during the year because there was a lot of turbulence on behalf of the tariffs and certain other factors.

items.statement: FY27 revenue expected to cross INR3,000 crores
items.quote: if you look at, I guess, on an overall basis, we are expecting to cross INR3,000 crores.

items.statement: FY27 EBITDA margin expected to exceed 10.25% (adjusted FY26 level)
items.quote: we expect that we should see an improvement in the overall margin levels as well going beyond 10.25% that we have achieved last year, if we exclude the onetime impact.

items.statement: Exports to grow 32% in FY27, primarily to Germany and USA
items.quote: the exports will grow by 32% this year, and primarily to Germany and to U.S.A.

items.statement: Railway revenue target INR100 crores in FY27; defense target INR50 crores
items.quote: we should be crossing INR100 crores as far as the railways are concerned. And that's what our internal target is, and we should be able to achieve that. Defense is a little slow, and we are targeting -- we are trying to see how do we cross INR50 crores this year.

items.statement: Hosur facility expected operational from September 2026 for hybrid/EV programs; Tamil Nadu subsidy INR39 crores over 10 years
items.quote: The facility is expected to become operational from September 2026 onwards and will primarily cater to hybrid and EV-related programs for key OEM customers. items.quote: passenger vehicles expected to grow by around 5% to 7%, 2-wheelers by around 6% to 8%, and commercial vehicles by around 4% to 6%, and 3-wheelers by around 9% to 10%. EV penetration in the 2-wheeler segment is also expected to improve further to around 7% to 8%

items.statement: 40 new program launches ramping in FY27, including hybrid/EV components; single-source supplier for many

items.quote: Unless, of course, the global -- the geopolitics which is happening and that brings about some disaster, I think we are ready to reach the levels that we are talking of now.

items.quote: we seem to be pretty much on target to be between the INR250 crores and INR300 crores number for

items.quote: overall, I se e if current end of petroleum prices remain, overall material costs should rise by almost around 10% to 12

items.quote: I think probably I think in the fourth quarter of the current financia l year, they should be able to ready to commission the plant

items.statement: Margin improvement driven by product mix shift toward domestic, ROW, cardiac and generic businesses
items.quote: The improvement in overall margins is by and large because of product mix changes. Domestic business is doing good. ROW market busine ss is doing good. Cardiac business proportions has moved

items.quote: Overall, I think our freight cost has moved up by almost, I think, in the fourth quarter by almost around 25%. And that trend is continuing currently also.

items.statement: Unichem inventory elevated due to shift from air to sea shipments; no concern per management
items.quote: Significant amount of air shipment was there in Unichem maybe a year back to almost around 40% kind of shipment was moving by air. Now it's hardly around 4%, 5% kind of shipments ar e moving it

items.quote: Our expectation is, Rahul, that we should do about INR3,400 crores to INR3,500 crores of revenue. Our PAT expectation is between INR700 crores to INR750 crores.

items.quote: In terms of like R&D expenditure next year, I think we expect to spend about 7% to 9%. And in terms of earnings, we have already budgeted that.

items.statement: Brazil subsidiary revenue expected to grow from ~INR280 crores to INR55-60 million (USD) in FY27
items.quote: We are expecting that business should go to INR55 million to INR60 million this year. So that is one big bump you're seeing in our numbers.

items.statement: Margins will contract in FY27 with PAT dropping by half from INR1,400 crores to INR700-750 crores

items.quote: we have already seen 25% to 30% increase in the input raw materials. And see, I think even industry, fortunately, most of the procurement for the kharif, at least half of the procurement has already been done.

items.quote: We are thinking that we should be able to do about INR75 crores to INR100 crores annualized over the year. We'll be able to achieve it.

items.quote: We don't have anything in '27. That's true. But I think post '27, you'll see some of these other exclusivities will start kicking in.

items.quote: As of now, I don't have an update, but hopefully, we'll be able to achieve something in this financial year as well.

items.statement: Aluminum premium (MJP) increased, freight costs at all-time high, LME-SHFE price difference for aluminum widened to $330-$360 per ton, fiber optic costs up 3x-4x year-on-year.
items.quote: There is a fairly large difference between LME and the Shanghai Metal Exchange, what we call the SHFE prices which, for aluminum, has increased to about $330 to $360 a ton.

items.statement: Cable division capex working towards INR10,000 crores revenue target; spent INR400 crores in FY26, carrying forward INR850 crores into FY27, pulling forward spending by ~INR400 crores.
items.quote: Capex is working towards getting to that INR10,000 crores. We have already spent about INR400 crores in FY26. And if you look at all the carry-forward projects which we have into FY27, that's about INR850 crores.

items.statement: CTC conductor exports starting with Middle East approvals; working on Europe and U.S. approvals; expect higher export percentage in FY27 and FY28.
items.quote: Initially, we have got approvals from Middle East manufacturers and has started exporting to them. We are now working towards getting approvals in Europe and the United States as well.

items.statement: U.S. cable business expected to grow significantly in FY27 over FY26 and further in FY28 as approvals widen and initial orders increase from broader customer base.
items.quote: We feel that our business will go up in FY27. It will further go up in FY28 because we are spending a lot of time in getting approvals there and started getting from a much wider range of customers initial orders.

items.statement: Cable division EBITDA margin at 10.2% for FY26; competition from UltraTech and Adani focused on building wires and light-duty cables, not high-value specialty cables; overall market pie growing.
items.quote: I don't think either the current plan or the immediate launch that UltraTech is going to do -- the Aditya Birla Group is going to do is going to affect these high-value products.

items.statement: Plans to increase royalty rate 10-15% annually alongside ~10% volume growth.
items.quote: Yes. Going forward, we are also planning to increase 10% to 15% every year along with a volume growth of around 10%, which we are achieving from last 2, 3 years.

items.statement: Own manufacturing plant to continue 100% capacity utilization in near future.
items.quote: This year, we have utilized 100%, and it will continue to have 100% utilization in the near future also.

items.statement: Royalty charged per ton, so steel price fluctuation does not impact business.
items.quote: We are charging royalty on per ton basis, not on the percentage basis. So the price fluctuation is not impacting our business at all, either in own manufacturing or in the branding business.

items.statement: Royalty rate rose to INR435/ton in FY26 from INR398 last year.
items.quote: Yes. This year, the average rate is INR435 per metric ton which was INR398 last year.

items.statement: Royalty income expected to contribute increasingly larger share of overall earnings.
items.quote: This royalty led revenue model is in our view, the defining financial characteristic of Kamdhenu's business, and we expect it to contribute an increasingly larger proportion of our overall earnings over the coming years.

items.statement: Expects steel demand trajectory to sustain and potentially accelerate over medium term.
items.quote: We expect this demand trajectory to sustain and potentially accelerate over the medium term, driven by a confluence of structural factors.

items.statement: Geopolitical disruptions in crude oil and gas may pressure near-term margins.
items.quote: While these factors may exert near -term pressure on margins, both for us and for our franchisee partners, the resilience of the underlying demand environment provides confidence in the ability to manage through this period.

items.statement: Framing treasury policy to reward shareholders; no further investment planned in paint business.
items.quote: The treasury will be utilized only for the steel business and reward to the shareholders.

items.statement: Plans to increase market share in South; rest of India focus on existing unit capacity.
items.quote: Yes. In the South, we are planning to add more franchisees. And the rest of India, we are planning to increase the capacity of existing units.

items.statement: Brand premium across India around INR2,600 per ton, up to INR6,000 in some states.
items.quote: Today, in all over India, our premium is around INR2,600 per ton. In some states, our goods are sold for INR6,000 per ton extra, which is the best local brand there.

items.statement: Franchisee capacity around 5 million tons; new data to be released in Q1.
items.quote: And hopefully, in the Q1, we will release this data, the existing capacity is around 5 million.

items.statement: Regional volume mix: North 31%, East 35%, West 19%, South 15%.
items.quote: in North, we have 31%, East, we have 35%, West we have 19%, and South, we have 15% on the overall volume.

items.statement: Estimated retail branded TMT market share around 20%.
items.quote: Ma'am, exact data is not available for the TMT product, but on the estimated basis, we are calculating retail branded market share is 20% of Kamdhenu brand product, retail branded.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 EBITDA margin expanded to 15.6% from 8.58% in Q3 FY26 and 11.53% in Q4 FY25, driven by price pass-through and operational efficiencies.
items.quote: The EBITDA margin as well expanded to 15.6% in Q4 FY26 compared to 8.58% in Q3 FY26 and 11.53% in Q4 FY25, once again representing an expansion of 407 basis points year-on-year and 702 basis points sequentially.

items.statement: Management targets AZO EBITDA margin of ~13% and API EBITDA margin of 15-16% at steady state, significantly above current levels.
items.quote: For both answering on EBITDAs for both the ATC as well as Atlas business, we would guide that Management would like to target EBITDA margin of about 13% of the AZO business. And eventually, if we get the API business right, 15% to 16% in the API business going forward.

items.statement: AZO capacity expansion of ~1.5x planned at Rs. 10-15 crore capex once utilization hits 75-85%, to be funded via internal accruals.
items.quote: As soon as we hit that range, we would like to do a little expansion with a small CAPEX of about Rs. 10 crores to Rs. 15 crores which would probably be financed through internal accruals and increase our capacity.

items.statement: US demand for Blue and AZO pigments reviving after tariff reductions; Europe remains structurally slow but opportunities pursued.
items.quote: We have seen a revival in that. So, our US business, once the tariff has been reduced again, it has again started to improve.

items.statement: Blue pigment margin improvement driven by raw material price pass-through, inventory gains, and operational efficiencies; management aims to sustain higher gross margins.
items.quote: It is a mixture of several factors of internal strategy, a little bit of the inventory addition as well as your operational efficiencies all put together that have driven the strong numbers.

items.statement: Company aims to reach Rs. 1,000 crore revenue within next few years; debt reduction ahead of schedule with strong cash flows across all four units.
items.quote: We will certainly be looking to grow, and we certainly have the goal of reaching Rs. 1000 crore as a company within the next few years.

items.statement: Gokul Jaykrishna stepped down as CEO after 8 years, remains Managing Director; Arjun Jaykrishna appointed CEO to drive next growth phase.
items.quote: As of the last Board meeting, I stepped down as the CEO of Asahi Songwon Colors Limited, and it's been an amazing journey of eight years as a CEO and 17 years as Managing Director.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 EBITDA margins expected to be maintained at Q4 FY26 levels across all three segments
items.quote: on the EBITDA, all three segments should be able to maintain quite easily even under the current circumstances of disruption globally, the margins that we have seen in Q4. So, Q1 should be able to easily maintain those in terms of our performance.

items.statement: No capacity expansion CAPEX planned for Blue business
items.quote: Management view on the capacity and volume growth of the Blue business is clear that we are not looking to do on the Blue business any CAPEXs to increase capacity. This is clear.

items.statement: Chinese API/pigment prices up 30-40% due to export incentive removal, freight doubling, crude rise
items.quote: Chinese has increased around 30% to 40% of their price because of all three reasons.

items.statement: Blue demand environment remains depressed, one of longest low periods since inception
items.quote: probably one of the longest low or depression sustained periods in terms of demand in the chemical industry in general also in Pigments that has been seen since our company started probably.

items.statement: Capex guidance for FY27 and FY28.
items.quote: Yes, so Yes, the capex for FY27 most likely would be in the range from INR40 crores to INR50 crores and for FY28 another would be in between INR35 crores to INR40 crores.

items.statement: Plans to open 4 additional Jean Dousset stores in FY27, reaching 6 locations.

items.statement: Each existing Jean Dousset store generates INR30-35 crores annual sales and INR8-10 crores bottom line.
items.quote: Each existing Jean Dousset store generates between INR30 crores and INR35 crores in annual sales depending on the location, demonstrating the strong scalability and revenue potential of the brand's retail model.

items.statement: D2C business EBITDA margins are 15% to 20%.
items.quote: We've outlined the plan to grow our direct-to-consumer business to about INR1,000 crores. And as I've mentioned that the EBITDA margins on that are 15% to 20%.

items.quote: The website is called Enchanted Disney Fine Jewelry and because of this focus, we've been seeing a 30% to 40% organic growth in this channel.

items.statement: No dividend for current year; will consider once zero net debt is achieved.
items.quote: Yeah, for the current year, we've decided not to distribute a dividend because I think the current priority is investing in the growth of the business.

items.statement: Net debt currently around INR200-250 crores; total debt INR450 crores with INR200 crores cash/investments.
items.quote: So as of right now, we have around INR200 crores to INR250 crores of net debt. Our expectation would be that over the next 2 years or so, we should be at a zero net debt position.

items.statement: Currency exposure largely hedged via USD purchases and forward contracts.
items.quote: So at any given point of time, we are more or less completely hedged as far as exposure to currency markets is concerned.

items.statement: May consider share buyback once zero net debt achieved, subject to Board approval.
items.quote: And obviously, based on capital allocation and when we get to zero net debt, the company may buy back shares of the company as well. But these are not decisions that I can take without the Board's consent.

items.statement: Order book stands at INR4,675 crore entering FY27
items.quote: We enter FY27 with an order book of INR4,675 crore, providing healthy revenue visibility and reaffirming customer confidence in our capabilities and execution.

items.statement: Targets INR10,000 crore revenue by 2030 with minimum 15% EBITDA margins
items.quote: And as I mentioned, long term, by 2030, we expect the company to be at about INR10,000 crore of revenue with at least minimum 15% EBITDA margins.

items.quote: Looking ahead, we aspire to build a INR1,000 crore revenue business in batteries and energy storage over the next 3 to 4 years, supported by a growing order pipeline and favourable industry dynamics.

items.statement: Commissioned cell-to-battery manufacturing line in Indore for vertical integration
items.quote: To strengthen vertical integration and manufacturing efficiency, we commissioned a cell to battery manufacturing line in Indore, enhancing our ability to scale as demand grows.

items.statement: Added 110 MW of BESS business to FY27 order book via MoAs with Chalukya Power and Pickrenew Energy
items.quote: We are also pleased to sign MoAs with Chalukya Power and Pickrenew Energy, resulting in 110 megawatts of BESS business being added to our FY27 order book.

items.quote: So we are already in the process, right now, a vehicle is under design, and it will go for certification also shortly. So we expect to launch 1 or 2 variants this year.

items.quote: Our effort is and intention and expectation is for the next five years, given the current scale we are in, for the next five years, we hope that we will maintain the same kind of momentum.
